“If people didn’t appreciate Cody before, personally I don’t understand it,” Van Dijk said. “But I think it was a no-brainer for us as a team and a club to keep him. There were talks but, in my eyes, you can’t let him go and that’s why I said it. He is a friend as well. Ours, please – let’s keep it that way.”

Sports.title: Argentina star Mauro Icardi hit with 73-YEAR driving ban after video posted online by his girlfriend alerted authorities to his expired driving licence
Sports.content:
Argentina star Mauro Icardi hit with 73-YEAR driving ban after video posted online by his girlfriend alerted authorities to his expired driving licence

Argentinian striker Mauro Icardi has been handed a remarkable 73-year driving ban for driving without a licence.

The former PSG and Inter Milan goal machine found himself in hot water after a video posted by Icardi's new girlfriend China Suarez caught the attention of the Argentine Ministry of Transport.

The video posted showed her hanging out of the window of a car driven by Icardi, just outside of Buenos Aires. The Ministry for Transport then launched an investigation which revealed the striker's driving licence had expired.

The Ministry have since published a statement on X saying: 'We found that Icardi's driving license had expired. For this reason, we have ordered his provisional disqualification... the player will need to be assessed to determine his fitness to drive. Road safety allows for no exception.'

The Ministry confirmed Icardi has been handed a driving ban until the end of the century.

The two-time Serie A golden boot winner issued a raunchy statement in response to the his suspension, writing: 'Think about fixing the roads to improve traffic flow instead of wasting time writing tweets and scratching your balls.'

Icardi has been a free agent since leaving Galatasaray and had links to Spurs in the summer but now has a new issue on his hands

The striker began dating China Saurez (left) shortly after his divorce from famous WAG Wanda Nara last year

The striker is now locked in a battle against the ministry challenging the suspension with the hope of having it lifted.

As part of his punishment Icardi also has also had his Italian driving licence cancelled despite it being valid until 2029.

The striker again took to social media to voice his displeasure, writing: 'I want to know how you have managed cancel my Italian driving licence.'

The striker is no stranger to controversy off the pitch having been embroiled in one of the most famous footballing scandals.

In 2013, after first joining Inter Milan, fellow Argentinian Maxi Lopez welcomed the then 19-year-old to Italy by frequently inviting him to his house to meet his family and enjoy time off together and over time Icardi privately grew close to Lopez's then wife Wanda Nara.

Lopez and Nara eventually separated in late 2013 and shockingly a year later Nara tied the knot with Icardi.

Both Nara and Icardi repeatedly denied their relationship had begun before her divorce from Lopez.

Yet the perceived betrayal had led to the striker being kept out of the Argentine national team for most of his early career due to the scrutiny he received.

Nara and Icardi endured an acrimonious separation early last year and begun dating his new girlfriend China Suarez but remains in litigation with Nara over the pair's divorce settlement.

Sports.title: Rodri issues defiant response to Man City being found guilty of vast majority of Premier League rule break charges as former star insists he 'believes' in the club despite verdict
Sports.content:
Rodri issues defiant response to Man City being found guilty of vast majority of Premier League rule break charges as former star insists he 'believes' in the club despite verdict

Former Manchester City captain Rodri insists he 'believes in the club' and their success cannot be taken away after they were found guilty of the vast majority of their Premier League rule break charges.

Rodri, whose seven-year spell at Man City ended in the summer when he moved to Barcelona, became the first individual associated with the club to speak following the bombshell news on Friday.

Daily Mail Sport understands Man City were found guilty of all but one of their 115 charges by an independent panel.

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties and even relegation.

Points deductions could even be applied onto previous seasons, raising the chance that City will be stripped of their Premier League titles.

When asked about the verdict ahead of Spain's Nations League match against England on Saturday, Rodri reiterated his belief Man City will be found innocent.

Rodri has insisted Man City's success cannot be taken away from them despite the club being found guilty of the majority their Premier League rule break charges

The former Man City captain insisted he believes in the innocence of the club amid the verdict

The midfielder referenced a previous 2020 decision which saw Man City banned from the Champions League and fined by UEFA for a breach of financial rules, which was later lifted on appeal by the Court of Arbitration for Sport which also reduced the club's fine to £9million.

'We have faced something similar in 2020 if I remember correctly, a similar process, a different accusation but similar process.

‘In the first instance we were found guilty but we believed in the club and the innocence the club maintained, and in the end we ended up being acquitted.

‘I believe in the justice system and I believe in the innocence of the club.’

When asked whether he had been given assurances by the club of their innocence, Rodri added: 'They always tell us the confidence of their innocence and when you look in someone’s eyes and they are talking in that way – and we have the example of 2020 the process was the same and at the end nothing happened – we were very calm in this way.

'We were never a team that was nervous about these kind of things. I am not going to say it is normal but some teams go through these situations and it is part of football today.

'Everyone has to follow the rules and for me that’s great. They always expressed the confidence they never did anything wrong and we believe in that, and that’s the thing.

'We will believe the club. I have been there and I know how they work and how they cooperate.'

Rodri insisted Man City's success was 'deserved' and the result of hard work from the players and staff

Rodri won four Premier League titles, the Champions League, two FA Cups, three Carabao Cups and a FIFA Club World Cup during a glittering spell at Man City under Pep Guardiola.

When asked whether he it hurt that Man City's achievements have been questioned, Rodri insisted the success of the players and staff during that period cannot be taken away.

'For us, the players, it is a different thing. For you guys there are all kinds of opinions but we always tried to think in a positive way,' Rodri said.

'When you live daily in that club and all the people that worked hard all these years to have all the success we have had, not only Pep [Guardiola] and the players, but from the owners to the guys that work daily, what we did they cannot take it out of us.

'It is not something that is paid by money, it is paid with effort and partnership, being shoulder to shoulder every day.

'We had a lot of success over the years and I can tell you that everything was deserved and I am glad I could live one of the best eras in English football.'

Man City are set to appeal the verdict.

A Manchester City spokesperson said: 'The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023.

'The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

The club have maintained that they are innocent throughout the process and are expected to appeal

Man City, who have always strongly denied wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024.

Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges.

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

A three-man panel was tasked with considering the evidence, with the initial expectation a verdict would have been reached on the case within months. It has since taken three-and-a-half years.

The original 115 charges were extended to a total of 130 after an administration issue in what is the most expensive and wide-ranging case in English football history.

City remained steadfast in maintaining their innocence over more than 115 alleged breaches across eight years, some including the start of the Pep Guardiola era.

The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Sports.title: Devastating untold story of Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen's marriage: Read every ugly detail, the secret letter stashed in a drawer... and her savage last three words that left him so ruined, friends feared he had cancer
Sports.content:
Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen's divorce in 2022 shocked America. The greatest quarterback in history and the woman who was once the world's highest-paid model were a fairytale match made real.

Now, after years of extensive research speaking to friends, eyewitnesses and teammates, bestselling author Lars Anderson's new book Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness reveals how it all went so terribly wrong.

Tom Brady longed to stay connected to his old life, to keep feeling that high-voltage climax of competition he'd been chasing since he was a teenager.

But he was also tormented by the mounting feeling that it was almost immoral to keep playing because the job essentially rendered him an absent father and husband for half the year.

His brain dictated one course of action. His gut chartered another – a problem similar to trying to walk in opposite directions at once.

'It's not always what I want,' he said in January 2022. 'It's what we want as a family. And I'm gonna spend a lot of time with them and figure out in the future what's next.'

In particular, Brady felt that his Victoria's Secret model wife Gisele Bundchen 'deserved' more of his time as a husband and a father.

Brady's unrelenting desire to continue playing football had placed enormous strain on the marriage. At first, she tried to gently nudge him into retirement.

In 2017, minutes after Brady had just masterminded the greatest comeback in NFL history to win his sixth Super Bowl, Gisele and their two children ran onto the field to celebrate.

But the first words Gisele said to her husband of eight years had nothing to do with the game and everything to do with the future: Would now be the perfect time to retire?

Brady didn't know what to say. He hugged his wife and acted as if he hadn't heard the question.

A new book by Lars Anderson has revealed the untold story of Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen's shock divorce that shocked America

When Brady first met Gisele, whose net worth was close to $400 million and had graced more magazine covers than anybody on earth, he said he was only planning to play in the NFL for 10 more years

As his wife's career faded into the background and her yearning for him to be at home with their family grew, Brady built a dynasty with Bill Belichick and the New England Patriots

Later that night in Houston, as the team celebrated, Gisele pressed her husband a second time. Brady was unresponsive.

After a third attempt, he finally answered. 'Too bad, babe,' he said. 'I'm having too much fun right now.'

Weeks later, the couple and their children went on vacation with Jay Feely, a former teammate of Brady's with the Michigan Wolverines.

Gisele asked Feely to do what she could not: persuade her husband. Gisele pressured Feely to frame retirement as Brady's final and most important act of leadership – one for his family.

'She was dead serious, too,' Feely later said.

'Play as long as you want,' he told Brady.

Brady winked at his buddy.

Gisele went for a more direct approach in 2018, days after Brady and the New England Patriots had suffered a gut-wrenching Super Bowl loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

Gisele wrote her husband a letter – serious, handwritten. She explained that their marriage wasn't working. She needed more of him, more of his time, more of his attention, more of his heart.

She needed him to be present when he was at home, not responding to text messages on his constantly buzzing cell phone or replaying a game in his mind.

She needed more help with the kids. She needed the chance to sleep in just a few days a week. She needed more time for her own career.

Gisele ran onto the field to celebrate with Brady after he had just completed the greatest comeback in NFL history, only to immediately question him on a potential retirement

Brady and Gisele have son Benjamin (left) and daughter Vivian (right). But she also helped raise Jack (center), the son Brady shares with actress Bridget Moynahan: pictured in 2021

'People need to understand that Gisele was a bigger international star than Tom,' said a former Brady teammate. 'She was getting tired of living on Tom's schedule and being somewhat in his shadow during football season. She has a lot of pride, too. And, I mean, how many times did you see Tom supporting her career? There clearly were imbalances there.'

The couple went to marriage counselling, but Brady eventually filed the heartfelt letter in a drawer.

He'd pull it out on contemplative nights and reread every word, wanting to be reminded that he needed to tend to his marriage with the same tenacity he tended to his job.

In early 2020, the family relocated from to Florida when Brady signed for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

'Think about being married to Tom,' said one of Brady's friends, a former NFL player. 'The guy gets up at the crack of dawn, thinks all day about a game that is foreign to his wife, comes home and is in bed each night by nine. He can't really eat out or go out without causing a scene. Everything he puts in his mouth tastes like s***. The whole lifestyle had to be getting tiresome for Gisele.'

BRADY: AN AMERICAN STORY AND THE PRICE OF GREATNESS Lars Anderson's new Brady biography is released on Tuesday September 29 and is available to purchase HERE

Worried that enrolling their young children at a new school would be 'too much change,' Gisele committed to homeschooling Benny and Vivian in Tampa. 'We were only going to stay for a year,' she said.

One year turned to two.

And so it was that, in January 2022, America's most famous quarterback found himself weighing the case of Brady vs. Brady – the sportsman vs. the family man.

He deliberated for nine days. It was close to a hung jury; Brady leaned 55 percent one way, 45 percent the other.

But on February 1, he announced the verdict: At the age of 44 and after 22 years in professional football, his NFL career was over.

That decision lasted just 40 days.

On March 13, Brady announced he would return for a 23rd season, his sights set on an eighth Super Bowl win.

'I've realized my place is still on the field and not in the stands. That time will come. But it's not now,' he said.

At first, Gisele made the right noises, expressing public support for her husband's decision to play on.

'I don't think relationships just happen. It's never the fairytale people want to believe it is,' she said that summer.

'When you love someone, you don't put them in a jail and say, "You have to live this life." You set them free to be who they are.'

But when Brady walked into One Buc Place in July for the start of training camp, the sight of him – gaunt and cadaverous – was that of a man worn thin, reduced to bone and sorrow.

Brady and Gisele looked smitten on vacation in 2022, just weeks before he announced his un-retirement

Gisele paid an emotional tribute to Brady after he announced his retirement for the first time. She also initially supported his decision to return publicly but things quickly turned sour

Nearly everyone in the building worried he was ill, maybe even battling a serious disease. His teammates estimated he'd lost close to 20 pounds, and the vibrancy of his spirit had dimmed like a candle running low on wax.

'For Tom to lose that much weight, on his frame, it was a lot,' said his former Buccaneers head coach Bruce Arians. 'It was very clear that the reason for the weight loss was the stress from the personal issues he was dealing with.'

'His cheekbones had freaking cheekbones,' said another coach. 'With all respect, he looked like a cancer patient with really good hair. He just seemed miserable, not even close to the Tom we all loved. He was so stressed.'

In truth, Gisele had been so upset at Brady's U-turn that she had flown off to Costa Rica.

Brady wound up taking Benny and Vivian, then 12 and 9, to their first day of class at a new private school in Florida.

During practice on July 28, center Ryan Jensen, one of Brady's closest friends and his biggest defender on the field, collided with another player.

Crashing to the ground, Jensen screamed 'F***!' and clutched his left knee. Practice stopped. Brady lifted off his helmet and ran to Jensen.

Kneeling by his side and knowing the meaning of that scream – torn ligaments, fractured bones – he watched as the medical staff tended to his friend. Getting visibly upset, Brady stood and walked away.

He wandered around the eerily quiet field, hands on his hips. 'It was pretty clear he was asking himself, "Why the f*** did I come back?"' said one Buccaneers staffer.

'I think that's when he realized he'd made a horrible decision. He didn't come back and risk adding more troubles to his marriage to get the s*** kicked out of him!'

In late August, for the first time in his career, Brady asked his head coach if he could take an extended leave from camp.

He said he'd come back; he just didn't know when.

Things had got so bad that he and Gisele now required a serious discussion in a remote location.

There was a noticeable change in Brady when he walked into One Buc Place in the summer of 2022 for training camp

Brady had lost so much weight that his Buccaneers coaches and teammates thought he looked like a cancer patient

'I've got to take care of some personal things,' Brady told coach Clyde Christensen with a lifeless stare.

Christensen later speculated that Brady may have been experiencing a form of serious psychological shock.

Something had blindsided him – something very bad and something that had completely devitalized him.

Brady's absence from camp was excused, but only a few at One Buc Place knew he was traveling to a private resort in the Bahamas to make one final, desperate attempt to keep his family together.

With just six months left in his football career, the bond he and Gisele had was flickering out like a match in a strong gust of wind, the fragile illusion of forever now fast fading.

'Tom didn't know what the heck was going on,' said an assistant coach. 'And we didn't know if he was ever coming back.'

When he returned to Tampa after 11 days away, his spirit seemed more broken than before.

It was evident that a scarring incident had transpired.

The frantic, nearly two-week effort to rescue his marriage had failed. Those close to Brady feared the countdown to divorce was on.

But Brady remained utterly captivated by Gisele, still lost in the enchantment of her.

'Tom was an empty shell of who he was when he got back,' Christensen said. 'There was no joy. Everything was hard work.'

'Everything was going good between Tom and Gisele,' one eyewitness close to Brady said. 'Tom was FaceTiming with Gisele during the day between meetings, just checking in to see if she needed anything. These were normal conversations, and she seemed happy.

'Then one day, Gisele, who is really into astrology, basically looked into the stars and told Tom, "We're not compatible." And just like that, she was done.

'But what triggered that? Was it the years of feeling like she wasn't his top priority? That he kept playing when she'd asked him to step away? Maybe.

'Or was there a particular spiritual adviser telling her, "Hey, this relationship is bad for you. Get out of it now. Even the stars are telling you that." One thing is certain: In no way, shape or form was this a normal marital breakdown.'

Brady and Gisele announced their divorce on October 28, 2022, after 13 years of marriage.

In February 2025, Gisele gave birth to her third child, her first with boyfriend Joaquim Valente, her former jiu-jitsu instructor.

According to one of Brady's friends, he was absolutely 'stung' that she had become pregnant just two years after divorce.

In February 2025, Gisele gave birth to her third child, her first with boyfriend Joaquim Valente, her former jiu-jitsu instructor

According to one of Brady's friends, he was absolutely 'stung' that she had become pregnant just two years after divorce

Just over a month after the birth, Brady shared a photo of himself on Instagram – his preferred form of mass (and often cryptic) communication.

In the color photograph, Brady's right arm is extended and a ball has spiraled out of his hand. He is silhouetted by the sunset's golden glow.

Underneath, Brady wrote: 'True Love.'

To those who knew him well, there was no ambiguity. As one friend described it, that was 'the softest middle finger.'

PART TWO COMING NEXT WEEK: The shocking sex incident that left Brady's college teammates questioning everything...

Adapted from Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness by Lars Anderson. Copyright © and reprinted by permission of Celadon Books.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand calls for Man City to be STRIPPED of title after bombshell guilty verdict - as teams who could be handed 'stolen' trophies are revealed
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand calls for Man City to be STRIPPED of title after bombshell guilty verdict - as teams who could be handed 'stolen' trophies are revealed

Former Manchester United defender Rio Ferdinand has suggested he will be picking up another Premier League title after Manchester City were sensationally found guilty of financial rule breaks in the division.

A guilty verdict was delivered on all but one of their 115 rule-break charges concerning the Premier League’s financial regulations.

The competition accused the club of widespread financial cheating over an era of sustained success – with an independent panel hearing concluding in 2024.

City are set to appeal the decision but any punishment is now expected to follow, with some fans calling for the club to be stripped of the trophies they won at the time.

That includes the league title the club won in the 2011-12 season, which was claimed ahead of United when Sergio Aguero famously netted in the last minute of the final day against QPR.

It meant City won the league ahead of local rivals United on goal difference, with Ferdinand in the United team that lost out that day.

Rio Ferdinand has suggested he is in for another Premier League medal after Manchester City were found guilty on 114 of 115 financial charges

The former defender was referring to the dramatic title won by City when Sergio Arguero scored late against QPR

And the former defender has taken to social media, essentially demanding that City are stripped of the title they won that year.

'Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet,' the 47-year-old wrote on social media.

He would leave United at the end of the 2013-14 season, in which City won the Premier League again – though Liverpool finished second.

In the bombshell event that City are stripped of their titles won during their period of financial breaches, United would have two championships reinstated - 2011-12 and 2017-18, while Liverpool would receive the trophy for 2013-14.

Simon Jordan, meanwhile, wrote on X: '115 charges … well well … fun and games ahead this is seismic!'

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation.

Points deductions could even be applied onto previous seasons, raising the chance that City will be stripped of their Premier League titles. Beneficiaries, in that case, would be the likes of United and Liverpool - who would be awarded three more Premier League titles each.

A Manchester City spokesperson said: 'The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023.

'The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

FOLLOW LIVE: All the reaction and latest news as Man City are found guilty on 114 of 115 charges

Sports.title: Forget the appeal, the mud attached to Manchester City's name will now stick forever. To the rest of football, they are CHEATS, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
A little more than three years ago, Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak touched upon the reputational damage caused to his football club by their fight with the Premier League.

'It's very frustrating because it takes so much from the great work that's happening at this club,' Mubarak told the club website. 'What these players have achieved is incredible.'

Khaldoon was speaking in the wake of City's Treble win in 2023. Six months earlier, the club had been landed with the 115 charges that will from this day forward form such an ugly part of their identity.

And that is a key component of what this has been about for City and indeed what it will be about for a long time yet as they attempt to move on from today's devastating news.

It's always been about reputation. It has always been about what a traditionally working class club formed 146 years ago in the Manchester suburb of West Gorton is now seen to stand for.

So deep, drawn out and ugly has City's confrontation been first with UEFA and then more recently the Premier League that it will sit like an asterisk next to their name for years to come.

It is understood the Premier League have triumphed on the vast majority of charges against Manchester City

Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak (left) spoke on the reputational damage - which could stick with City for years to come - after their Treble win

The football world can now start to judge City's on-pitch achievements in its own way

If Khaldoon thought or presumed that the frustrations he talked about in June 2023 would evaporate once the Premier League's judgement was passed then he has been firmly disabused of that notion today.

For all that we can expect City to appeal this verdict – for all the money and expensive legal power they have ploughed into this dreadful, ugly fight – the mud attached to City's good name will stick.

And this is a long, long way from what they once were and some way from what they thought they may one day be when Sheikh Mansour of Abu Dhabi rescued the club from the verge of financial oblivion at the back end of the 2008 summer transfer window.

This is not what that dream of success on the field was supposed to be about.

Perhaps it's ironic that back on that frantic day – September 1, 2008 – the new City attempted to throw money around as though there were absolutely no restrictions. And there weren't back then. UEFA's Financial Fair Play rules were still a year away from conception.

So City bought the Brazilian Robinho for £32million from Real Madrid, tried to hijack Manchester United's signing of Dimitar Berbatov from Spurs – just because they could – and talked openly of signing Cristiano Ronaldo from their neighbours at OId Trafford.

Some of it was a bit crass but it must also have felt like great fun for a football club that had for so long been patronised and slighted by their local rivals and pretty much regarded as a vague curiosity by just about everybody else.

The club is a long way from when Sheikh Mansour of Abu Dhabi rescued the club from the verge of financial oblivion

They spent money freely - trying to hijack Dimitar Berbatov's move to Manchester United

City were playing in their big new stadium by then – leased from the council after the 2002 Commonwealth Games – but much else about them still screamed 'small'.

When City signed Vincent Kompany from Hamburg just nine days before the takeover, for example, manager Mark Hughes was so embarrassed by the press and media facilities at the club's Carrington training ground that the club persuaded Sale RUFC to let them use theirs for the Belgian's unveiling on their site over the hedge next door.

It was never any surprise, then, that City wished to move fast. This was their moment to seize and their opportunity to grasp. Abu Dhabi were not here to play, as the saying goes.

But it was when European football and, after that, our own Premier League decided to impose a new and utterly without precedent spending model on its member clubs that City's new owners ran into the murky waters that now threaten to wash so many of their achievements away.

Had Abu Dhabi known that such a shift in football's financial landscape was about to take place, would they have bought the club in the first place? It's at the very least a question worth thinking about.

City denied wrongdoing from the start.

'The attempt to damage the club's reputation is organised and clear,' was a retort repeated so often it may as well sit beneath the crest on their sky blue shirt.

Nevertheless, the rest of football made up its mind a long time ago and will now feel vindicated. To their mind – and in the eyes of the Premier League – City have been cheating.

Eight Premier League titles, three FA Cups, six League Cups and one Champions League have all been won by the club in the modern era

City's own supporters tend broadly to be split into three camps.

A tiny minority section who no longer attend games, disillusioned by City's change from the club they presumed represented their values to one they now think does not. Another group who believe totally in their club's innocence and, perhaps more significantly, another large number who feel the rules are merely unfit, a tool deliberately imposed by clubs like United and Liverpool to try and keep the upwardly mobile down where they want them.

That debate about the spending restrictions remains live and is one had on repeat at football clubs up and down the Premier League. It is not just City.

Nevertheless the 'Red Cartel' narrative is deeply-engrained within the Etihad Stadium. Their emergence as England's most powerful football team came at a time when City were not represented in the analysts' chairs at places like Sky, BT (as it was) and the BBC. The sports pages of newspaper websites continue to drip with red and even the now-departed City coach Pep Guardiola has referred publicly to that.

It all plays to the deeply-held notion in and around City that the Premier League – and before them Europe – would have liked it had City merely stayed in their lane, one once inhabited so entertainingly by vaguely calamitous figures of yore such as Peter Swales, Francis Lee and Thaksin Shinawatra.

City have already burst through that red tinted glass ceiling, of course. Eight Premier League titles, four FA Cups, seven League Cups and one Champions League have all been won in the modern era.

But now that we have our verdict – now that a line can begin to be drawn – football can at least start the process of judging City and all those on-pitch achievements in its own way. From that point of view this is a line in the sand moment.

City supporters are split into three camps, having made their minds up a long time ago

This will be a long haul back to acceptance and sound standing for City. Guardiola will doubtless be glad he is well out of it.

The internet meme of Brian Clough – played so brilliantly by Michael Sheen in the Damned United film – telling his Leeds players to put their medals in the bin because you have 'won them all by bloody cheating' will get a fair airing over the coming days.

The Premier League's verdict is more resounding than many of us thought likely. We presumed more shades of grey.

And while we await sanction, the plain truth of it all for City is that many people in football had made up their minds on this one an awfully long time ago.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola was convinced Man City were innocent and used that sense of injustice to motivate his stars. Now he will have some awkward questions to ask his bosses with doubts being raised over his era of dominance, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola was convinced Man City were innocent and used that sense of injustice to motivate his stars. Now he will have some awkward questions to ask his bosses with doubts being raised over his era of dominance, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Pep Guardiola always counted the Community Shield as a trophy and for that there was only one reason. It’s legacy. His legacy in English football. His legacy at Manchester City.

There will be mounting questions and debate about what that means and looks like now, in the wake of the extraordinary verdict handed down by an independent commission.

For a large majority, City’s defeat in their case with the Premier League means more than just an asterisk next to any achievement over a nine-year period from 2009. It will mean that the trophies simply are not recognised, whether City are ultimately stripped of them or not.

And it doesn’t stop there. While the charges cover up to 2018, the wider argument is that Guardiola’s dominance was built on cheating. Cheating he will not have been privy to but a financial leg-up of attracting better players under Roberto Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini that in turn accelerated the football club and allowed the Catalan to prosper.

Without the early trophies, the 2012 title, it’s arguable whether even Txiki Begiristain could have convinced Guardiola to join.

So the whole lot will be lumped in. The six Guardiola league titles, the Champions League, three FA Cups, five Carabaos, a Club World Cup, a Super Cup and yes, those three Community Shields.

Pep Guardiola won the lot with Manchester City - but his achievements will now forever be tarnished

Guardiola has always publicly insisted City's innocence, based on conversations with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak

That is irrespective of the appeal that City will launch and its end result. City and Guardiola’s success has always been muddy in the court of public opinion and Friday’s news only solidifies that further.

Whatever happens from here, there is no coming back from the entrenched viewpoints, no grey area. The success will be forever tarnished for those who always believed in their guilt.

Guardiola’s next move will be fascinating, in what he says and where he’s spotted. There is a stand named after him at the Etihad Stadium, a statue on its way. He is a City Football Group ambassador and one who has always publicly insisted their innocence.

Insisted it based on conversations with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano – the latter's family are understood to have moved back to Spain earlier this year.

These are people he likes, people he trusts. People who convinced him to stay in Manchester far longer than initially planned. In an ironic twist, the charges actually helped in that regard, elongating their partnership.

The battles with the Premier League and before that, UEFA, had Guardiola subscribing to the world according to City and produced moments that spoke to that – like in February 2023, when the charges dropped, quoting Julius Caesar to underline what he felt was a betrayal by other top-flight clubs and claiming that the club had already been condemned.

He fumed at the assumption of guilt, he name-checked Daniel Levy, he sarcastically said they’d bring Paul Dickov and Mike Summerbee out of retirement when relegated.

‘It’s the same as with UEFA,’ Guardiola said. ‘The same articles, the same accusations. You need to go to League One. No, no, League One is too much. League Two. Or maybe the Conference. We were in Maine Road, we are not with a history of lots of titles. We’ve been in those divisions, we will be back there.’

Listening to Guardiola in those moments was like listening to any executive at City. And he’s not one to toe the party line if he doesn’t believe in it – as evidenced amid fan protests against ticket prices in recent years.

While the developments had no bearing on his players, he used this sense of perceived injustice to motivate himself to reel in Arsenal to win that title, to do the Treble.

He fumed at the assumption of guilt, he name-checked Daniel Levy, he sarcastically said they’d bring Paul Dickov and Mike Summerbee out of retirement when relegated

‘I’m not moving from this seat,’ he said – almost chillingly – that afternoon. ‘I… can… assure… you. More than ever I want to stay.’

Eventually he did, claiming a lack of energy and the realisation that City needed fresh ideas.

In fairness to him, he had remained in situ waiting for an outcome for more than long enough. He will believe that nothing happening away from the pitch should impact the glory constructed by his players, by Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva and Vincent Kompany and Erling Haaland but equally he knows that it must.

Guardiola initially insisted that he would walk if it transpired that City’s hierarchy had lied to him but behind the scenes he had quickly become convinced that they would have little to answer in front of legal experts. What the brushes did was bind Guardiola and City even tighter.

It formed a militance within Guardiola, who had been incandescent on the day of their 2019 FA Cup final victory at a question effectively alleging that he had received off-the-book payments from his employers.

This is a guy who once privately told his players that Europe’s referees were all against them in the Champions League to provoke a response, so the idea he used the boardroom pitchforks as motivation to slowly raise a big middle finger is only logical.

City certainly do not rewrite history in lifting four consecutive league titles without Guardiola. They likely do not complete the Treble without Guardiola. He would not have stayed to see out a decade, either.

City certainly do not rewrite history in lifting four consecutive league titles without Guardiola. They likely do not complete the Treble without Guardiola

No manager who coaches footballers to play in the way City did for so many years ought to be at the centre of such murk. And yet, here they are

But he will have questions of those he has formed bonds with within the hierarchy, whose own reputations will be sullied by this affair. Even as recently as last week, those right at the top, led by Al Mubarak and Soriano, were projecting an air of calm.

‘Once we have a ruling, believe me, we're going to have a wonderful sit down together and I'll say everything I've wanted to say for the last three years,’ Al Mubarak said in an interview at the end of last season. Not exactly the words of a man worried for the immediate future.

There will be awkward conversations going on about the last 10 years. It’s leaving supporters in a state of flux and should have the most decorated manager in their history feeling conflicted too.

No manager who coaches footballers to play in the way City did for so many years ought to be at the centre of such murk. And yet, here they are.

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Strip Man City of ALL eight of their Premier League titles and relegate them for their defrauding of Man United and Liverpool's history. English football is broken irretrievably and will never be the same again
Sports.content:
Nothing will ever be quite the same again in English football. On the last Friday in September 2026, something broke irretrievably in our game. Something was ruined. Something was lost. Please don't laugh too bitterly at this, but this was the day when the last of our innocence slunk away into the corner and stood against the wall, its head bowed.

When the news emerged that Manchester City had been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations, it plunged the game into a pit of fire and a world of recriminations and repercussions that may redraw much of the recent history of the top flight.

This is our Calciopoli Scandal that rocked Italian football in 2006 and relegated the mighty Juventus to Serie B, this is our equivalent of the bribery and match fixing scandal that defrocked Marseille in 1993, this is our Black Sox Scandal that surrounded the fixing of the 1919 World Series. It is a bleak, bleak day for the English game.

Say it Ain't So, Pep. Say that none of this is true. Because, one of the greatest sadnesses of all in these guilty verdicts is that they tarnish the achievements in this country of Pep Guardiola, one of the greatest coaches that has ever lived. They tarnish everything that City have achieved since they were taken over by Abu Dhabi. They have brought the whole edifice crumbling down.

But it is not the greatest sadness. The greatest sadness is in the cost to fans of so many other rival clubs who were cheated of what they should have won. City's dishonesty robbed them of moments that would have lasted a lifetime. It robbed them of celebrations with friends that they would never have forgotten. It robbed them of days out that would have been forever bathed in sunshine.

Sir Alex Ferguson would have won 14 league titles, not 13, if City had not evaded the rules. Steven Gerrard's domestic career with Liverpool would not have been defined by that slip against Chelsea in 2013-14 because Liverpool would have won the title. Manchester United would not still be wandering in a post-Ferguson wasteland because they would have won the title in 2017-18 under Jose Mourinho.

Pep Guardiola and Man City club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak celebrate their 2024 title

Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool were among those beaten by City in the wake of their dishonesty

And Liverpool, not City, would have won one of the greatest title races of all time in 2018-19. And Jurgen Klopp and not Guardiola would have emerged victorious in that battle and history may have come to regard him as the greatest manager of the era that followed Ferguson instead.

Klopp's Liverpool came second to City in both the 18-19 and 21-22 title races by a solitary point. When he was asked after his departure in 2024 about the possibility of City being stripped of those titles, Klopp said: 'If you organise a bus parade, I am in. How long it takes I don't care.' That day may be coming sooner than he thought.

So the heartbreak lies in what others have lost as much as in the iniquity of what City gained. It lies in the defrauding of history and the way we were manipulated. City were a magnificent team to watch under Guardiola. Perhaps the best our league has ever seen. But that doesn't count for much anymore. Our eyes might as well have been scratched out. Our memories mean nothing now.

Some will say it is a great victory for the Premier League and, yes, it has established its authority over its member clubs and, yes, the alternative to winning this legal battle was unthinkable for it.

But the 'triumph' should make it question its direction of travel. This is a win for the Premier League in one way but in another, it is a catastrophic loss. City, and Guardiola, were its standard-bearers. They were its best team. They set new standards for beauty and quality. Now, it turns out, that was all built on sand. It may be that the league has won a battle but lost a wider war. City are part of the Premier League, too. The league is eating its own.

Everything that City have won since the Abu Dhabi takeover is discredited. Everything feels sullied. All the titles and trophies that were won between 2009 and 2018 are most at risk. The 'Aguerooo' moment from 2012 when City won their first top flight title for 44 years with a last-gasp winner from Sergio Aguero at the Etihad? That is tainted. That is spoiled. That is undermined.

The 'Aguerooo' moment from 2012 when City won their first top flight title is tainted

Jose Mourinho and Manchester United missed out on titles at the hands of Man City

Martin Tyler's greatest moment of commentary has been muted. The greatest moment in Premier League history? Not any more, it isn't. It may, in fact, come to be seen as a symbol of one of the most cursed eras in our national sport.

The guilty verdicts mean that City were playing by different rules to everybody else. And whatever you think of the rules, others respected them and so City should have done. The verdicts say they ignored the rules, that they manipulated the funds available to them unfairly. The verdicts say they had an unfair advantage. The verdicts say they cheated.

And so everything they achieved in those years is invalidated. And because those years provided the foundation upon which everything else was built, then everything that followed in the unparalleled success of the Pep Guardiola years is besmirched, too. No one is saying Guardiola knew what had passed before, of course, but he was an unwitting beneficiary of it.

And so what do we say now of the four top flight titles in a row that Guardiola's side won between 2020-21 and 2023-24? No other had done that in the long history of English football. That should have been Guardiola's greatest legacy but it turns out it was built on the shifting sands of the dishonesty of those that came before him. In a way, he too has been betrayed.

What now? Asterisks are not enough. The very least that should happen is that City be stripped of the titles they won in 2012, 2014, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024. That scenario is said to be 'unlikely'. It should not be. The very least that should happen is that they be relegated from the Premier League and made to start next season in the Championship.

They will appeal, of course, and so that will protect their participation in the Premier League for the rest of this season and perhaps beyond. But if that appeal is unsuccessful, they should be cast out of the top flight. The entire credibility of English football is at stake here. If they escape with a lesser punishment, credibility will be lost.

The unparalleled success of the Pep Guardiola years at Man City is besmirched, too

The guilty verdicts should also make English football pause and take a long, hard look at itself. The Premier League can celebrate its victory but it has become a place where owners have declared war on clubs' long-standing fans in their desire to maximise revenue and destroy tradition.

It should make the league look again at its willingness to allow nation-states to own its football clubs, as is currently the case with City and Newcastle United. The power that they wield and the fabulous riches they command and the arrogance that seeps from them led directly to the entire 115 charges farrago.

This may be just the beginning for City, too. It is a bleak day for them but it may get worse. The verdict could be a gateway for City's rivals each to claim more than £100million in compensation. I spoke to one high-ranking official at a rival Premier League club recently and he predicted an avalanche of law-suits against City if they were found guilty of the most serious charges.

Anyone who missed out on a Champions League spot because City occupied one of the places, for instance, would be keen to seek redress, he said. A team that finished eighth, say, would want their prize money adjusted to the total it would have been if they had finished seventh. City may be entering a world of pain.

Guardiola was a human shield for the club while he was there because all recognised his talent and the beauty of the teams he produced. Now, when the storm breaks, Guardiola is gone and City are even more defenceless. Some, too, will seek to settle old scores.

Away from the pitch, City have ruled with a mixture of intimidation, obfuscation, charm and public relations expertise. They have sought to bully some sports journalists for reporting the truth. It is not a modus operandi peculiar to them but they have pursued it with vigour and relish.

The verdict could be a gateway for City's rivals each to claim more than £100million in compensation. Liverpool missed out on the title to City in 2014 when Steven Gerrard slipped

Their public relations tactics have been extremely effective. I have spoken to several high-ranking executives at other Premier League clubs who have been bitterly amused by the idea, which City have managed to promulgate, that they are disadvantaged outsiders fighting against a football establishment.

City, we were told, had been targeted by a supposed 'Red Cartel' of Manchester United, Arsenal and Liverpool, so that they could be kept with their noses pressed against the glass. We were told that Financial Fair Play and, later, Squad Cost Ratio rules baked in the superiority of United, Arsenal and Liverpool.

Well, if City are victims, they have been prosperous victims indeed. They have won eight league titles since 2011-12 and one Champions League. They are the fifth most valuable football club in the world. Their majority owner, Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan is the UAE Vice President and Deputy Prime Minister. Outsiders? All these years? Please. Pull the other one.

Outsiders now? It is hard to see how it could be otherwise, for some time at least. City will be regarded as pariahs in the Premier League and beyond. They were, we thought, the best of our game. But now we know that was just an illusion.

Sports.title: The clubs who could seek compensation as Premier League sides consider legal action after Man City found guilty of vast majority of rule breaches - and what happens next: Key questions answered
Sports.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their rule-break charges concerning the Premier League’s financial regulations.

The competition accused the club of widespread financial cheating over an era of sustained success – with an independent panel hearing concluding in 2024.

The long-awaited verdict has now been reached with the belief it is a victory for the Premier League, despite Man City having strenuously denied the charges.

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation.

Daily Mail Sport's Mike Keegan provides answers to the key questions, including the next steps, Man City's expected appeal and how serious the punishment could be.

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their 115 Premier League rule-break charges

WHAT DOES IT MEAN?

This cannot be viewed as anything other than an overwhelming victory for the Premier League.

To see Manchester City found guilty of the ‘vast majority’ of the 115 charges is an outcome that Richard Masters will no doubt see as vindication for what has been a costly, long-running legal battle in which the stakes were incredibly high.

It is safe to assume that had the tables turned the other way, the chief executive would have been in P45 territory.

More important than that, those who City feel were the key protagonists, the so-called ‘Red Cartel’, will also feel vindication.

To put it simply, Manchester City have been found guilty of cheating their way to success between 2009 and 2018, a period when they dominated English football.

The verdict cannot be viewed as anything other than an overwhelming victory for the Premier League and its chief executive Richard Masters

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?

There has been no statement from the Premier League, while City’s only says that the process remains ongoing and is subject to strict confidentiality.

What is clear is that City will appeal. What is not clear is whether the sanction will drop before any appeal.

WHAT ARE THE PUNISHMENTS?

Take your pick. Hefty points deductions, potential relegation and transfer bans are all on the table. Rule W51 in the Premier League handbook states ambiguously that ‘such other penalty as it shall think fit’ is an option.

There is, however, a scepticism among some, based on a lack of noise from many of the other clubs and the lenient punishment recently handed to Chelsea that whatever penalty lands will not see City stripped of titles or relegated. ‘They’ll get a slap on the wrist and ordered to pay legal costs and not much else,’ one exec predicted.

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation

HOW DOES AN APPEAL WORK?

In all likelihood City will appeal and recent cases tell us that they tend to be dealt with expeditiously.

An appeal board would be set up, appointed by the chair of the panel and, again, featuring three people. Some feel that this would be an exercise in the Premier League marking its own homework.

At this early stage, it is worth an assumption that City could argue the panel was not impartial. The bad news for them, however, is that this is a high bar to clear.

Unlike City’s case with UEFA, it cannot go to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (who overturned UEFA’s findings).

WHAT ABOUT COMPENSATION?

Last year, in a move believed to have been instigated by former Arsenal chief executive Tim Lewis, the Gunners, Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool and Manchester United served legal notices reserving their right to take action.

Should the verdict stand, they will then seek damages for a wide variety of issues. The most costly claims are likely to come from those who say they missed out on Champions League qualification during the period in question thanks to City’s law breaking. But the scope would not end there.

Clubs could also, for example, argue that as a result of the breaches they were unable to sign a calibre of player that would have allowed them to be more successful on the field. Some believe £200m would not be out of the question, but that remains to be seen.

Ex-Arsenal chief executive is understood to have instigated a move last year that saw the Gunners, Tottenham, Liverpool and Man United served legal notices reserving their right to take action

WHAT ABOUT THE INDEPENDENT FOOTBALL REGULATOR?

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the Regulator declined to comment when contacted by Daily Mail Sport. However, David Kogan will be well aware of the situation.

The IFR was brought in for a variety of reasons, not least to ensure that those owning the nation’s football clubs were fit and proper to do so. The IFR would have the power to force City’s owners to sell, but such a scenario is viewed as unlikely.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?

The Premier League and City are not commenting.

Given the verdict is in, the two parties will enter into a period of negotiation with regards to when the detail will be released. That will also include suggested redactions, as both sides go through what is likely to be a finding that may well run into the hundreds of pages.

DIDN’T CITY TRIUMPH OVER THE PREMIER LEAGUE RECENTLY ON SPONSORSHIP RULES?

They did, with three senior judges deeming the rules unlawful. As a result, a series of amendments were made. City again launched a legal challenge, but surprisingly came to an agreement with the Premier League in September. Those cases, however, were always separate to the 115, as it became known.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland U-turn confirmed immediately after Man City found guilty of 114 charges
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland U-turn confirmed immediately after Man City found guilty of 114 charges

Erling Haaland was due to speak to the media for Norway this weekend but Manchester City's charges update has reportedly led to a change

View 2 Images Erling Haaland's Norway press conference was cancelled after Man City's guilty verdict (Image: Marius Nordnes / Nordnes Foto/Getty Images)

Norway have reportedly taken the decision to remove Erling Haaland from press conference duty following news of Manchester City being found guilty of alleged financial breaches. The City striker was originally scheduled to face the media this weekend ahead of Norway’s clash against Portugal on Sunday in the Nations League.

‌



News emerged on Friday claiming that City had been found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges that were brought against them by the Premier League back in 2023.

‌



City are now facing a wait to discover what punishment they could receive, with the club having the right to appeal the outcome, which has been widely reported in the media. As a result, City face the prospect of being given a punishment which could range from a points deduction all the way up to expulsion from the Premier League.

‌



Haaland is currently with the Norway squad for the extended international break, and was recently in action on Thursday night as he helped his country claim a 3-2 win over Denmark, where he was on the score sheet twice.

Rodri speaks out on Man City guilty verdict as press conference stopped after 'justice' claim READ MORE :

Premier League clubs consider legal action as Man Utd react to Man City guilty verdict READ MORE :

The striker was expected to speak to the media this weekend ahead of Norway’s next game against Portugal, but that will no longer be the case.

As reported by TV2, Haaland has been replaced for Norway’s pre-match press conference duties by Benfica duo Andreas Schjelderup and Fredrik Aursnes.

‌



Norway’s media manager Morten Skjonsberg is reported to have given a message to the media that Haaland will no longer be speaking to reporters this weekend.

“We are making changes to tomorrow’s press conference,” the message is reported to have read. “(Stale) Solbakken, (Fredrik) Aursnes and (Andreas) Schjelderup will be on the ground floor.”

Haaland has already previously spoken about the charges that were brought against City, where the striker says he was reassured that the situation would be resolved.

"I spoke with the bosses, and in the end, I believe them," Haaland said in an interview with TIME Magazine in July last year. "It’s such a tricky situation for me to even sit there and speak about, because I wasn’t really involved in it.

Sports.title: Premier League clubs consider legal action as Man Utd react to Man City guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs consider legal action as Man Utd react to Man City guilty verdict

Manchester City's ongoing legal battle against the Premier League has already seen Manchester United and other clubs consider taking action over potentially losing millions

View 2 Images Manchester United have been looking into the seasons when they were beaten to silverware by Manchester City after their guilty verdict from financial breaches (Image: (Photo by Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

Manchester United are reportedly weighing up taking action against Manchester City after they were found in breach of 114 financial rules. Between 2009 and 2018, which is the time period City are guilty of breaking Premier League regulations, many clubs including United lost out on silverware.

‌



Eight Premier League titles have been won by City since the 2011/12 campaign, where they infamously pipped United to the crown on the final day. The validity of numerous Carabao and FA Cup triumphs are also now under scrutiny with United going as far as looking for financial compensation.

‌



According to The Athletic, United are one of many clubs that have been exploring the ramifications on their own success and finances due to City's misconduct. Other Premier League teams are considering legal action and it could become a class action, with multiple top-flight outfits coming together as one to seek damages.

‌



Every new Premier League champion if Man City are stripped of titles for 114 guilty charges READ MORE :

An appeal from the latter is expected to arrive first, though, with any action from elsewhere following that process. Their report also claims that United have been looking specifically into the season's they were most impacted.

At the very top of that list would undeniably be the 2011/12 campaign when Sergio Aguero scored an iconic goal to snatch the title from United.

City's historic 100-point season a few years later also came with United finishing second and that campaign was also during the nine-year period of which City are accused of financial breaches in.

‌

The same scenario played out in the season without fans after the Covid-19 pandemic but it did arrive after 2018, which is the final year when the club were under investigation.

Losing out on those honours would have almost certainly had a financial impact on the club regarding things such as prize money and participation in the Club World Cup.

‌



United icon Rio Ferdinand has already made his thoughts perfectly clear on what he wants to see happen through a variety of posts on the social media platform X.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

He first said: Another premier league medal to be added to the cabinet [eyes emoji. He also demanded medals for Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who were in charge during campaigns where United finished second to City.

‌



He concluded his demands by stating: "Seriously tho…. Ryan Giggs should have 14 Premier League titles [nine laughing face emojis]. Come on @premierleague."

View 2 Images Man Utd icon Rio Ferdinand wants to see another Premier League medal added to his trophy cabinet at the expense of Manchester City

City are the only party involved to provide a public statement on the matter with the Premier League refusing to comment as the matter is still ongoing due to City's appeal.

Article continues below

Via a spokesperson, City said: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Sports.title: From tiny crowds to signing Conor McGregor... the rise and rise of BKFC
Sports.content:
From tiny crowds to signing Conor McGregor... the rise and rise of BKFC

Darren Till and Yoel Romero the latest BKFC card in Manchester tonight as the sport of bare-knuckle boxing continues to grow

View Image Conor McGregor with David Feldman

If David Feldman has his way, Conor McGregor will be a bare-knuckle boxer within 18 months.

‌



The signing of the biggest star in UFC history, albeit one with a tarnished reputation, would represent a huge coup for an organisation whose roots can be traced back to warehouse in Philadelphia. And as the promotion returns to Manchester tonight for a show headlined by another two ex-UFC stars in Darren Till and Yoel Romero, BKFC boss Feldman believes the sky is the limit.

‌



Feldman started his promotion in a warehouse with just one fight and four people watching. He is now selling out arenas all over the world and recently staged a show at Boston's Fenway Park. "When I came out with this in early 2010, 2011, the country wasn't ready for it yet; we weren't ready for it yet," he told Mirror Fighting. "As the country evolved into wanting more things that were a little extreme, and people didn't pay attention as much and they were more on their phone... this became more of a sport for them because it was fast-paced, it was quick moments, it was what I call 'oh s***' moments.

‌



"When I came out with it in 2018, the timing was right. Now that we're here in 2026, we're primed to be the top three player in all of combat sports and that's an amazing run in eight years. We didn't develop a promotion; we developed a sport. We had to get regulated everywhere around the world and we had to change perception of what people thought it was.

"This wasn't just us going out and grabbing boxers and doing another boxing event, or MMA guys doing another MMA event. We started a new sport. We had to change the rules and regulations, we had to change the perception, we had to educate people what it was. So to do all that in eight years is a fantastic run and a fantastic rise."

‌



Bare-knuckle boxing inevitably invites criticism due to its perceived level of violence. But Feldman counters: "Over the past eight years, we compiled all our data, and our data now states we have less concussive and sub-concussive damage, we have fewer facial fractures, and we have fewer hand breaks than boxing or mixed martial arts - we only have more cuts. So that's an unbelievable statistic knowing that it looks very brutal, but it's more superficially brutal and not internally brutal.

"I accept it's going to take years and years and years to compile the same data as the other sports have been out there, but we can test for concussions, we can test for brain injury right now. We can test for that, and they don't have it. So what's going to be the future effect of them? We don't know, but I'll tell you this: they're fighting for less time, they're fighting with a less surface and less weight on their fist, so they're not getting hit as hard. We've already measured that. They're not getting hit as hard, they're not getting hit as much, and they're not getting hit for as long of a length. That will tell you three things there that they shouldn't have the type of damage that they have in the other sports."

And of McGregor. The Irishman is currently recovering from the knee injury he suffered in the first round of his ill-fated comeback fight against Max Holloway in July. Assuming he returns to full fitness, he is contracted to have just one more fight with the UFC before becoming a free agent.

Article continues below

The former two-weight world champion is already a part-owner of BKFC and Feldman said: "It's a 10 out of 10 that he fights with us. He's probably not going to fight his next MMA fight until March or April, and he has to get that out of the way first. I'm not saying that's definite; I'm just saying from what I'm hearing. So that's already another seven months down the road, and then you need time to do the fight, so I would say he will fight in 15 to 18 months."

Sports.title: Man City get new punishment verdict as three factors for guilty ruling appeal made clear
Sports.content:
Man City get new punishment verdict as three factors for guilty ruling appeal made clear

Manchester City have been handed new verdicts on what will follow them being found guilty of a significant number of financial charges

View 2 Images Manchester City's next steps regarding an appeal have been revealed (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Two legal experts have shared their thoughts on the next steps for Manchester City regarding their expected appeal and potential punishments. Earlier today, it emerged that the club had been found in breach of 114 Premier League financial regulations.

‌



City were initially charged in February 2023 with this outcome from their hearing against the Premier League just under two years ago. And there is expected to be further delays to any final solution with it understood that City will be appealing against the guilty verdict.

‌



Sports barrister at Church Court Chambers Yasin Patel has now offered his thoughts on the appeal while also making it clear that some clubs could take action.

‌



He said: "City's lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors - importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

Every new Premier League champion if Man City are stripped of titles for 114 guilty charges READ MORE :

Man City verdict LIVE: Premier League giants found guilty of 114 of 115 charges READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

"Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City's wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon."

‌



Ian Hargreaves, a partner at specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, has also discussed City's next moves following the latest development.

Hargreaves said: "The rumoured verdict is not the end of the story but the beginning of a new phase in what has become one of the most closely watched legal battles in global sport.

"The key questions this news raises are what sanction the panel considers proportionate and what guidance can be drawn from previous cases. There is a wide range of options, with a transfer ban at the more moderate end of the spectrum and expulsion from the league the most severe repercussion.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City released a statement of their own

"There is also the question of whether the panel's decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel's findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides."

"The outcome will also have wider implications for the balance of power in European football, although Premier League clubs will point out that these findings relate to historic conduct and not the league's current financial framework."

‌



A City statement read: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool are the sides to have been denied Premier League titles during the period in which City are judged to have secured an unfair advantage.

Article continues below

City are not back in action for another two weeks, with the extended international break stretching into October, and their first opponents upon return are Liverpool — arguably the club who have been denied the most silverware by City over the past decade.

Sports.title: Man Utd star handed late international call-up after 'unfortunate' injury blow
Sports.content:
Man Utd star handed late international call-up after 'unfortunate' injury blow

A Manchester United star has been called up for the Nations League as a result of an international team-mate sustaining an injury

View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee has been called up by the Netherlands (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee has received a call-up to the Netherlands squad. The 25-year-old, who has featured four times for the Red Devils this season, has been selected by head coach Xavi Hernandez as a replacement for the injured Brian Brobbey.

‌



The Sunderland AFC striker limped off clutching his hamstring during the Netherlands' 1-1 draw with Germany on Thursday. Speaking after the match, Xavi confirmed that Brobbey had been forced to return to Sunderland for treatment and that a replacement forward would be drafted in.

‌



The head coach explained: "Brian is indeed injured, unfortunately, so we will call up another striker. We haven't decided who yet; I haven't had time for that yet."

‌



It has now been confirmed that Zirkzee will link up with the Netherlands squad ahead of Sunday's Nations League clash away to Serbia. The United striker is expected to arrive at KNVB headquarters in Amsterdam on Friday evening to undergo a medical assessment before joining his international teammates.

‌



Zirkzee will then fly out to Belgrade on Saturday with the rest of the Dutch party. The fixture against Serbia will be the first of three international appearances Zirkzee is set to make for his country in the coming weeks.

Following the trip to Belgrade, the Netherlands face Greece on Thursday, October 1, before hosting Serbia at Eindhoven in the return fixture.

Xavi will be hunting for his first victory as Netherlands head coach after claiming a draw in his opening match against Germany on Thursday.

‌



Following Felix Nmecha's opener for Jurgen Klopp's side, Liverpool's Cody Gakpo equalised for the Dutch in stoppage time. Yet Xavi believes his side were worthy of all three points against Germany.

"We created chances, applied pressure and we were superior in the second half. He had an incredible game, I told Marc that after the match as well.

"He's a close friend, a top guy and a top professional. I'm happy for him, but he was playing against us. Germany owe the point they got today to Marc-Andre."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury makes surprise offer to Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury makes surprise offer to Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn

Fury and Joshua will clash in Cardiff on December 11 in a fight which has been brewing for a decade - and a world title will be on the line

View Image (Image: tysonfury/Instagram)

Tyson Fury has offered to take Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn out for a pint of Guinness after December's Battle of Britain.

‌



Fury and Joshua will clash in Cardiff on December 11 in a fight which has been brewing for a decade. The British heavyweights will meet for a world title six years after they held the four portions of the championship between them. The build-up to Thursday's announcement was dominated by Hearn's rivalry with UFC chief Dana White.

‌



White, through his boxing outfit Zuffa Boxing, has long insisted he will be involved in the fight but Hearn insists Joshua's contract states he can't be. And Fury told FurociTV: "In Joshua's contract, apparently it says TKO and Dana couldn't be involved. That was in mine, but I took it out. I took it out so he could be involved. F*** 'em, I want him involved, two baldies together. I like Dana, good businessman, and a good guy.

‌



Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight date and venue finally announced READ MORE :

Tyson Fury announces NEXT fight after Anthony Joshua showdown READ MORE :

"He's a man who came from nothing to being a billionaire, and look what he's done with the UFC. Unbelievable. I think he can do really well in boxing. I think he drives Eddie Hearn out, feeds him to the fishes. I haven't got no problem with Eddie, never have done. He's just got, you know, a rival boxer, and that's it.

"There's no big deal between me and Eddie; I'd go out for a beer with Eddie Hearn today, wouldn't give a f***, and tomorrow, and the day after, and next week, and after the fight, no problem. Listen, either way, whatever happens, I'll take him and his pal out for a few Guinnesses. I'll probably have another fight after that, another ten Guinnesses, and then have another fight."

Article continues below

Fury, meanwhile, insists his fight with Joshua won't see the second half. "I'm going to knock AJ out 100 per cent. I just want to get in there and smash him to pieces," he added. "I'm going to box the head off him and stop him inside six or seven rounds. Joshua for me is an old dosser bum and a weightlifter. He lifts too many weights, doesn't have enough speed, and has no cardio."
