World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 25, 2026
World.content:
press review

Uganda Begins $121M South Sudan Power Interconnection Project

Uganda has commenced implementation of the South Sudan-Uganda Power Interconnection Project (SUPIP) after securing US$121 million from the African Development Fund (ADF) to finance the Ugandan component of the regional electricity initiative. Combined with counterpart funding from the Ugandan government, the financing will support the construction of high-voltage transmission infrastructure linking Uganda's electricity grid to South Sudan. The project is expected to facilitate cross-border electricity trade, strengthen Uganda's northern transmission network, and provide South Sudan with access to more reliable and affordable power.

Malawi's Electoral Body Under Fire Over Relocation to Blantyre



The Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) is facing pressure over plans to relocate to Blantyre - the country's commercial capital - alongside a string of staff union grievances that risk undermining public confidence in the body ahead of upcoming elections. An executive order directed MEC to move its headquarters back to Blantyre after it had relocated to Lilongwe in June 2023 to be closer to the seat of government. The commission's staff union has demanded an urgent meeting with leadership, citing unresolved issues surrounding the relocation and lease uncertainties.

Liberian Govt Says Cybercrime Law Doesn't Target Free Speech

Senator Francis Dopoh has reassured Liberians - particularly journalists, activists, and social media users - that the newly enacted cybercrime law is not intended to suppress criticism or peaceful dissent. This clarification follows the recent arrest of an individual over a social media post, which sparked public debate about the legislation. Dopoh said the law instead targets behaviors posing direct threats to individuals, institutions, and national security. He added that its protections for women, girls, and children will help combat online threats, blackmail, and the non-consensual sharing of private images.

Zimbabwe Parliament Wants State of Emergency Over Harare Sewage Crisis

Harare is facing a public health crisis as raw sewage continues flowing into rivers feeding Lake Chivero, the capital's main water source, according to a parliamentary committee report. The report paints a grim picture of Zimbabwe's deteriorating wastewater management system, stating that only 20 of the country's 63 sewage treatment plants are currently operational. Active plants discharge an estimated 570 megaliters of raw sewage daily, worsening pollution levels across major water sources.

World.title: Nigeria: 'Dangote Refinery IPO Opens Ownership to Nigerian Investors'
World.content:
Nigerians can invest in Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals with a minimum subscription of N5,250 under an initial public offering launched recently. The company is offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 each. The offer, valued at about N2.15 trillion if fully subscribed, opened September 14 and is scheduled to close October 13.

FCMB Group Chief Executive, Ladi Balogun, said the offer gives Nigerians access to a world-scale business while demonstrating the growing reach of the country's capital market.

"It presents an opportunity for every Nigerian to experience the benefits of investing in world-class and world-scale businesses that would otherwise be inaccessible,"Balogun said at the opening gong ceremony and Facts Behind the Offer presentation at the Nigerian Exchange in Lagos.

Balogun said Nigeria's capital market was deepening as it attracted retail, high-net-worth, institutional and international investors through a widening range of channels.



"Retail investors are buying shares on their mobile phones through fintechs, banks and brokers," he said. "High-net-worth individuals and institutional investors such as pension funds are bringing depth to the market, while international investors are bringing scale." He said the breadth of participation demonstrated the market's capacity to help credible Nigerian companies raise capital at scale. Balogun also described the refinery as largely insulated from the macroeconomic and currency risks associated with the Nigerian economy.

"The number of such companies on our Exchange is growing," he said. "This indicates the potential and direction of the Nigerian economy."

World.title: Niger: Canadians, Australians and Americans Relaunch Niger's Uranium Industry
World.content:
Niamey — Niger's military junta is seeking to relaunch the country's uranium mining industry with the signing of an agreement with Australian company Atomic Eagle, through which the State of Niger has established the Madaouela Mining Company (MAMICO). The company, 60% owned by Atomic Eagle and 40% by the Nigerien State, plans to revive uranium mining operations in Agadez, in the central-northern part of the country.

The agreement provides for an initial royalty payment of 10 million US dollars, as well as investments in local development and in strengthening the capacity of the mining administration. According to the Ministry of Mines, the project should also create around 1,000 jobs for young Nigeriens.

Madaouela has a resource of 52,843 tonnes of uranium oxide, an estimate based on exploration carried out by the previous licence holder, GoviEx Uranium Inc., which obtained the licence in 2016.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The agreement settles the dispute that arose following the expropriation of the project from GoviEx in 2024. GoviEx and Tombador Iron merged in November 2025, creating Atomic Eagle. Under the agreement reached, the new company will withdraw its arbitration proceedings within seven days of the signing of the agreement.

The pact signed with the Australian company came just days after Canadian mining company Global Atomic obtained approval from the Board of Directors of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) for debt financing of up to 414.2 million US dollars for its Dasa uranium mine project, also in the Agadez region.

The Dasa deposit is operated by Société Minière de Dasa (SOMIDA), a Niger-based company 80% owned by Global Atomic and 20% by the Nigerien government. Discovered in 2010 and authorized in 2020, the deposit has been under mining activity since 2022, but its full development has been subject to several delays. The completion of the mine is now expected in the first half of 2028, with commissioning scheduled for the second half of the year.

Niger's mining sector was historically dominated by French industry, first Areva and subsequently Orano. Niamey nationalized the local subsidiary amid deteriorating relations with France and closer ties with Russia. Orano, 90% owned by the French State, has launched several legal actions against Niger, accusing the authorities of confiscating its assets in the country.

Despite the Russian presence in the country and the insecurity caused by jihadist groups, Anglo-Saxon mining companies do not appear to be facing particular obstacles in investing in Niger's uranium sector.

World.title: Nigeria: Nigeria, U.S. Sign Framework to Attract Investment Into $700bn Mineral Resources
World.content:
Nigeria's Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US Deputy Secretary of State, Christopher Landau.

The framework is expected to use the relationship between the Nigerian and US governments as a foundation for business-to-business transactions and investment across Nigeria's mineral value chain.

Nigeria and the United States have signed a framework aimed at attracting American investment into Nigeria's estimated $700 billion mineral resources.

The agreement was signed on behalf of the governments of the two countries by Nigeria's Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the US Deputy Secretary of State, Christopher Landau, on Wednesday at Nigeria's Mission House in New York.

According to a statement by Kehinde Bamigbetan, Special Adviser to the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, the signing took place on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.



The framework is expected to use the relationship between the Nigerian and US governments as a foundation for business-to-business transactions and investment across Nigeria's mineral value chain.

It covers cooperation in geological data and exploration, mineral development and processing, infrastructure and technical capacity.

Speaking at the ceremony, Mr Alake said the agreement represented a shift from Nigeria's traditional role as an exporter of raw minerals towards greater domestic value addition.

"Some agreements manage the present, and some agreements shape the future. The framework we sign today belongs to the second kind," Mr Alake said.

He said Nigeria and the US shared the view that supply chains for critical minerals must be secure, resilient and supported by responsible investment.

"But let me be clear about Nigeria's ambition. We are not here to remain a source of raw material for the values that others create. Our goal is to turn potential into lasting value at home through stronger local processing, new skills, quality jobs, and new opportunities for Nigerian businesses," he said.

According to the minister, the framework would enable both countries to collaborate on exploration, mineral development and processing, infrastructure and technical capacity.

He said its implementation would support the economic diversification objectives of President Bola Tinubu's administration and promote industrial growth.

Mr Alake, however, said the signing was only the beginning of the process.

"Now comes the harder and more important work: moving from agreement to implementation. A signature is a promise, results are the proof," he said.

He added that Nigeria would, in the coming months, identify viable projects, mobilise investments and establish commercial partnerships capable of delivering measurable benefits to both countries.

US pledges partnership

Mr Landau said the United States regarded Nigeria as a strategic partner, describing the country as a regional power because of its population and economic position.

He said the agreement would create opportunities for greater prosperity in both countries and reaffirmed the US commitment to supporting Nigeria's economic growth.

"The signal we are sending is that the United States and Nigeria are partners," he said.

Mr Landau said the two countries had undertaken several initiatives under Presidents Donald Trump and Bola Tinubu over the previous one and a half years, adding that Washington wanted to build on the momentum.

The US delegation included the Deputy Assistant Secretary for West African Affairs, Rich Michaels; Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Southern Africa, Foreign Assistance and Critical Minerals, Chris Kulukundis; Senior Policy Adviser to the Deputy Secretary, Wyatt Toehlkeke; and Jitu Sardar.

Sanwo-Olu, other Nigerian officials attend

Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu witnessed the signing alongside the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development, Yusuf Yabo; Director-General of the Nigerian Mining Cadastral Office, Simon Nkom; Executive Secretary of the Solid Minerals Development Fund, Fatima Shinkafi; and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Solid Minerals Company, Martin Imonitie.

Close 

Governor Sanwo-Olu later said on X that he was present at the Mission House when Nigeria and the US signed an important framework for investment in Nigeria's mining sector.

"The focus of the framework is to move beyond simply exporting raw materials by building a stronger local value chain through processing, exploration, better infrastructure and technical capacity.

"This will help us turn Nigeria's mineral wealth into lasting growth and support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's Renewed Hope Agenda to diversify our economy.

He said the initiative could help convert Nigeria's mineral resources into economic opportunities and support the federal government's economic diversification agenda.

World.title: Tanzania: Cash Still King in Public Transport Despite Four-Year Digital Push
World.content:
Dar es Salaam — CASH remains overwhelmingly king across Tanzania's public transport sector, with electronic transactions accounting for only 6.8 per cent of fares collected over the past four years, official data show.

Land Transport Regulatory Authority (LATRA) Director General Habibu Suluo said yesterday that 62.18 million passengers were recorded through online ticketing systems during the four-year period, of whom 59.27 million, equivalent to 95.3 per cent, paid their fares in cash. Only 2.91 million passengers, or 4.7 per cent, used digital payment channels, he said.

In monetary terms, cash payments accounted for 1.99tri/- of the 2.13tri/- collected, while electronic payments amounted to 144.28bn/-, representing 6.8 per cent of the total.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The figures highlight the gap between the policy drive towards digital payments and their adoption across the transport sector, despite requirements for electronic transactions in several services.

The requirements, backed by the Electronic Transactions Act (Cap. 442), cover bus rapid transit services, long distance buses, ferries and ride-hailing platforms.

Mr Suluo acknowledged the challenges of increasing digital adoption, but said operators and the government were gradually recognising the transparency benefits of electronic payment systems.

Beyond digital payments, LATRA reported significant growth in the regulated transport sector during the sixth phase government's tenure.

Commercial vehicle licences increased by 146.1 per cent, from 239,953 in 2021/22 to 590,468 in 2025/26, he said.

The number of buses connected to LATRA's Vehicle Tracking System also rose from 5,979 to 14,743 during the same period.

Turning to road safety during the rainy season, Mr Suluo urged transport stakeholders to prepare for anticipated El Niño rains and ensure vehicles were properly maintained before starting journeys.

He said vehicle owners should pay particular attention to braking systems, tyres, lights, windscreens and windscreen wipers.

"Heavy rains could cause flooding, water to overflow across roads, slippery surfaces, soil erosion, landslides and rockfalls, damage to roads, strong winds and fog, all of which could compromise road safety," he said.

Mr Suluo urged drivers to avoid flooded areas, particularly where water was flowing rapidly or its depth was unknown and to reduce speed and increase following distances during rain, fog and other periods of poor visibility.

He also advised drivers to exercise greater caution in areas affected by landslides, erosion, cracks or damaged road edges.

Passengers, he said, should check weather forecasts and road-condition updates before travelling and avoid unnecessary journeys during heavy rains.

World.title: Africa: Nigeria Demands Two Permanent UN Seats, Veto Powers for Africa
World.content:
Nigeria has demanded at least two permanent seats for Africa on the UN Security Council, with veto powers for as long as the privilege exists.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima made the demand while delivering President Bola Tinubu's national statement at the 81st UN General Assembly in New York.

He also demanded five non-permanent seats for Africa, in line with the continent's longstanding common position on reforming the Security Council.

Shettima said the Council's present configuration no longer reflected contemporary geopolitical realities and weakened the legitimacy of global decision-making.



"The world of 2026 cannot remain captive to the distribution of power in 1945," he said.

He said Africa could no longer remain outside permanent membership while issues concerning the continent continued to occupy substantial attention of the Council.

According to him, Nigeria's position is consistent with the Ezulwini Consensus and Sirte Declaration, adopted as the Common African Position.

Under the position, Africa seeks at least two permanent seats with all existing privileges, alongside five non-permanent seats on the Council.

The African Union reaffirmed the demand in May, saying Africa's exclusion from permanent representation constituted a historical imbalance requiring correction.

Shettima argued that institutions claiming authority to act for humanity must adequately reflect the people on whose behalf decisions are taken.

He linked Security Council reform to efforts to restore confidence in multilateralism amid widening geopolitical divisions.

The Vice-President also reaffirmed Nigeria's commitment to the UN Charter and international cooperation.

He said Nigeria supported an international system where diplomacy takes precedence over coercion and international law guides relations among states.

Shettima recalled Nigeria's contributions to international and regional peace operations in Liberia, Sierra Leone, Darfur, Mali and The Gambia.

He said Nigeria also continues to work through ECOWAS, the African Union and Gulf of Guinea mechanisms.

According to him, these efforts cover mediation, counter-terrorism, democratic governance and maritime security.

Shettima said persistent conflicts across different regions underscored the need to return to dialogue, collective responsibility and peaceful settlement of disputes.

Close 

He identified the conflict in Sudan and other theatres as requiring urgent diplomacy because of their humanitarian, economic and geopolitical consequences.

The Vice-President also warned against a global environment where propaganda blurred distinctions between victims and aggressors and complicated accountability.

He maintained that an inclusive and effective UN remained indispensable to global peace and sustainable development.

Nigeria's demand comes amid renewed calls by African leaders for reforms to an institution whose permanent membership remains unchanged since its creation.

The Security Council has five permanent members: China, France, Russia, the UK and the US, each possessing veto power.

Africa currently has no permanent representative on the Council.

The African Union's preferred reform model provides for at least two permanent African seats, including veto privileges while existing members retain them.

The reform model also seeks five non-permanent seats for Africa.

Shettima said Nigeria remained committed to a multilateral order capable of responding more credibly to 21st-century realities.

According to him, differences among nations must not obscure their common humanity or responsibility to preserve peace for future generations. (NAN)

World.title: Brandi Glanville emptied her 401(k) after spending ‘hundreds of thousands’ on medical bills
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Brandi Glanville needed a comeback — personally and financially.

After years of costly health struggles turned her life upside down, the former "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" star told Fox News Digital she needed to get back to work.

"I had the leisure of saying no in the past, but then I had all these medical bills and whatnot," she admitted. "So I had to say yes. And it was kind of like at a time where I needed to prove to myself that I could do it again."

BRANDI GLANVILLE ENDS UP IN URGENT CARE AFTER TRYING VIRAL TIKTOK TREND

But for Glanville, the financial fallout from her health battle has been just as daunting as the physical toll.

"The medical system here is broken," Glanville explained. "So I have, like, from 8 a.m. on, I have creditors from, like, medical things calling me, like from Cedars-Sinai. It's out of control. Like I spent hundreds of thousands of dollars that I had saved. I emptied my 401(k). And it's all for medical bills. And I had insurance, and they told me nothing was wrong. I'm so angry. You know, going into my mid-fifties I had a cushion and that's gone. So it's very scary right now."

After years of suffering, Glanville revealed in September that she had been diagnosed with highly resistant ESBL Klebsiella and Enterobacter with biofilm, coccidioidomycosis, also known as Valley fever, Demodex dermatitis and mononucleosis.

Glanville has said her daily IV treatment was expected to cost between $3,300 and $6,000 per month.

WATCH: BRANDI GLANVILLE SAYS HEALTH BATTLE FORCED HER TO SPEND ‘HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS'

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Glanville previously shared that she believed she picked up a parasite after visiting Morocco in 2023. She suffered from facial paralysis and was initially diagnosed with stress-induced angioedema. She told Fox News Digital at the time that she spent more than $70,000 in an attempt to find an answer to the medical mystery that consumed her daily life and disfigured her face.

After everything her body had already endured, Glanville was determined to test her limits on "Special Forces: World's Toughest Test." One challenge pushed those limits further than she expected.

While filming the show, Glanville said contestants were trained on how to fall from a helicopter into the water. But moments before her jump, an instructor told her to keep her head up — a last-second direction she said left her little time to react.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"My head hit the water. It was like a Mack truck – it, like, ran over my head. I thought that was it," she recalled. "And then a few seconds later, my body hits the water so hard. It was paralyzing almost. I was like, 'Oh my God.' But it was in slow motion."

The former "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" star said she suffered a perforated eardrum, a concussion, a bruised sternum and a cracked rib — injuries that forced her to travel by boat to the hospital because doctors didn't want her flying. Glanville recalled battling an intense headache on top of the excruciating pain from her rib injury, which made it difficult to breathe or cough.

Once at the hospital, Glanville said doctors warned her she couldn't fly and told her she could be stuck there for at least two weeks and potentially need surgery. But after spending several days recovering and returning to the hospital for another evaluation, the reality star said she was determined to leave — even if doctors still weren't thrilled about her getting on a plane.

Battered but undeterred, Glanville said she still considered the experience a personal victory.

"Honestly, I'm so proud of myself. I feel like a badass, even though I didn't last long," she told Fox News Digital. "I went in, I conquered, I got hurt, and then I left and that was enough for me. "

World.title: UK Prime Minister says football fans 'singled out' by alcohol ban not imposed on rugby matches
World.content:
United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham is pushing back against England’s restrictions on alcohol at men’s soccer matches, calling the ban "discrimination" and suggesting the rules could be tested on a trial basis.

Burnham told reporters, "I don’t think it’s fair for football fans to be singled out," as he argued that they should not face restrictions that do not apply to spectators at other sporting events.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Under current laws, fans are prohibited from drinking alcohol in view of the pitch at stadiums hosting clubs in England’s top five tiers of men’s football. Those restrictions do not apply to other sports.

ANDY BURNHAM TAKES OVER AS UK PRIME MINISTER, CALLS FOR 'NEW POLITICAL MODEL'

The Football Supporters’ Association, which advocates for football fans in England and Wales, has called for the "outdated" legislation to be reviewed. Police chiefs, however, have warned against relaxing the law and want to meet with Burnham to "explain the challenges."

The legislation dates to 1985, when it was introduced by Margaret Thatcher’s government for football grounds in England and Wales. Then-Home Secretary Leon Brittan said alcohol was a "major contributory factor in violent and disorderly behavior" at stadiums.

Burnham’s connection to the sport is personal. He is a proud football fan and a season-ticket holder at Everton, the Premier League club.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Prior to becoming the head of government of the U.K., Burnham spoke out against restrictions on football fans while attending a rugby league match at Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium. Unlike during men’s football games, spectators were allowed to consume alcohol in the stands.

While in New York City for the United Nations General Assembly, Burnham was asked whether his position had changed now that he was in Downing Street. "I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different," the prime minister replied.

"And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done. It could happen on a trial basis. But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long held view of mine. I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently."

Government sources told the BBC that Burnham was restating a long-held personal view rather than announcing a new government policy. Within government, however, the comments are not being interpreted as a sign that Burnham intends to change the law, according to the outlet.

A spokesman for the U.K. Football Policing Unit warned that changing the law could create new challenges for police and raise concerns about the "safety of staff and fans at football games."

The spokesman said: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behavior from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behavior."

FSA chairman Tom Greatrex pushed back against that argument, saying it was "unfair to criminalize football fans for having a pint while watching the match, especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol (while) watching an Oasis gig or rugby league."

World.title: Florida GOP nominee blasts 20-year Dem incumbent as a 'socialist' rubber-stamp with 'precious little to show'
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Calling out federal waste and foreign aid subsidies while pointing to his own record of bucking party leadership in Tallahassee, GOP 14th congressional district nominee Mike Beltran promises to bring a sharp litigator’s cross-examination to Washington’s budget crisis.

In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital detailing his bid to unseat 20-year Democratic incumbent Kathy Castor, the former Florida state representative laid out a case rooted in strict fiscal accountability, pledged to challenge even Republican leadership on bloated federal budgets, and warned of the Democrats' embrace of socialism.

HOUSE CONSERVATIVES UNLEASH MULTIMILLION-DOLLAR MIDTERM BLITZ AGAINST DEM 'SOCIALIST' INSURGENCY

Beltran argues that despite her lengthy tenure on Capitol Hill, the people of Tampa Bay have not been served well by Kathy Castor.

"People in Tampa Bay have precious little to show for Kathy Castor's two decades of incumbency. She's had no major legislative initiatives. All she's really done is rename post offices. And all that's likely to happen if we reelect her is for her to rename every post office from Tampa to Timbuktu.

"She votes with her party over 90% of the time, including radical socialists. She voted in lockstep with Nancy Pelosi and she's poised to elect the Speaker Hakeem Jeffries. And Speaker Hakeem Jeffries would appoint a Chair Raskin, a Chair Omar, a Chair Cortez, and those folks would push radical policies in Congress that are completely out of line with what Tampa families need."

Beltran argues that in the Florida Legislature he served as an independent conservative voice, not automatically beholden to party leadership, and pledges to continue that approach in Washington.

"I've had the courage to vote against special interests even when my own party had lost its way. I've voted against insurance companies, home builders, trial lawyers, I voted against various special interests…whenever somebody was doing something that wasn't good for Tampa families.

"And I had that bipartisan record throughout my time, starting in 2019 and continuing through to 2024, unlike my opponent who discovered bipartisanship merely weeks ago. So I'm always going to do what's best for the communities that I represent, regardless of party, regardless of special interests, regardless of pressure. And that's what I'm proud of, having that independent voting record."

Beltran argues that the United States needs to reexamine its military and geopolitical relationships, with an eye to fiscal prudence:

"It cannot be a one-sided exchange. You cannot have a wealthy country like Germany spend under 2% of GDP on their military when we're spending over 5% of our GDP on our military budgets, about a trillion dollars. And a lot of that is spent overseas protecting other wealthy countries.

"You see Ukraine and Israel, they're defending themselves from their adversaries. They're doing a good job of that. But we are borrowing $2 trillion a year from countries like China. And that's causing inflation. And what that says is that we don't have money to be sending, particularly to wealthy allies like Germany and Spain.

"These are countries where we have bases, where we've had trouble getting basing privileges or overflight rights for the conflicts that we do need to engage in. And we shouldn't be subsidizing them anymore.

"You see Israel spends over 10% of GDP on defense, as does South Korea. Those countries are carrying the weight of their own defense, but we don't see that from all of our NATO allies. And they're a lot closer to these rogue states, to these conflict regions than we are. They should be doing more, and they're doing less, and that's unacceptable."

As an attorney, Beltran makes the case that he will bring a strong skill-set to Capitol Hill, to do away with business as usual and to fight for the citizens of Hillsborough County:

"My legal skills are quite good. I'm a good cross examiner. I'll be good at scrutinizing witnesses who come before committees that I serve on. I've litigated in the federal courts, so I know the federal statutes. I know issues that need to be redressed. I know how to write statutes so that they can be easily applied by judges, so that attorneys can counsel their clients on what the law is and what they need to do to comply with that.

"I'm proud to be a practicing attorney. I've helped a lot of businesses and individuals throughout Tampa Bay for almost 20 years.

FIRST DATA CENTER BILL CLEARS HOUSE AS BOTH PARTIES SCRAMBLE FOR ANSWERS ON AFFORDABILITY

"And my opponent is also an attorney, but she hasn't practiced in a very long time. She was, I think, a land use attorney, she says, before she was a county commissioner. But I don't think she brings that same skill-set. I've never seen her cross-examine a witness to any effect. And I haven't seen her apply her legal skills to any legislative initiative. In fact, it's kind of difficult to identify anything that she's enacted that's of any particular value to Tampa or otherwise."

Kathy Castor has repeatedly voted against the interests of ordinary Americans in Florida's 14th district, Beltran argues:

"Well, she opposed tax cuts for the middle class and working class and retirees. She opposed removing taxes on tips, removing taxes on Social Security, removing taxes on overtime.

"And she wanted to pay, through taxpayer funds, for trans surgeries for children. And that was a very recent vote. That wasn't something that we have to reach into ancient history to find. And I opposed that.

"I see no reason why a single mother here in Hillsborough County should be paying taxes to pay for trans surgeries for minors while she actually is being taxed on her overtime or her tips."

Beltran pledges to confront the leadership of his own party if he disagrees with their policies, but also notes he will work with Democrats:

"Obviously, we've had Republicans who have also spent too much money. And so I'm going to go to Washington. I'm going to work with my party, and I'll work across the aisle, and I'll work with any administration that's in power to identify waste, fraud, and abuse, identify unnecessary government programs, identify savings, and identify cost controls, and make sure that we are the fiscal conservatives that we say we are.

"That's what's necessary to save this country because we need to balance the budget and we need pay down the debt and we need to live within our means, because if we don't balance our budget, then the budget will be balanced for us and it will be done when somebody cuts off our credit and people stop lending to us."

Finally, as democratic socialist candidates have won Democratic primaries across the nation and in Florida, Beltran notes that Castor has consistently refused to condemn socialist ideology, or candidates with such views in her own party.

"We see Kathy Castor, who's embraced Angie Nixon, who is one of those avowed socialist candidates. She said that her party was a big tent party, and that needs to be a very big tent to accommodate Angie Nixon…I'm not sure I'd like to be in a tent of any size with her, but my opponent welcomes her with open arms.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"And she's going to vote in lockstep with these socialists, first to elect Hakeem Jeffries and then to appoint these socialists to committee chairmanships. She's done very little to distance herself from the radicals within her party. Even as she masquerades recently as a moderate, she will empower the socialists.

"And that's really what's at stake in November. It's not just me, it's not just Kathy Castor, it is the direction of the country and whether we're going to embrace these radical policies, or whether we are going to have economic growth and prosperity and safety here in the United States."

World.title: Carville says the GOP is better than Democrats at one key skill the 2028 Dem nominee will need
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville said Republicans are better at pushing positive and negative narratives than Democrats on Thursday and warned his party that its 2028 nominee will need that skill to win.

Carville has frequently condemned the Trump administration, predicting that 2026 will be a year of landmark victories for the Democratic Party. He has suggested multiple times that President Donald Trump, after presumably losing political power in the midterms, may resign from office early and be pardoned by Vice President JD Vance after Vance becomes president.

One listener, however, contacted Carville and his co-host Al Hunt on their "Politics War Room" podcast, juxtaposing how Republicans and Democrats talk about each other.

"He wants to know why the Republicans are so much better than the Democrats at creating boogeymen," Hunt summarized. "Republicans will paint all Democrats with a socialist brush, yet Democrats can’t seem to do the same thing when it comes to racism, antisemitism or corruption, despite the fact that all three are prevalent among Republican members of Congress."

100 DAYS UNTIL MIDTERMS AND DEMOCRATS ARE WINNING BECAUSE THEY ACTUALLY HAVE A MESSAGE

"The gist of the question is Republicans are very good at painting Democrats as boogeymen, socialists, communists, all that kind of stuff," Hunt continued. "But the Democrats don’t do as good a job, Rob worries, about painting Republicans with their racism, antisemitism, etc."

Carville argued that the Republicans are doing so badly they may not even need the Democrats to condemn them.

"First of all, it is a good question," Carville replied. "Secondly, what’s happened now is they’re painting themselves that way, OK? They’re going down not because of Democratic messaging, not because of a relentless offense by the Democrats that, you know, points out their foibles. They’re going down because the public sees it, and they don’t need that. A Democratic intervention right now is not called for."

Carville said that the Democratic nominee will need to master this skill to win in 2028.

"The gist of the question from our listener is totally correct. And for whatever reasons, Ben [sic], I think it’s because we’re more of a coalition. Not only do we not have a consistent negative story to tell about the other party, we don’t have a consistent positive story to tell about ourselves," he said. "Hope and pray that in 2028 we have a really skilled candidate that’s able to do that."

"But that is a fact of American politics," he added. "We’re not as good as they are at the negative, and we’re not as good as they are at a positive."

SOCIALISTS ARE HELPING GOP CAMPAIGNS HEADING INTO NOVEMBER

Mary Marslender, a former senior advisor to Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., and a former Trump appointee who is now a Republican consultant, said there is a disparity in how well each side uses that rhetoric against the other.

"It isn’t even close, and it isn’t the disparity Carville thinks it is," she told Fox News Digital. "When Republicans label Democrats as socialists, it’s not just empty rhetoric; it’s grounded in how many Democrats describe themselves. Recent polling found that 59 percent of Democrats identify as supporters of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA)."

"The DSA has openly advocated for policies such as court-packing, sweeping changes to financial institutions, the abolition of capitalism, open borders, eliminating prisons and the Senate, and expanding administrative power. The Democratic Party has embraced socialism, and there seems to be no turning back," Marslender continued.

However, she disagreed with Carville's comment that Republicans have already destroyed their own reputation without Democratic help.

"Carville’s claim is more political spin than reality," Marslender said. "If Republicans had truly destroyed their own credibility, Democrats would not need Carville’s advice to ‘sit this one out.’ In fact, Carville reveals the Democratic Party’s real problem: they lack both a compelling message and a strong messenger, and are now hoping for a ‘really skilled candidate in 2028.’"

"A party that has watched the Trump administration deliver on border security, energy independence, and prioritizing American workers cannot credibly claim that Republicans have already undermined themselves," she continued. "If Republicans were as self-destructive as Carville claims, Democrats wouldn’t be waiting for a future savior; they would already be capitalizing on Republicans’ so-called failures. Carville’s argument underscores that Democrats still recognize weaknesses in their own positioning and strategy."

Most of what Democrats do today is name-calling."

World.title: Indiana attorney general sues high school sports association over race-based board quota
World.content:
Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita has sued the state’s governing body for high school athletics over a policy that reserves two seats on its board of directors for racial minorities.

The lawsuit, filed Wednesday in Marion County Superior Court, seeks to force the Indiana High School Athletic Association (IHSAA) to eliminate a provision reserving two of its 19 board seats for "qualified minorities." The association’s bylaws define a minority director as "an individual other than a white male or female."

"Hoosier students should not be governed by a sports association that picks its leaders based on race," Rokita said in a statement announcing the lawsuit. "IHSAA’s quota tells kids that skin color, rather than merit, is an appropriate way to judge people."

TRUMP ADMIN'S PUSH TO SCRAP DEI IN FEDERAL GOVERNMENT TAKES LANDMARK STEP WITH NEW HIRING RULE

"That lesson has no place in Indiana’s education system, and, regardless, the law does not permit it," he continued. "The IHSAA exists to build character. A racial litmus test for choosing leadership on the IHSAA’s board does the opposite, and after months of delay, the Association left us no choice but to take legal action."

The state’s complaint alleges the quota constitutes an "overt racial classification" that treats potential board members differently based solely on their race. It accuses the IHSAA of violating Indiana’s nonprofit laws by abusing its authority, misapplying corporate assets and acting inconsistently with its stated public purpose.

The lawsuit asks the court to issue a permanent injunction requiring the IHSAA to immediately remove the racial qualification from its bylaws and prohibit the association from adopting future policies that allocate board seats based on race. It also seeks a declaration that the existing provisions violate Indiana law.

The IHSAA defended its policies in a statement Thursday and said it was disappointed Rokita proceeded with litigation.

"The IHSAA disagrees with any suggestion that our bylaws violate federal and state civil rights laws or in any way constitute an abuse of its nonprofit status," the organization said. "To the contrary, the IHSAA is committed to serving all student-athletes and member schools throughout Indiana. Consistent with that mission, we value broad representation and diverse perspectives among those who help guide and support interscholastic athletics across the state."

The organization added that the lawsuit was filed despite its willingness to consider Rokita’s concerns through its "established governance and bylaw review processes."

"For more than a century, the IHSAA has governed high school athletics on behalf of its member schools," the statement said. "It is unfortunate that distractions like today’s lawsuit take away from what really matters: the student-athletes."

The lawsuit marks the latest escalation in a dispute first brought into public view last year.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Fox News Digital reported in May 2025 that the Pacific Legal Foundation and Equal Protection Project had sent a letter demanding that the IHSAA remove race- and sex-based requirements from its board-selection process.

At the time, the bylaws provided for a 19-member board that included two "qualified female representatives" and two "qualified minorities." The groups warned that legal action could follow if the provisions were not removed.

"We hope that IHSAA will do the right thing and voluntarily remedy the discriminatory bylaws provisions, but if it does not, all legal options are on the table," Equal Protection Project founder William A. Jacobson told Fox News Digital at the time.

Pacific Legal Foundation attorney Laura D’Agostino similarly argued that candidates should be evaluated on their qualifications rather than their demographic characteristics.

"Public boards should reflect the talents and commitment of all citizens, not arbitrary categories of race or sex," D’Agostino told Fox News Digital. "Every individual who wants to step up and serve their community should be encouraged to do so based on what they bring to the table, not held back because of who they are."

According to the new complaint, Rokita’s office separately directed the IHSAA in April 2026 to remove its racial quota. The association responded in June that it disagreed with the attorney general’s legal position but would consider the issue during its next round of bylaw amendments in May 2027.

After further correspondence and an Aug. 25 meeting of the IHSAA Executive Committee produced no immediate change, Rokita’s office proceeded with the lawsuit.

The complaint says the IHSAA has used some form of a racial requirement for board membership since 1993. The current definition has remained in place since the association’s 2001-02 bylaws, according to the filing.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The lawsuit targets the two seats reserved for racial minorities. It does not ask the court to eliminate the two board seats designated for female representatives.

World.title: Secret service, cheap beer and Arch Manning: Tennessee prepares for college football chaos, with Trump visit
World.content:
KNOXVILLE, TN - Secret Service officials stood outside Neyland Stadium on Friday afternoon putting the final touches on their plans for President Trump's arrival to the biggest college football game of the weekend.

Roads were starting to be closed, students were roaming around Tennessee's campus on their way from class, while a number of Texas Longhorn fans took in the sights on this beautiful day before a top-15 showdown in the SEC.

It's all adding up for a monumental afternoon in Knoxville, as Arch Manning makes his first ever stop at the University of Tennessee in hopes of beating his uncle Peyton's beloved Vols.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Essentially, this game has everything you could ask for in college football. And, if the previous two weeks in Austin and Oxford are any indication, we are in for one heck of an afternoon.

As you made your way around the beautiful Tennessee campus, it wasn’t hard to pick up on the anticipation of Saturday's game. For only the fifth time in each team's history, the Vols and Longhorns will play each other, with this one taking place inside the historic Neyland Stadium.

DONALD TRUMP ADDS POLITICAL STAKES, ANTICIPATION AND POTENTIAL SIDELINE CHAOS TO TEXAS-TENNESSEE SHOWDOWN

Standing inside the Tennessee apparel store, fans ran into former wide receiver Joey Kent.

Around other parts of campus, Peyton Manning took time to visit with students, one day after country star Ella Langley brought her expansive tour to the Vols basketball arena.

But, there is also something to be said for the visiting fans who are lucky enough to make the trip to Tennessee for the game on Saturday. There were plenty of Texas fans wearing burnt orange roaming the beautiful campus, throwing up the signature 'Hook em' as they ran into some of their own.

For the first time this season, Arch Manning and the Longhorns have hit the road, with 102,000 fans waiting for their arrival on Saturday morning.

"This place is gorgeous, and I'm not afraid to pay an opponent a compliment," one Texas fan told OutKick. "I've been to a number of SEC campuses, but this one might take the cake on Saturday (besides DKR). Everyone has been so nice to us since we arrived on Thursday, and the downtown scene with what i think is 'Market Square' is gorgeous.

"But, it will end up being a whole lot better when we leave here with a win."

Secret Service Preparing for What Will Be a Chaotic Saturday in Knoxville for Trump

At just about every corner around Neyland Stadium, you could see security preparing for Donald Trump's arrival.

Meetings were being held outside Tennessee's cathedral, while it wasn’t hard to notice officers walking the perimeter, even if they were plain-clothed officers.

The security has obviously been increased ahead of President Donald Trump touching down just miles away from campus.

Tennessee officials were so hellbent on getting fans inside the stadium before kickoff, amid the increased law enforcement traffic, that they are offering half-priced concessions from 9 a.m. ET to 10 a.m. ET inside Neyland Stadium, including alcohol.

FOUR DAYS IN OXFORD: INSIDE THE CHAOTIC RETURN OF LANE KIFFIN TO OLE MISS, THAT TURNED INTO PURE CINEMA

As for fans and students on the Tennessee campus, the presence of President Donald Trump brought a mixed bag of feelings.

"Why in the world would he (Trump) choose this game? He should have gone to Florida or something," one student told OutKick. "This place is going to be a traffic nightmare already. But, I guess he has to garner some more support for a bill (Protect College Sports Act) that does not help the everyday citizen."

Another student, who found out about Trump coming to campus on Friday morning, was excited about being in the same stadium as a sitting president.

"Look, I'll be able to one day tell my children I got to watch a football game in the same stadium as the President," a Tennessee sophomore told OutKick. "I really don't care what side of the aisle you're on or how bad the traffic will be, it's actually pretty cool."

That's one way to entice fans to enter the gates early: just offer them cheap beer that will take some of the sting away from potentially missing out on a full-blown tailgate.

While the exact time has yet to be announced, due to security measures, the President will most likely be scene from inside the stadium as Air Force One flies over before landing at Tyson McGee Airport. Then, he will depart for Tennessee's campus via motorcade, with a number of streets being blocked off on Friday night in advance of his arrival.

No. 1 Texas Versus No. 14 Tennessee in High-Stakes SEC Showdown

Somewhat lost in all of the pregame talk of security and traffic concerns, we are prepared to witness a monumental game between two storied programs.

And yes, there will be plenty of family members with the last name 'Manning' in the house to either cheer on their nephew Arch, or quietly pull for the Tennessee Vols.

You can obviously expect Peyton Manning to be torn, though he clearly wants to see his nephew find some type of success in the same stadium that the elder-Manning set multiple passing records.

TENNESSEE LINEBACKER ARION CARTER TURNS $427 NCAA SUSPENSION INTO POWERFUL CANCER RESEARCH FUNDRAISER

But, this is also a showdown between two teams fighting to keep a goose-egg in the loss column.

Can Tennessee upset the No. 1 ranked Longhorns behind true-freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon? Sure they can, though relying on his running backs will play a pivotal part in this matchup. We all saw what Arch did through three quarters against Ohio State two weeks ago, and it wasn’t as if he lit up the scoreboard last week against UTSA.

For the Vols to beat Texas, it will take a monumental effort from a defensive unit led by All-SEC linebacker Arion Carter. And, this won't be an easy game for that group, as linebackers coach William Ingle is currently hospitalized with an unknown illness just a few miles away from the Tennessee campus.

Though, as we've seen over the past three weeks in college football, anything is possible once you hit the field, and it would not be shocking if No. 14 Tennessee pulled off the upset on Saturday afternoon.

Either way, we are set to see a number of firsts in Knoxville.

Get yourself situated for a fantastic Saturday, and it all starts here in East Tennessee.

World.title: Supreme Court for the third time rejects Republican redistricting push in Missouri
World.content:
WASHINGTON — For the third time, the Supreme Court on Friday shut down efforts by Missouri Republicans to use a new congressional map in the midterm elections that are already underway.

The court blocked an appeals court ruling that sought to revive the 2025 map despite two previous Supreme Court decisions and a ruling by the Missouri Supreme Court that ruled against Republicans on the same issue.

In doing so, the justices granted an emergency application filed by People Not Politicians, the group challenging the new map.

The election will proceed using a 2022 map that includes six seats held by Republicans and two held by Democrats. The state has already started sending out ballots to military and overseas voters, and some absentee voting began Tuesday.

The proposed 2025 map would have eliminated one of the Democratic seats, held by Rep. Emanuel Cleaver.

The Missouri map was part of a nationwide push by Republicans at the urging of President Donald Trump to draw new congressional districts that would favor their candidates. Democrats in other states, including California, responded by drawing new maps, too.

The St. Louis-based 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Monday ruled that the Republican-drawn Missouri map could be used, but it never went into effect. The Supreme Court’s ruling Tuesday overturns that decision.

The appeals court had ruled the state had to use the 2025 map in part because the primary election had already taken place using it. But in a conflicting ruling, the Missouri Supreme Court said the 2022 map had to be used, while making it clear that Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins, a Republican, was to blame for the confusion.

The state high court ultimately held Hoskins in contempt for his actions.

The court battle started after opponents of the new map gained enough signatures to trigger a state referendum on whether it should be used. Under state law, whenever a state law is subject to a referendum, it is suspended until after the vote takes place.

But Hoskins delayed a decision on whether the referendum push was legitimate until the eve of the primary. He rejected the proposal and ordered the new map to be used.

The Missouri Supreme Court then quickly ruled that there were no grounds to reject the referendum proposal and that, with the issue being put to voters in November, the map should be put on hold and the 2022 districts used instead.

The litigation seemed to be over until a new lawsuit was filed on Sept. 4 by Rick Brattin, the Republican nominee in the district held by Cleaver, as well as Rep. Bob Onder, R-Mo., and two voters.

That moved the fight into federal court, where Missouri-based U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark ruled that the new map should be used. That decision ultimately led to the appeals court ruling and Supreme Court intervention.

World.title: Supreme Court allows Trump administration to use expanded database for potential voter purges
World.content:
WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Friday permitted the Trump administration to use an expanded federal database containing citizenship information, as the president encourages states to purge people from voter rolls.

The justices, divided 6-3 on ideological lines with conservatives in the majority, granted an emergency request filed by the government after lower courts ruled that the Trump administration’s changes to the database were likely unlawful.

Critics have said the data is unreliable and could lead to U.S. citizens being kicked off the voter rolls.

But the court noted in its unsigned ruling that the National Voter Registration Act bars the broad purging of voter rolls in the weeks leading up to an election, which “limits the potential impact” of the decision this year. States can still make individualized queries about voters.

On the broader legal questions raised in the case, the court said that federal law requires the government to respond to requests from states for information about citizenship.

The lower court injunction “prevents the federal government from using the program it believes is best suited to the task,” the court said.

In dissent, liberal Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson wrote that the government had not done enough to show that the lower court ruling needed to be blocked.

In her view, “the harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the nonexistent harm that the Government experiences when it is prevented from taking an action that it likely lacks the authority to take,” she added.

Various groups challenging the plan, led by the League of Women Voters, have argued that it violates several laws, including the Social Security Act and the Privacy Act.

The Supreme Court decision “puts millions of Americans at risk for being unlawfully targeted by the administration’s unreliable voter purge database,” the groups said in a statement.

Conservative who have backed the administration’s efforts to tighten voting laws, welcomed the decision.

The ruling “just makes it easier for states to get federal citizenship data to help them clean up voter rolls,” Jason Snead, executive director of the Honest Elections Project, said in a statement.

The Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements program, known as SAVE, was set up by Congress in 1986 so that government agencies could quickly determine someone’s immigration status when they applied for benefits like Social Security.

The Trump administration expanded SAVE after President Donald Trump issued an executive order in March 2025 that required agencies to take steps to better ensure that only U.S. citizens vote in elections.

The government expanded the database by adding information from the Social Security Administration, which enabled searches using Social Security numbers and allowed officials to do bulk searches.

After states started putting their voter rolls through the newly expanded system, some local officials noticed mistakes; many of the flagged registrants were newly naturalized citizens, according to reporting from ProPublica and The Texas Tribune.

Texas was one of the first states to put its full voter rolls — more than 18 million registrations — through the SAVE database last year. Just three people have been charged with voting illegally as a noncitizen.

A federal judge blocked the Trump administration plan, with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit reaching the same conclusion.

In court papers, Solicitor General D. John Sauer said that the district court’s ruling “threatens the integrity of upcoming elections” by preventing the government from responding to state requests to verify the citizenship of potential voters.

Opponents argue the expanded database could force bureaucratic obligations on newly naturalized citizens who are asked to prove their citizenship after being flagged by the system.

Noncitizen voting is extremely rare. All states are required to conduct voter roll list maintenance under federal law, and states already have processes to identify any noncitizens who do accidentally make it onto the voter rolls.

World.title: New Jersey lieutenant governor resigns after release of damaging ethics report
World.content:
New Jersey Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell has resigned from his position following an investigation that found he violated state ethics and harassment policy, Gov. Mikie Sherrill said Friday at a press conference.

“He submitted his resignation to me this afternoon, which I accepted,” Sherrill said. Caldwell was not present at the announcement.

On Thursday, Sherrill urged Caldwell’s resignation after releasing a report summarizing the findings of a probe of his behavior conducted by a law firm hired by the state, which found evidence that he violated ethics rules by committing sexual harassment.

In a statement Thursday, Sherrill said that Caldwell, a fellow Democrat, “engaged in serious, repeated violations of state policy and failed to uphold the responsibilities of his office. I’m calling for his resignation and giving him until tomorrow to do so.”

Caldwell’s resignation, she added, “is necessary and in the best interest of New Jersey residents.”

Dale Caldwell and Mikie Sherrill in Trenton in 2025. Julian Leshay Guadalupe / USA Today Network via Reuters file

Investigators said in the 61-page report that they found credible evidence that Caldwell violated workplace policy “in his conduct by commenting to a female staffer that young women want ‘young sperm.’”

They also found he violated an ethics code and code of conduct “when he brought guests to ticketed events without payment or reimbursement” and “when he sought to obtain a promotion for a state employee with whom he had a romantic relationship.”

Lawyers for Caldwell, who has denied the allegations, said in a statement Thursday night that they “strongly disputed the three findings in the investigation,” as its conclusions “go further than the evidence supports.”

“This unnecessarily protracted and one-sided process lacked the requisite due process that should be afforded every citizen of this state,” said Caldwell’s attorney Thomas Calcagni.

Calcagni didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment Friday.

On Friday, Sherrill pushed back on Calcagni’s criticism of the investigation, saying: “I think it’s very thorough. It lays out exactly what the investigation looked into.” She added that Caldwell’s own statements were included in the report, saying, “So, obviously he was fully involved in this as well.”

Sherrill also defended having Caldwell step in as acting governor on several occasions after the investigation began, saying, “As a former federal prosecutor, it is important to me that everyone have a fair hearing.”

“Once I saw those complaints, once I saw the findings of that investigation, I acted quickly and asked for the resignation of the lieutenant governor,” Sherrill said.

The governor said her demand that Caldwell step down is part of her efforts to dismantle a culture that ignores victims.

“There has been a culture in Trenton, probably since the birth of our nation, to sweep this under the rug,” Sherrill said. “That is not the kind of government I’m running. When I say there is a culture change taking place, I mean it. This is part of it.”

New Jersey state Assembly Speaker Craig Coughlin, a Democrat, applauded Sherrill for her “commitment to hold public officials to the highest standards.”

“Following an independent investigation, Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell was right to resign from office today,” Coughlin said in a statement. “We must ensure the work of governing is uninterrupted and that serving the people of New Jersey remains a top priority.”

Caldwell was also serving as New Jersey’s secretary of state, an office that oversees elections.

Sherrill said Friday that the state’s acting comptroller, Shirley Emehelu, would become acting secretary of state with just weeks to go until the midterm elections.

“Shirley is a veteran of the U.S. Department of Justice and the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office,” Sherrill said. “She has the judgment to run these elections and the strength to stand up to Trump’s attacks on voting.”

The lieutenant governor’s duties also include filling in for the governor when she leaves the state. Sherrill said that until a new lieutenant governor is in place, there is “an order of command” for who would step in for her during any absence, beginning with the state Senate president.

Under New Jersey law, the lieutenant governor must be replaced within 45 days of the position becoming vacant. Sherrill said she would “certainly” make a permanent appointment within that time frame but does not plan on naming an acting lieutenant governor in the meantime.

“We will be making sure with our chief counsel that we’re following the rules,” Sherrill said. “This is a little bit of a new area for New Jersey, so we’re going to ensure that we get legal opinions and follow the process there.”
