World.title: 10 experiencias en el Matarraña para sacarle todo el jugo a la comarca aragonesa en septiembre
World.content:
Pedalear por la vía verde de la Val de Zafán, caminar por el Solo Sculpture Trail, dormir en un antiguo molino de papel y más pistas en esta zona de la provincia de Teruel que es tierra de cañones y, sobre todo, de buitres

Wikipedia dice, todo el mundo repite —incluida la IA—, y será verdad mientras no se demuestre lo contrario, que el río mediterráneo mejor conservado del planeta es el Matarraña. Este afluente del Ebro, de casi 100 kilómetros de longitud, ha dado nombre a la comarca en la que Teruel se funde y confunde con Tarragona y Castellón, y ha labrado las rocas calizas de los Puertos de Beceite, donde nace, como si en vez de agua pura llevara carburo de silicio verde, abrasivo y cortante a más no poder. Aparte de fabulosos cañones y de pozas que piden a gritos bañarse hasta bien entrado el otoño, este rincón del noreste de la provincia de Teruel tiene muchas otras cosas que sorprenden al viajero.

La primera es que aquí no hablan como los demás turolenses, sino chapurriau, una variedad aragonesa del catalán cantarina y cadenciosa que, a los forasteros, salvo que sean de las provincias de al lado, les suena a valenciano. Matarraña —o Matarranya, como lo escriben también— es un no parar de sorpresas. Tomen nota de estas 10.

Más información 24 horas en Ayamonte, la ciudad de Huelva donde vivir uno de los mejores atardeceres de Europa

Penetrar en la comarca siguiendo a un tren loco

Por Matarraña pasó un tren hoy difícil de explicar, que iba de La Puebla de Híjar a Tortosa, del norte de Teruel al Bajo Ebro, y que pretendía llegar algún día hasta la orilla del mar. Un loco sueño ferroviario que duró 30 años (de 1941 a 1971) y que dejó este abrupto y solitario rincón del mapa aragonés lleno de puentes inútiles y de estaciones en mitad de ninguna parte.

Se esfumó el tren, pero su itinerario y su espíritu insensatos permanecen en la vía verde de la Val de Zafán. Una buena manera de hincarle el diente a la comarca es echarse a pedalear desde la que fue la estación de Valjunquera con las bicis y los guías de Senda. Salvo en un par de túneles, que no se ve nada, se va descubriendo un paisaje cada vez más ordenado de olivos y almendros y una luz cada vez más mediterránea. Hay una parada obligada en el alto viaducto que hay a 9,5 kilómetros del inicio, para saludar al río Matarraña. Al otro lado, en otra antigua estación, se halla el muy recomendable hotel La Parada del Compte.

Comer lo que comió Picasso

Pedaleando por una vía verde llana no es que se haga mucho ejercicio, pero hambre sí que se hace. Para calmarla, no hay mejor opción en toda la comarca que Fonda Alcalá. Ubicado en Calaceite, miembro de la Asociación Los Pueblos Más Bonitos de España, por esta casa de comidas algo más que centenaria —data de 1922— han pasado García Márquez, Álvaro Cunqueiro, Francesc Català Roca, Paco de Lucía, Serrat… No en este orden, lógicamente. El que no pasó, pero sí comió lo que aquí se hace, fue Picasso. Les perdius de Picasso, las perdices que le guisaron en esta casa y le llevaron enlatadas a Francia en 1967, y las judías blancas de Beceite con sardinas de cubo son dos platos legendarios, fundamentales. Pero el chef Ignacio Alcalá se inventa todos los días otros más excitantes y divertidos, que es lo que aprendió a hacer en las cocinas de Neichel y Can Roca.

Hacer senderismo en una galería de arte

He aquí sin duda lo más flipante de la comarca, naturaleza aparte: Solo Houses, una hermosa finca campestre de 200 hectáreas en el municipio de Cretas, donde llevan 13 años materializándose como naves alienígenas casas alucinantes de arquitectos de vanguardia que se pueden alquilar desde 850 euros por noche y donde pronto lo hará un hotel de habitaciones circulares exentas, con vistas al bosque diseñado por Smiljan Radić, Premio Pritzker 2026. Obviamente, alojarse aquí es solo para amantes de la arquitectura y gente con pasta.

Una mujer pasea entre esculturas del Solo Sculpture Trail, en la localidad de Cretas. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

El resto debe contentarse con ver los ovnis de lejos, paseando entre las vides de la bodega Venta D’Aubert y las esculturas del Solo Sculpture Trail, un circuito creado por los propietarios de todo esto, los galeristas Christian Bourdais y Eva Albarrán, para exponer al aire libre y vender obras que tampoco parecen de este mundo. Se tarda hora y media en ver las 20 esculturas y solo cuesta cinco euros. También se puede visitar la bodega y catar cinco de sus vinos por 25.

La bodega Venta D’Aubert. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Asomarse a la vecina Tarragona por un desfiladero

Si pasear por un sendero de pago entre esculturas carísimas parece algo pijo y rebuscado, en el pueblo de al lado, en Arnes, podemos hacerlo en un lugar verdaderamente salvaje, el desfiladero de Els Estrets, y bañarnos en las aguas inmaculadas del río que lo atraviesa —un afluente del río Algás, que a su vez lo es del Matarraña—, sin pagar un euro. Al llegar al aparcamiento donde arranca la senda, descubriremos estupefactos Les Gronses, unas formidables moles anaranjadas donde pululan escaladores, cabras monteses y buitres leonados.

El desfiladero de Els Estrets, en la vecina Terra Alta de Tarragona. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Y nada más echarnos a andar, un cartel que dice: “Parc Natural dels Ports”. Estamos en Cataluña, concretamente en la Terra Alta de Tarragona. Otro cartel advierte que el baño solo está permitido en el Toll Blau (el charco azul). Allí veremos dos o tres humanos y, más adelante, si es que se dejan ver, alguna nutria y la libélula Macromia splendens, en peligro de extinción. Mucho más fácil de observar, libando en las lavandas, es la mariposa Cleopatra. El desfiladero se recorre, yendo y volviendo por camino evidente, en un par de horas.

Dormir en un antiguo molino de papel

Vistas desde el hotel La Fábrica de Solfa, en Beceite. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Beceite, además de un bonito pueblo, con muchas de sus casas colgadas sobre el encañonado río Matarraña, es el campo base ideal para explorar la comarca, porque está cerca de su paraje más deseado —el Parrizal, donde nace aquél— y porque hay un hotelito familiar que es un hotelazo. La Fábrica de Solfa, que así se llama, fue un molino de papel: con la fuerza del río se trituraba ropa vieja y se obtenía la pasta necesaria. Ahora es una fábrica de actividades: todas las que se cuentan en este reportaje y algunas más. De amorosos cuidados que prodigan Javier y Alberto Moragrega a los que llegan exhaustos después de hacerlas. Y de ricos platos: el recapte de fesols de Beceite, el ternasco de Aragón, las texturas de té de roca y todo lo que se sirve en el restaurante Marca al Agua. Tampoco se desayuna mal, viendo a las nutrias jugar en el río saltarín. Lo único malo es que aparecen al rayar el sol, así que hay que madrugar.

Darse un baño de multitudes y otro en un ‘fish spa’ natural

A solo tres kilómetros de Beceite se encuentra el Parrizal (o Parrissal), el desfiladero que nadie que visita esta comarca deja de admirar y recorrer, a tal punto que hay que reservar online para evitar mayores aglomeraciones de las que ya se forman sobre las tablas de dos palmos de ancho que hay instaladas en las paredes verticales del cañón, a buena altura sobre las aguas impolutas del recién nacido Matarraña. Avanzar nadando por el propio río, que sería lo deseable para librarse del sudor propio y de los atascos, está prohibido.

Pasarelas en la senda del Parrizal. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

Donde sí está permitido mojarse y remojarse es en La Pesquera, en las pozas que forma el río Ulldemó, afluente del Matarraña, a tres kilómetros también de Beceite. Comparadas con las de otros ríos de montaña, estas aguas de hipnótico color verde jade son hasta cálidas. Y mucho más relajantes: metes los pies y acuden docenas de diminutos barbos y madrillas a limpiar tus células muertas. Esto es ictioterapia y La Pesquera, un fish spa natural, sin kimonos ni musiquillas new age.

Remar con el último sol en el pantano de Pena

Kayak al atardecer en el pantano de Pena. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

A la misma distancia de Beceite que el Parrizal y La Pesquera, está el pantano de Pena, uno de los más antiguos de Teruel (de 1930) y el único de la cuenca del Matarraña. Si hubiera muchos pantanos, no sería el río mediterráneo mejor conservado del mundo. Ir allí a navegar en kayak al atardecer es una de las actividades que recomienda y organiza La Fábrica de Solfa. Desde el hotel se llega con una bici eléctrica en un cuarto de hora y, después de rodear el embalse en media más, se embarca y se rema hasta el centro para admirar cómo el penúltimo sol se duplica en la cabecera y el agua se vuelve de oro. Girando luego el kayak en redondo y apuntando con la proa hacia el noreste, se ve cómo los últimos rayos iluminan la Caixa, una cumbre que a los matarrañeses les parece que tiene forma de caja de caudales y por eso la llaman así. Si remando y girando se vuelca accidentalmente, o adrede para refrescarse, no pasa nada: aquí está permitido el baño.

Asistir al banquete de 500 aves carroñeras

José Ramón Moragrega entre buitres en el Observatorio de Aves Mas de Bunyol. ANDRÉS CAMPOS

En la sierra de Arca, donde está la Caixa, anidan multitud de buitres leonados. No es solo que allí hay cortados rocosos idóneos para ellos. Es que al pie de la montaña, en una masía de Valderrobres, vive José Ramón Moragrega, que lleva más de 30 años alimentándolos. Todos los días, Buitreman —así le llaman— sale a las 9.15 con una carretilla llena de pulmones de cerdo y la vuelca ante una muchedumbre expectante de estas enormes carroñeras. Hasta 500 de ellas se reúnen para compartir de muy malos modos este desayuno, formando una monumental tremolina de polvo, chillidos e iracundos aleteos. Todo puede verse y fotografiarse en el Observatorio de Aves Mas de Bunyol, una masía que es también un formidable hide, con grandes ventanales orientados a los cuatro vientos para no perderse nada, desde el momento en que Buitreman vuelca la carretilla y se aparta a toda velocidad de sus pequeños de picos afilados como cuchillos —por eso va con casco, porque más de una vez ha salido descalabrado—, hasta cuando aparecen los alimoches para disputarse las migajas de la tragantona.

Al despedirse de los visitantes, Moragrega les confía casi entre lágrimas su delicado estado de salud y que sus niños pueden quedarse pronto sin desayuno si alguna entidad pública o privada no asume la gestión del observatorio, que es también alojamiento rural. Es un negocio rentable, asegura.

Vuelta a las rocas huesudas del Masmut

Muchos buitres leonados que desayunan en Mas de Bunyol pasan el resto del día haciendo la digestión en las Rocas del Masmut, en Peñarroya de Tastavins, donde hay una importante colonia de ellos. El PR TE-157, uno de los Senderos Turísticos de Aragón, bien mantenido y señalizado, invita a rodear este manojo de peñas anaranjadas de más de 100 metros de altura, similares a los Mallos de Riglos, cuyo nombre se cree que viene de los masmuda, una tribu bereber que quizá estuviera asentada aquí cuando España era musulmana.

Es una ruta circular de poco más de tres horas, cuatro si el senderista se desvía a los tres kilómetros para subir al mirador del Masmut. Situado a 500 metros de las rocas y a similar altura, es un buen lugar para verlas como las ven los buitres, asomando como las falanges de un gigante muerto y enterrado bajo la costra caliza del Matarraña.

Un pícnic regenerativo para despedirse del Matarraña

La última sorpresa de esta ruta llena de ellas la puede dar Tel·lúric, una masía centenaria del municipio de Ráfels cuyos nuevos propietarios no es que respeten la tradición agrícola de los masos, de estas catedrales civiles del campo matarrañés, es que van un paso más allá. O un paso más acá, porque trabajan la tierra con tal cuidado que no solo no se agota, sino que se regenera. Los olivos, los almendros y las viñas que atiende Sorin Dragoman no son soldados invasores de ejércitos cuadriculados, sino pacíficos hermanos de los pinos, las carrascas, el tomillo, el romero, el té de roca y el poleo.

Con todo lo que aquí se produce (vinos, aceite y almendras con certificación ecológica y de agricultura regenerativa) dispuesto sobre un mantel a cuadros, y también con las carnes a la brasa que salen sin parar de la cocina, se organizan unos pícnics delante de la masía que son una manera estupenda de despedirse del Matarraña. El águila culebrera sobrevuela los cultivos de Tel·lúric sin sospechar que son cosa de humanos.

World.title: New group home for psychiatric patients tried in Rotterdam
World.content:
Rotterdam is to set up a new type of supervised accommodation for homeless people with serious psychiatric problems and addiction issues.

Forty people will be brought together under one roof in Poortugaal, a village near Rotterdam that is also home to a forensic psychiatric clinic, in a supervised environment where they can receive more structured support.

The residents will be allowed to stay in the facility for up to eight years, receiving long-term and structured support that is often lacking in temporary accommodation.

Around 1,500 people in the Netherlands are classed as posing a high risk to public safety. They often have learning difficulties, suffer from psychiatric illness and struggle with addiction, which can lead to aggressive, disruptive or deranged behaviour in public.

Many of the patients have spent their lives alternating between living on the streets and being incarcerated in clinics or prisons, posing a danger to themselves and others.

Pillar to post

“They get passed from pillar to post when what they really need is intensive support for several years,” Laura van Goor, of Artes, the organisation running the facility, told Nieuwsuur. “But we don’t have that right now in the Netherlands.”

Psychiatric clinics are intended for short stays of around three months, but patients often end up staying longer to prevent them ending up back on the streets.

But the treatment is short-term and keeping patients in care for longer adds to waiting lists.

Van Goor said the patients would have more freedom to move around on the campus than in smaller-scale facilities, while also benefiting from a more structured regime. They will not be allowed out unsupervised.

Drink and drugs will be formally banned, unlike in temporary housing where usage is usually tolerated. “But it’s not a case of ‘if you use, you’re out,’ Van Good said. “That’s not possible: 95% of them have drug problems.”

World.content:

Almost half of Dutch people say that have experience social nuisance in their neighborhood, from noisy neighbors to the drug trade, according to new figures from the Dutch statistics office.

The CBS released its biennial Safety Monitor on Friday, which found that 42% of adults say they dealt with some type of anti-social behaviour near their homes during 2025.

The report looks at crime and safety issues across the country.

The largest number of complaints stem from loitering youth, which make up 26% of the reported problems. Issues with neighbors account for 20% of the concerns.

Overall problems with nuisance have risen in the past few years. Some 14% of people say they have experienced significant social nuisance in their neighborhood, up from 12% in 2021.

Those living in urban areas have the most problems. City residents report nearly four times the number of issues than non-urban dwellers.

World.title: Cabinet wants private companies to pay more towards gas storage
World.content:
The Dutch government wants to make private companies responsible for storing gas for the winter to cut its liabilities as prices on the markets soar.

At the moment the cost of filling the four gas storage facilities in Norg, Grijpskerk, Bergermeer and Alkmaar is met by the government-funded operator Energie Beheer Nederland, but soaring gas prices mean they are facing a €1 billion loss.

Private companies have no commercial incentive to stock up on gas for the winter because prices are currently forecast to drop after the autumn.

Demand has been stoked by the need for European governments to meet EU-set targets to fill their gas reserves by the start of November. The Netherlands last week reduced its target figure from 74% to 64%. The current storage level is 57.5%.

Under EU rules the Dutch government is also not allowed to keep the stored gas it buys for itself, but must export it to other member states who need it, as well as the UK, which has limited gas storage facilities.

The Netherlands’ facilities date from the time when it exported gas from the Slochteren field in Groningen, but since it was forced to end production two years ago because of earthquakes in the northern province it has filled the chambers with imported gas.

LNG imports

The high cost of importing liquefied national gas from the United States, which is the main supplier, have added to the government’s costs.

It wants to pass on the cost to commercial companies such as Essent, Eneco and Vattenfall by making it mandatory for them to build up their own reserves. A similar obligation is in force in Austria.

“At the moment there is virtually no market in the Netherlands for storing gas in the seasonal storage facilities, even though seasonal storage is an essential element of supply guarantee in the portfolio of suppliers’ prospectuses,” the letter, sent from the ministry of economic affairs, said.

“The question is whether the bill should continue to be met by the Dutch taxpayer, or whether supply guarantee can be be ensured through a different mix of measures for a lower cost.”

World.title: Xavi satisfied as Gakpo earns Oranje late draw against Germany
World.content:
New Dutch national football coach Xavi Hernandez declared himself satisfied with his team’s performance following the 1-1 draw with Germany in Amsterdam.

Cody Gakpo converted a magnificent skewered pass by debutant Ruben van Bommel with a crashing volley in stoppage time to earn Oranje the point their second-half dominance deserved.

“We were a little nervous in the first half, but the second half is the way we want to play,” the Spaniard said after the opening game in the Nations League, his first match since being appointed last month.

Germany took the lead in the 32nd minute when Felix Nmecha pounced on a loose ball in the penalty, but the Dutch were aggrieved that their opponents had played on after Brian Brobbey went down injured in the centre circle.

Captain Virgil van Dijk said: “We thought the ball should have gone out, but it didn’t go out, and it was unfortunate that it fell right in front of them after a good block by Jan Paul van Hecke.”

Van Dijk had the ball in the net after 15 minutes, but his header was disallowed after the referee decided Brobbey had impeded goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen.

Zierkzee recall

Brobbey was replaced by AZ striker Mexx Meerdink, who missed a glorious chance to equalise on his debut after Crysencio Summerville made space in the penalty area with a smart turn.

On Friday Xavi called up Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee, who last played for the national team two years ago, as a replacement for Brobbey ahead of the next Nations League match against Serbia in Belgrade on Sunday.

Van Bommel, who became the third generation of his family to play for Oranje after and his father, Mark, his grandfather, Bert van Marwijk, came on in the second half and capped his debut with the assist that set up Gakpo’s goal.

“I ran forward and I saw Cody free at the far post, and I thought, I have to get it to him somehow. It wasn’t an easy finish, but the pass wasn’t bad either,” the PSV winger said.

Another second-half substitute was Borussia Dortmund midfielder Joey Veerman, who made his first appearance in an orange shirt for two years after being frozen out of the international set-up by Xavi’s predecessor Ronald Koeman. Veerman came on for Marseille’s Quinten Timber, who was selected to take the place of the injured Frenkie de Jong.

World.title: Dutch PM Jetten warns “hands off the ICC” in debut UN speech
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten gave a fiery address to the United Nations on Thursday, defending the International Criminal Court and the rule of law.

“Hands off the ICC and all those other institutions that protect the international legal order,” he said in his first address at the UN’s annual meeting in New York.

Although Jetten did not call out American president Donald Trump specifically, the speech came after reporting earlier this week that the United States is planning to escalate its fight with the ICC and sanction the institution as a whole as part of its campaign to dismantle the court “brick by brick”.

The White House has already sanctioned 13 staff members, including court president, Japanese Judge Tomoko Akane, over the investigation into alleged Israeli war crimes in Gaza.

“Take, for example, the attempts to undermine the International Criminal Court – a court based in my country, in my city. This undermines the international legal order as a whole. And that affects us all,” Jetten said.

As the court’s host state, the Netherlands is obliged to provide assistance such as cooperation with security, facilitating visas and transporting defendants and witnesses.

He also called for Russia to be held accountable for the war in Ukraine. “In this conflict, Ukraine has no choice but to defend itself,” said Jetten. “But Russia chooses to wage war day after day,” he said.

World.title: Van Weel survives no-confidence debate over crime stats row
World.content:
Justice minister David van Weel has survived a motion of no confidence after he apologised to MPs who accused him of misleading them over police crime figures.

MPs called an emergency debate on Thursday over the minister’s response to reports that police had not responded to some 10,000 criminal complaints because they lacked the capacity to do so.

Van Weel told parliament in June that more than half the cases were reports of crimes rather than official complaints, which police are required to investigate.

But he was corrected by the government’s audit office, the Algemene Rekenkamer, which said in its annual report to parliament that only 10% of the cited cases were verbal reports.

“The consequence is that victims of crimes such as sexual offences and serious theft had not had justice and these serious cases have not had any significant attention,” the auditors wrote.

Van Weel initially tried to shrug off the reprimand as a “difference of insight”, but after MPs called a debate and tabled a motion of no confidence he attempted to apologise for his choice of words.

Measures of crime

The minister blamed the confusion on the different criteria used to measure the seriousness of the complaint. Police prioritise crimes based on how much evidence is available to start an investigation, such as witness statements and camera footage, while auditors use the “Crime Harm Index”, which looks at the severity of sentences imposed by courts.

Van Weel acknowledged that he had “given the impression” that he “had trivialised the seriousness of the Court of Audit’s report”, but insisted: “That doesn’t make it wrong information.

Opposition MPs said the minister’s explanation did not go far enough and threatened to back a motion of no confidence tabled by the far-right PVV, which would have forced Van Weel to resign.

Different attitude

“The minister has had several chances to say he gave parliament the wrong impression, but hasn’t taken them,” said Caroline van der Plas of the farmers’ party BBB.

Van Weel made a second, stronger apology that stopped short of admitting he had misled MPs, which was enough to persuade all parties not to vote for the motion, with the exception of the PVV and Forum voor Democratie.

“I realise now, after your contributions, that I intentionally or unintentionally gave you the wrong impression and that you felt misled,” he said. “That was never my intention, but it shouldn’t have happened.”

“At the last minute we saw a different attitude,” Ingrid Coenradie of right-wing opposition party JA21 commented. “We would have liked to have seen that at the start.”

World.title: Poland extends tax rights to same-sex couples with foreign marriages
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The Polish government has granted same-sex couples who married abroad and have had their wedding certificates transcribed into the Polish registry the same tax rights as other married couples. The decision follows a ruling by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) requiring Poland – whose domestic law does not allow same-sex couples to form any type of legal union – to recognise same-sex marriages contracted in other EU member states. Podpisałem dziś interpretację ogólną, która zapewnia, że osoby, które uzyskały transkrypcję aktu małżeństwa będą miały w polskich urzędach skarbowych takie same prawa i obowiązki podatkowe jak wszyscy małżonkowie. — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) September 24, 2026 “Today, I signed a general interpretation ensuring that persons who have obtained a transcription of their marriage certificate will have the same tax rights and obligations in Polish tax offices as all other married couples,” announced finance minister Andrzej Domański in a social media post. A general interpretation is an official position taken by the finance ministry aiming to clarify the application of tax law in a specific area. Among the benefits that couples with a transcribed foreign marriage certificate can now receive include preferential treatment under inheritance and gift tax rules and the ability to file joint personal income tax returns. Couples may also pay tax on behalf of a spouse and refuse to testify as a witness in proceedings involving their spouse. “This is about basic equality, justice and fairness,” Domański told broadcaster TVN. “We want these rights to be enforceable in an effective way.” The finance minister said that the decision would have a “negligible” impact on the state budget. He also noted that such couples would be subject to the obligations that apply to other married couples in Poland, which include liability for their spouse’s tax obligations. Osoby, które uzyskały tak zwaną transkrypcję aktu małżeństwa, będą miały przed polskimi urzędami skarbowymi dokładnie takie same prawa i obowiązki jak pozostali małżonkowie – powiedział minister finansów Andrzej Domański w rozmowie z Grzegorzem Kajdanowiczem w @faktypofaktach w… pic.twitter.com/uVwDaD3ZDk — tvn24 (@tvn24) September 24, 2026 The finance minister’s decision has drawn criticism from right-wing politicians, who argue that recognition of same-sex marriage violates the constitution, which states that “marriage, being a union of a man and a woman, shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland”. Paweł Szefernaker, chief of staff to President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, said Domański’s actions were “inconsistent with the constitution” and had been carried out “without legislation, without debate, without honestly telling Poles what is really happening”. “Everyone has the right to a private life,” he added. “However, the state has a duty to protect the legal order and provide tax support for marriage.” Patryk Jaki, a deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s largest opposition party, said that the finance minister’s actions “clearly violate Polish law and will have legal implications in the future” for Domański, who is “writing additional points in the indictment against himself”. Sławomir Mentzen, one of the leaders of the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) group, said the tax interpretation “will be revoked on the very first day” if his party comes to power. To jest niezgodna z Konstytucją próba faktycznego zrównania małżeństwa ze związkami jednopłciowymi. Bez zmiany Konstytucji, bez ustawy, bez debaty, bez uczciwego powiedzenia Polakom, co naprawdę się dzieje. Każdy ma prawo do prywatnego życia według własnych wyborów. Ale państwo… https://t.co/0CQ9Lnfl02 — Paweł Szefernaker 🇵🇱 (@szefernaker) September 24, 2026 The changes follow a ruling issued by the CJEU in November 2025 ordering Poland to recognise same-sex marriages contracted in other EU states. The court found that failing to do so infringes the freedom to move and reside within the EU as well as the right to respect for private and family life. In light of that ruling, in March this year, Poland’s own Supreme Administrative Court (NSA) ordered Warsaw’s registry office to recognise a marriage conducted by two Polish men in Germany by transcribing it into the Polish civil registry. In May, the Polish government issued a regulation allowing such transcriptions of foreign same-sex marriages to take place nationwide. It went into force in August. However, even before then, some cities had begun transcribing marriage certificates, beginning with Warsaw and Wrocław in May. At the end of August, digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski reported that 84 same-sex couples had already transcribed their foreign marriages under the government’s new regulation. Poland has begun paying benefits to same-sex couples who married abroad then entered their marriage into the Polish registry. The EU court ordered Poland to recognise such marriages, even though domestic law does not allow for any form of same-sex union https://t.co/svnRjyBO8Q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 22, 2026 While foreign same-sex marriages can now be entered into Poland’s civil registry, questions have remained as to what that will mean in practice for such couples, especially as domestic law does not recognise same-sex relationships. In another development, labour minister Agnieszka Dziemianowicz-Bąk announced last week that the Social Insurance Institution (ZUS) has begun paying care allowances to qualifying same-sex couples who married abroad and have had their wedding certificates transcribed into the Polish registry. World.title: Prosecutors drop case in which Wałęsa was accused of lying about being communist collaborator
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prosecutors have ended a decade-long case in which former president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa was accused of falsely claiming not to have authored documents relating to his alleged cooperation with the communist authorities. Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that helped bring down the communist regime in the 1980s, has always denied longstanding claims that, in the 1970s, he acted as an informant to the communist security services. The case has become highly politicised, with right-wing figures – especially from the Law and Justice (PiS) party that ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 – critical of Wałęsa. By contrast, the former president, who turns 83 next week, enjoys good relations with the current ruling coalition of Prime Minister Donald Tusk. Waldemar Żurek, Tusk’s justice minister and prosecutor general, welcomed the decision to drop the case against Wałęsa, saying that, under PiS, “a politicised state apparatus hounded the legend of Solidarity, deliberately ignoring facts and basic logic”. Now, “truth has triumphed over an attempt to rewrite history”. Prokuratura ostatecznie umorzyła śledztwo przeciwko Lechowi Wałęsie. Przez lata upolityczniony aparat państwa ścigał legendę „Solidarności”, celowo ignorując fakty i elementarną logikę. Zignorowano bezsporny fakt historyczny – SB masowo fałszowała dokumenty i podpisy Wałęsy w… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) September 24, 2026 The case in question stems from statements made by Wałęsa in 2016 during an investigation by the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body that also has prosecutorial powers. Those proceedings, in which the former Polish president testified as a witness, were launched after documents apparently carrying his signature were found in the home archives of former communist interior minister Czesław Kiszczak. The files indicated that Wałęsa, working under the code name TW Bolek, signed a commitment to collaborate with the communist Security Service (SB). They also included payslips and informant’s notes. The former president had told the media at the time when the documents were discovered that they had been forged. When speaking to IPN investigators, he also denied having drafted or signed all but one of the documents. However, prosecutors subsequently claimed that – after comparing the documents from Kiszczak’s file with others they said had been written and signed by Wałęsa, as well as consulting forensic handwriting experts – Wałęsa’s testimony was false in the case of over 50 of the documents. In 2021, the former president was charged with giving false testimony. Then, in 2023, he was indicted, meaning the case was sent to court. However, in 2024, after Tusk’s government had taken power from PiS, prosecutors asked that the case be returned to them by the court, which agreed to the request. Now, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw has announced that it is discontinuing the case entirely, after finding that there are no grounds for Wałęsa to be prosecuted. Lech Wałęsa will face trial accused of falsely testifying not to have signed documents of cooperation with the communist authorities. If convicted, he can be jailed for up to 3 years. He calls the claims against him "terrible insults and monstrous lies" https://t.co/X0eb4e5ahm — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 30, 2023 In a statement explaining the decision, prosecutors claimed that there had been significant “methodological errors” made previously in attributing handwritten texts to Wałęsa and in handwriting comparisons between them. “There was no evidence to assume with 100% certainty that the comparative material actually came from Lech Wałęsa,” they wrote. In fact, “the evidence collected clearly indicated that Lech Wałęsa did not write long manuscripts during his life, and especially not in the 1970s”. “Some witnesses explicitly stated that, at that time, he was a secondary illiterate,” meaning someone who has lost their ability to read and write, said the prosecutors. “He was not able to write and could barely read.” This, along with other concerns over how the case was previously conducted, “led to the conclusion that there was no certain basis to assume that Lech Wałęsa was the author of the documents disclosed in the ‘Kiszczak files’, and therefore there was no evidence that he lied during the interrogation”. Hit! Ekipa Tuska ogłosiła Wałęsę analfabetą by wybronić go przed Bolkiem! To się nie dzieje! To niemożliwe! pic.twitter.com/PQnOn5XDb0 — Sławomir Cenckiewicz (@Cenckiewicz) September 24, 2026 Prosecutors also said that “the testimony of numerous witnesses proves that the files of TW Bolek, discovered in the possession of General Kiszczak’s widow, were most likely fabricated. Finally, they argued that, even if Wałęsa had given false testimony, he was protected by the constitutional right against self-incrimination while being interviewed as a witness. “The prosecution found that Lech Wałęsa could have feared that if he admitted to having prepared or signed the documents from the ‘Kiszczak files’…all his testimonies in which he denied being secret collaborator “Bolek” in previous proceedings…would be deemed false and would lead to his being held criminally liable.” Lech Wałęsa, Angela Merkel and Volodymyr Zelensky have been named the first distinguished members of the European Order of Merit. The award was created by the European Parliament to "honour those who did not simply believe in Europe, but helped build it" https://t.co/inosiiRQkW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 11, 2026 In response to the announcement, Wałęsa shared on his Facebook page the post by Żurek praising the prosecutors’ decision. Wałęsa then added a comment claiming that Jarosław and Lech Kaczyński, the founders of PiS, had ordered a right-wing historian, Sławomir Cenckiewicz, to fake the Kiszczak files. Cenckiewicz has written extensively about Wałęsa, including about his alleged collaboration with the communist security services. He also recently served as national security advisor to current Polish President Karol Nawrocki, who was elected last year with the support of PiS. In a series of social media posts on Thursday, Cenkiewicz said that he had “never read a bigger lie” than the prosecutors’ statement justifying dropping the case. He also ridiculed the idea that Wałęsa could have led the Solidarity movement in the 1980s and served as president in the 1990s if he was a “secondary illiterate”. Większego kłamstwa przebranego w wymiar sprawiedliwości RP nigdy nie czytałem! To większe kłamstwo niż skandaliczny wyrok Kapińskiego i spółki z 2000 r.! Reżim Tuska uznał, że Wałęsa nie był Bolkiem, a Instytut Sehna niczego kategorycznie nie ustalił! I powtórzyli brednie… — Sławomir Cenckiewicz (@Cenckiewicz) September 24, 2026 The accusations of communist collaboration have tarnished Wałęsa’s reputation among some Poles. In 2017, shortly after the Kiszczak files were uncovered, a poll by IBRiS for the Rzeczpospolita daily found that 28% believed Wałęsa was not a national hero. However, 62% said that he was. Earlier this year, Wałęsa was named as one of the first three distinguished members of the European Order of Merit, a new initiative launched by the European Parliament, alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and former German Chancellor Angela Merkel. World.title: Poland issues guidance on responding to air attacks and warns of Russia threat
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The Polish government has launched an information campaign on how to respond in the event of an air strike. It has also announced that 85,000 shelters are to be marked with clear signs across Poland and an evacuation plan is being developed. The moves come amid growing concerns over Russia strikes in Ukraine near the Polish border. The prime minister and foreign minister have warned that Russia could be planning “something big” this year, without specifying what that might involve. 🟡 KOMUNIKAT | MSWiA publikuje instrukcję reagowania podczas zagrożenia atakiem z powietrza. 📄 Ministerstwo Spraw Wewnętrznych i Administracji udostępnia nową instrukcję postępowania na wypadek ataku z powietrza. To rozwinięcie treści zawartych w „Poradniku Bezpieczeństwa”,… pic.twitter.com/aw3h07mdeF — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) September 25, 2026 On Friday, Poland’s interior ministry published information on how to respond to the threat of an air attack, expanding on a safety handbook sent to all 17 million households in the country earlier this year. The new guidelines explain where to seek cover during an air raid, how to prepare homes and what to do if an attack occurs while people are at home, at work, outdoors or in a car. They advise people to seek a shelter point, take a prepared evacuation backpack and any necessary medication, and use only stairs. If reaching a shelter would require spending a long time outdoors, people are advised to remain inside and move to a central room without windows. Separately, the ministry has prepared guidelines for schools after some were criticised last week for evacuating children outside school buildings during alarms in the eastern province of Lublin. W całej Polsce mają pojawić się obowiązkowe oznaczenia Punktów Schronienia. Specjalna aplikacja pokaże ich lokalizacje, a nowe oznakowanie ma ułatwić mieszkańcom znalezienie bezpiecznego miejsca w sytuacji zagrożenia. Materiał 🎥 Michał Niewodowski pic.twitter.com/HVoo3ypETT — 19.30 TVP (@1930_tvp) September 21, 2026 To make shelter points easier to identify, the interior ministry has prepared a draft regulation requiring local authorities and managers of designated sites to mark them clearly by the end of the year with a blue triangle on an orange background, as well as a green sign saying “Punkt schronienia” (“Shelter point”). The locations can also be found using a mobile application launched last year. According to the ministry’s own data, Poland currently has about 85,000 shelter points, which could host 23.7 million people, or 64% of the country’s population. A national plan is also being developed to coordinate potential evacuation as a result of war, a threat of war or a natural disaster. The plan is intended to establish evacuation routes and reception areas in advance, including how many people may need to be moved and where they could be accommodated. “When a threat arises, we warn the Polish people and defend our security. It is only natural that we prepare for worst-case scenarios, while deeply believing that they will never come to pass,” interior minister Marcin Kierwiński told the Rzeczpospolita newspaper. “Evacuation plans are being prepared…These plans rely heavily on the strength of the entire crisis response system. The more we strengthen that system, the more precise the plans will be,” Kierwiński added. Poland has launched a mobile application and website that allows people to find their nearest shelter in times of war or other emergencies https://t.co/YE3rsltCj5 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 22, 2025 The evacuation plans have become the subject of false claims circulating on social media. These posts allege that the government is preparing to forcibly displace Poles and ultimately eliminate the Polish nation, with some linking the alleged plan to an agreement between Berlin and Kyiv, reports the Onet news service. They claim that evacuees would never be allowed to return, allegations the government quickly moved to debunk. 📢 STOP FAKE NEWS! W sieci krążą fałszywe informacje, jakoby przygotowywany Krajowy Plan Ewakuacji miał oznaczać masowe wysiedlenie mieszkańców Polski ‼️To nieprawda‼️ 🔎 FAKT: Krajowy Plan Ewakuacji określa procedury na wypadek wojny, zagrożenia wojną lub klęski żywiołowej.… pic.twitter.com/YNEqXF3StJ — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) September 18, 2026 The measures are part of a broader effort to strengthen Poland’s civil protection system. Last week, Kierwiński said Poland plans to triple the current number of warning sirens in Lublin province to more than 1,000 by the end of 2026. This follows a series of Russian attacks in western Ukraine, including a drone strike on a passenger train travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw about 2 km from the Polish border. The recent escalation comes after several incidents in recent years involving violations of Polish airspace, including the entry of around 20 Russian drones on one night last year, as well as the explosion of a Russian missile in a field in eastern Poland earlier this year. Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned last week that Russia’s further plans could include attacks designed to test NATO’s response. Those warnings were echoed yesterday by Poland’s foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, who said that multiple sources suggested that “Russia is planning something big this year.” “I think Putin needs a pretext for mobilisation, so they might carry out a false-flag attack to tell the Russians, ‘We are under attack, and that is why we must mobilise,’” he added. World.title: Zelensky condemns knife attack by Ukrainian at Polish abbey that left priest dead and others injured
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has expressed his horror at an “evil” knife attack carried out today by a Ukrainian man at a Catholic abbey in Poland, which left one priest dead and others seriously injured. The incident has caused shock in Poland, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk pledging that the perpetrator, who is in police custody, will face the “full severity of Polish law”. W Opactwie Sióstr Benedyktynek w Jarosławiu obywatel Ukrainy dopuścił się straszliwej zbrodni. Jesteśmy wstrząśnięci tym złem. Według dotychczasowych informacji zginął ksiądz katolicki, a kilka innych osób zostało rannych. Składamy najgłębsze kondolencje rodzinie i bliskim… — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) September 24, 2026 The attack took place on Thursday morning on the grounds of a Benedictine abbey in the town of Jarosław in southeast Poland. Local police reported that a 31-year-old Ukrainian man had stabbed four male victims and one female. Three were members of the clergy and two laypeople. Authorities later confirmed that one of the men, a priest, had died of his injuries in hospital and that two others were in serious condition. The cathedral in the nearby city of Rzeszów named the deceased as Stanisław Zbojnowicz. The superior of the Benedictine Sisters Monastery, Barbara Dendor, told news website Interia that Zbojnowicz had been in a confessional when the attack began. He had rushed out to attempt to close the gates and protect other people, but was stabbed by the assailant before he could do so. In its initial social media post announcing Zbojnowicz’s death, the cathedral also said that a second priest, Marek Pieńkowski, had died. However, a few minutes later it deleted that claim, blaming the “enormous information chaos surrounding today’s tragic event”. One person was killed and four were injured in a knife attack at a Catholic convent in Poland this morning, with clergy among the victims. Police have detained a 31-year-old Ukrainian man on suspicion of carrying out the attack. The motive remains unknown https://t.co/93nbqpwnIA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 24, 2026 On Thursday afternoon, prosecutors revealed that the suspect, who has not been named, had entered Poland from Germany in the early hours of Thursday and “was heading to the border crossing [with Ukraine] in Korczowa”, which is around 30km (18.6 miles) from Jarosław. However, he ultimately did not cross the border and, for unknown reasons, ended up in Jarosław, where he entered the grounds of the abbey and began his attack, using a knife taken from the kitchen. Prosecutors said that doctors would assess the suspect’s condition before he was interrogated. Blood samples were also taken to be tested for the presence of narcotics and alcohol. The motive for the attack remains unknown. Dendor told news website Wirtualna Polska that the perpetrator was unknown to them. “He looked like a madman, in shorts and a T-shirt, even though it was cold today,” she said. Wirtualna Polska reports, based on the accounts of unnamed witnesses, that the Ukrainian man had earlier in the day knocked on the gates of the abbey and asked for financial assistance. However, he was turned away due to the suspicion that he was drunk or under the influence of drugs and was asked to come back later. That is standard practice for places that offer aid, reports the news service. The man “flew into a rage when he didn’t get help and allegedly threatened priests”, said one of the unnamed sources. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk expressed his sympathy for the loved ones of the victims of the attack and pledged that the perpetrator “will be punished with the full severity of Polish law”. President Karol Nawrocki likewise expressed his condolences and called on the authorities to “quickly and thoroughly clarify all the circumstances of this tragedy”. Later on Thursday afternoon, Zelensky also extended his condolences in a social media post published in Polish. “We are shocked by this evil,” he wrote. “The perpetrator of this evil must bear full responsibility in accordance with the applicable law.” Morderca z Jarosławia jest w rękach Polskiej Policji. Trwają czynności. Sprawca to obywatel Ukrainy. Będzie ukarany z całą surowością polskiego prawa. Łączę się w bólu z bliskimi ofiar tego brutalnego ataku. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) September 24, 2026 Earlier, the Ukrainian embassy in Warsaw had “condemned the brutal attack” in Jarosław. However, it also appealed for people “not to allow pain to turn into hatred or further violence”, saying that “accountability for the crime must be based solely on the law”. Polish-Ukrainian relations have been tense in recent months, amid rising anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland and anger at Zelensky’s decision to name a military unit after a group that led massacres of Poles during World War Two. There has been a rise in reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland this year. Marcin Piotrowski, a board member of the Folkowisko Foundation, which provides aid to Ukrainian refugees, told newspaper Rzeczpospolita today that the tragedy in Jarosław was already being exploited on social media. He expressed fear that “we are almost on the verge of lynchings”. 🔴Jesteśmy na granicy nastrojów linczowych. Obawiam się, że czyn pojedynczej osoby odbije się echem na milionach Ukraińców – mówi Marcin Piotrowski, socjolog i członek Rady Fundacji Humanitarnej Folkowisko, działającej na pograniczu polsko-ukraińskim.https://t.co/p048Fgg1Ct — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) September 24, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish constitutional court officials charged with preventing entry of new judges
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The crisis around Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has deepened further, after prosecutors charged two senior TK officials over their role in preventing new judges from taking up their positions on the court. Those judges were chosen by the government’s majority in parliament but rejected by President Karol Nawrocki and the TK’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, both of whom are aligned with the right-wing opposition. Following news of the charges, Święczkowski announced that he has initiated proceedings of his own against three other new judges who were admitted to the court this year after being chosen by the ruling coalition. That could result in them being expelled from their positions. Zarzuty w śledztwie dotyczącym niedopuszczenia sędziów Trybunału Konstytucyjnego do orzekania: ⬇️https://t.co/MPiKCEqGBs — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) September 23, 2026 After coming to power in December 2023, the government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk refused to recognise the TK, which was stacked with judges appointed by the former Law and Justice administration. It argued that, because some of those judges were unlawfully appointed, the TK itself was illegitimate. Earlier this year, Tusk’s majority in parliament finally began the process of appointing new judges to the TK to fill the growing number of vacancies. Normally, 15 judges sit on the tribunal, but many seats were empty after incumbents’ nine-year terms had expired and the government had previously refused to fill them. However, under Polish law, new TK judges must take an oath “before the president” in order to take up their position. Nawrocki, who was elected last year with the support of PiS, has refused to swear in four of the six judges chosen by parliament in March. Nawrocki argues that there were legal doubts surrounding their election. The government rejects this, as do the judges themselves, who organised their own swearing-in ceremony before a notary and then submitted the documents to the presidential chancellery. Afterwards, the four judges attempted to take up their positions at the TK. However, Święczkowski, who served in the PiS government before becoming a TK judge, refused to admit them, arguing that they had not taken the necessary oath before the president. The judges took their case to the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR), which in May issued an interim order requiring that they be allowed to take up their positions. But Święczkowski has refused to comply, arguing that the ECHR does not have the competence to make such a decision. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 While Święczkowski himself is protected from prosecution by legal immunity, two senior TK officials have now been charged over their role in refusing entry to the four judges. One of the two suspects, who can be named only as Zofia H. under Polish privacy law, is the director of the TK’s chancellery; the other, Piotr P., is the commander of the TK’s security service. They have been charged with abuse of power by a public official, which is punishable by up to three years in prison, and “maliciously and persistently” violating the employment rights of the judges, an offence that carries a sentence of up to two years. Prosecutors say that the officials’ actions were “to the detriment of the private interests of judges of the Constitutional Tribunal and the public interest in the proper functioning of the judiciary in Poland”. Both of the accused have been questioned and pleaded not guilty. The crisis around Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has deepened further after the tribunal ruled that the president is not obliged to swear in new TK judges appointed by parliament. President Nawrocki last month refused to swear in four new judges https://t.co/ycnweW9pSR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 13, 2026 The decision to bring charges was welcomed by Waldemar Żurek, who serves as justice minister in Tusk’s government as well as prosecutor general. “In a building that should stand guard over the constitution, unlawful blockades were organised, humiliating inspections were conducted, and malicious bullying was directed at legally elected judges,” he wrote on social media. “A state official has no right to place themselves above the law, and the gates of the tribunal are not the gates of a private fortress,” he continued. “Anyone who carries out unlawful political orders and destroys the foundations of the rule of law must reckon with criminal liability.” W budynku, który powinien stać na straży Konstytucji, urządzono bezprawne blokady, upokarzające kontrole i złośliwy mobbing wobec legalnie wybranych sędziów. Urzędnik państwowy nie ma prawa stawiać się ponad prawem, a bramy Trybunału nie są bramami prywatnej twierdzy.… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) September 23, 2026 The TK itself, however, condemned prosecutors’ actions, calling them “unlawful” and a “tool of personal pressure and a form of intimidation”. “The director of the chancellery and all other employees of the TK have performed and continue to perform their duties and official orders in accordance with the applicable law,” wrote the tribunal on its official X account. It argued that it would, in fact, have been a criminal abuse of power to have “allowed persons who have not taken the oath before the President to assume the office of a TK judge”. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! A fire last night at a ground station in Poland used by Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite internet company, was caused deliberately, says digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski. The facility is used to provide internet services across the region, including in Ukraine, which relies heavily on Starlink connections. Although the fire is still being investigated, “the modus operandi in this case is clearly Russian”, says Gawkowski. 🔴 Gawkowski o pożarze stacji Starlink. "Element wojny hybrydowej" Wicepremier Krzysztof Gawkowski ocenił pożar stacji Starlink na Mazowszu jako celową próbę zakłócenia łączności. – Wiele wskazuje na to, że pożar stacji Starlinków na Mazowszu to kolejny element wojny hybrydowej… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) September 24, 2026 Firefighters were called out at around 9 p.m. on Wednesday to the facility, which is located in the village of Wola Krobowska, just south of the capital Warsaw. Due to suspicions that the fire had been caused deliberately, police and officers from the Internal Security Agency (ABW) were also later dispatched to the scene. “We’re dealing with an arson attack that was intended to impact critical telecommunications infrastructure that influences internet operation,” Gawkowski, who also serves as deputy prime minister, told broadcaster TVN on Thursday morning. In a separate interview with TVP, the minister said that the facility is owned by Polish state telecommunications operator Exatel and “provides internet transmission through Poland, and also to Ukraine”. He noted that other internet providers use Exatel’s facility, including Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which is the owner of Starlink. Starlink terminals have been vital in Ukraine during Russia’s war against the country. Gawkowski told TVN that “the modus operandi in this case is clearly Russian” and “is another element of the hybrid warfare we are facing”. Poland has been one of the primary targets for Russian sabotage operations in Europe, including a series of arson attacks. “The Russians want to paralyse critical infrastructure, cut off water, gas and electricity, paralyse the internet,” said the minister. “All these processes have one goal: to incite panic and stir up emotions.” However, in his remarks to TVP, Gawkowski acknowledged that, for now, “it is impossible to say” for sure whether Russia was behind the attack. Poland is the "primary focus" of Russia's sabotage campaign in Europe, finds a new report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism. Among 151 incidents identified since 2022, 31 of them took place in Poland – more than in any other country https://t.co/QXfSI00FD6 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 3, 2026 The spokesman for Poland’s security services, Jacek Dobrzyński, likewise told TVN that “at this stage it is still too early to talk about the causes or motives of this fire”. However, he confirmed that “everything points to arson”. Justice minister Waldemar Żurek also told broadcaster RMF that “this could be an act of sabotage, and we are taking that into account, so nothing can be ruled out here, especially since these are sensitive elements that ensure satellite communications”. Polish news service Defence24 notes that ground stations are used by Starlink to connect its satellite constellation with terrestrial communications infrastructure. The facility in Poland, alongside one in Lithuania, serves the entire Central and Eastern Europe region, including Ukraine. Tu nieco więcej o roli stacji naziemnych w systemie Starlink. https://t.co/EYys481dSi — Mariusz Marszałkowski (@MJMarszalkowski) September 24, 2026 Earlier this month, a fire broke out at a drone plant in Poland belonging to WB Electronics, which supplies the armed forces of Ukraine and Poland, among others. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that there was “no doubt” the fire was caused deliberately, and that Russia was likely behind it. The Polish government has in recent months warned that Russia is planning to escalate its hybrid actions against Poland and other countries in the region, including through acts of sabotage, disinformation, and potential airspace and border violations. In July, a Russian missile entered Polish airspace before landing in a field in eastern Poland. On Wednesday this week, the same day as the fire in Wola Krobowska broke out, a Russian helicopter briefly entered Polish airspace. World.title: Poland and Belarus seek thaw in relations as foreign ministers meet for first time in a decade
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The foreign ministers of Poland and Belarus have met for the first time in a decade, as both sides indicated that they are open to thawing their long-frosty relations. The two countries have regularly clashed in recent years, in particular over Minsk’s alliance with Moscow, the migration crisis Belarus has engineered on the Polish border, and the persecution of Belarus’s ethnic Polish minority. Warsaw, meanwhile, has supported the Belarusian democratic opposition. However, on Tuesday this week, Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski confirmed to reporters that he had met with his Belarusian counterpart, Maxim Ryzhenkov, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Sikorski said that the initiative had come from the Belarusian side. “When a neighbour wants to unfreeze and improve relations, Poland is the first to reach an agreement,” said Sikorski, quoted by broadcaster RMF. “This is a first, introductory meeting, but meetings with other ministries and at other levels are also taking place,” he added, noting that Poland will also “soon be opening a new embassy building in Minsk”. When asked what topics had been discussed, Sikorski said that they had included the border situation and regional security. Asked if he had requested that Belarus not allow Russia to fly drones and missiles through its territory, he said that this was discussed “among other things”. The last known time that the Polish and Belarusian foreign ministers met was in October 2016, when Belarus’s Vladimir Makei visited Witold Waszczykowski in Warsaw. Sikorski said that this week’s meeting with Ryzhenkov had been possible because the situation on their shared border – where Belarus has since 2021 encouraged and assisted tens of thousands of migrants, mainly from Asia and Africa, to cross into Poland – is now “more normalised”. Poland has installed physical and electronic barriers along the border, sent thousands of armed officers to guard it, and has banned asylum claims by migrants who cross irregularly. Following those measures, the number of attempted crossings has fallen dramatically this year. Sikorski also noted that relations have been improved by Belarus’s recent decisions to release political prisoners, including Polish ones. Most prominent among them is Andrzej Poczobut, a leader of the Polish community in Belarus, who had been imprisoned on trumped-up charges for five years. The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 Minsk’s recent actions have provided “more freedom and greater reasons to try to stabilise relations”, said Sikorski. “A snowdrop can bloom if the weather is favorable.” Belarus’s foreign ministry continued that metaphor in a post on social media on Wednesday, sharing a photo of Sikorski meeting with Ryzhenkov and writing that “snowdrop diplomacy is a nice restart”. “But we’re in it for the harvest,” added the ministry. “Let’s plant an orchard – it needs nurturing every year, not once a decade. Minsk is ready to host.” Last year, Belarus called for “dialogue” with Poland in order to “reduce the risk of armed clashes” amid a military build-up around the border. However, it also issued a formal protest to Poland over a demonstration in Warsaw organised by exiled opponents of Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko. .@sikorskiradek, snowdrop diplomacy is a nice restart. But we’re in it for the harvest. Let’s plant an orchard 🍎 – it needs nurturing every year, not once a decade. Minsk is ready to host 🇧🇾🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/WSN5n4uOtE — Belarus MFA 🇧🇾 (@BelarusMFA) September 23, 2026 News of Tuesday’s meeting was criticised by Stanisław Żaryn, who served as spokesman for the Polish security services under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government and later as an advisor to President Andrzej Duda. In a social media post, he said that Sikorski and media outlets are “forcibly pushing us into another reset with Belarus (and perhaps even with Russia)”. However, “Belarus chose its strategic path long ago and won’t turn away from Russia”, he added. He asked if Poles are meant to forget about the death of Mateusz Sitek, a Polish soldier killed by a migrant from a group trying to force its way over the border from Belarus. His suspected killer, a Moroccan national, is believed by Polish prosecutors to still be in Belarus, which has refused to extradite him. Should “we just move on as if nothing happened regarding Belarus’s involvement in the war against Ukraine and the intelligence war against Poland?” continued Żaryn. ⚠️Radosław Sikorski spotkał się z Szefem MSZ Białorusi. Media już piszą o „przełomie”, a Sikorski zapewnia, że „Polska jest pierwsza do zgody”. Na siłę wtłaczają nas w kolejny reset z Białorusią (a być może i Rosją). Na czym mają polegać przełomy i „zgoda” w stosunkach z… pic.twitter.com/DZ41wSgjL0 — Stanisław Żaryn (@StZaryn) September 23, 2026 Francišak Viačorka, a leading figure in the exiled Belarusian democratic opposition, also expressed scepticism in an interview with Polish newspaper Fakt. “We believe that the authorities in Minsk cannot be trusted,” he said. “Of course, when the authorities communicate with Western partners, they promise that everything will be fine, that they want dialogue, but then their words fail to match their actions.” “I understand that Minister Sikorski is doing everything to protect Polish interests and the sovereignty and security of his country, but I think that in Minsk they see it differently.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Russian military helicopter briefly entered Polish airspace on Wednesday morning, the operational command of Poland’s armed forces has announced. The incident is the latest in a series of airspace violations by Russia, which have also involved drones and, most recently, a missile. It follows recent warnings by the Polish government that Moscow has been planning further “provocations” intended to test NATO’s defences and unity. ❗️ Informujemy, że 23 września br. o godz. 11.08, na północ od miejscowości Braniewo, doszło do krótkotrwałego naruszenia przestrzeni powietrznej Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej przez śmigłowiec Mi-8 Sił Zbrojnych Federacji Rosyjskiej. Śmigłowiec wykonywał lot z Obwodu Królewieckiego.… pic.twitter.com/afULQdSeTc — Dowództwo Operacyjne RSZ (@DowOperSZ) September 23, 2026 On Wednesday afternoon, Polish operational command announced that, shortly after 11:00 a.m. that day, an Mi-8 helicopter belonging to the Russian armed forces had briefly entered Polish airspace near the town of Braniewo, after crossing from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. The helicopter did not travel further than 300 metres into Polish airspace and remained there for 42 seconds. In response, the Polish military scrambled fighter jets and placed ground forces on standby. “The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defences,” wrote operational command. At the time of writing, Russia has not commented on the incident. Today’s violation appears to be the first publicly reported instance of a Russian military helicopter crossing Poland’s land border. Last year, in two separate incidents, a Russian Su-24 bomber and a naval helicopter flew over Poland’s territorial waters in the Baltic Sea. In 2023, two helicopters belonging to the armed forces of Belarus, a close ally of Russia, briefly entered Polish airspace before crossing back over the border. On one night in September last year, around 20 Russian drones entered Poland over its eastern borders amid Russian attacks on Ukraine. Polish and allied forces shot down some of them, while others hit the ground without causing casualties. In July this year, a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile carrying a significant explosive payload entered Polish airspace before landing in a field in eastern Poland. The object that crashed in the Lublin region on Thursday was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile carrying a "significant amount" of explosive material. In the last few weeks, Poland has regularly intercepted Russian aircraft that have flown close to Polish territorial waters in the Baltic Sea. This month, Russian drones have repeatedly hit targets in Ukraine near to the Polish border, including a passenger train travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw. Just last week, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that, according to intelligence sources, Russia is planning drone and missile strikes on eastern NATO countries, which it would present as accidental. World.title: Czech Statehood Day 2026: What Is Open and What to Do in Prague
World.content:
September 28 is a public holiday in the Czech Republic, marking Czech Statehood Day and the feast of St. Wenceslas. This year, the holiday falls on a Monday, giving many people a three-day weekend.

For anyone planning to spend the day in Prague, however, there are two practical questions: which shops will be open, and what can you do around the city?



Where you can shop on September 28

Under Czech legislation regulating retail opening hours, shops with a sales area of more than 200 square meters must close on September 28.

The restriction applies throughout the day and covers large supermarkets, hypermarkets and home improvement stores.

Smaller shops with sales areas of up to 200 square meters are exempt and can open at their owners’ discretion. Petrol stations and pharmacies can also operate.

Other exceptions include shops located at airports, railway stations and bus terminals, as well as retail outlets inside healthcare facilities.

Why September 28 is Czech Statehood Day

The holiday commemorates Prince Wenceslas, a member of the Přemyslid dynasty who became one of the central figures in Czech history.

Wenceslas was killed by his brother Boleslav I on September 28, 935, in Stará Boleslav. His death later became the foundation of a cult that developed around him from the late 10th century onward.

His remains were transferred to Prague in 938 on Boleslav’s orders and buried in the Rotunda of St. Vitus. The reasons behind the transfer are not known with certainty, but the move helped strengthen Wenceslas’s status as a religious figure while also reinforcing Prague’s position as the center of the emerging Czech state.

Over the following centuries, Wenceslas became the patron saint of the Czech lands and an important symbol of Czech statehood.

The connection between Wenceslas and Czech political tradition was further strengthened under Charles IV, who commissioned the Crown of Saint Wenceslas. The crown became one of the principal symbols of the Czech monarchy and remains part of the Czech Crown Jewels.

See the Czech Crown Jewels at Prague Castle

September 28 is also the final day of this year’s exhibition of the Czech Crown Jewels at Prague Castle.

The jewels are being displayed in Vladislav Hall as part of the exhibition Habsburgs 500. Admission is free, and the display also includes a coronation robe dating from 1653 and other historical objects.

The exhibition closes at the end of the day on September 28.

Government buildings open to visitors

Several normally restricted buildings will also be accessible to the public.

Straka Academy, the official seat of the Czech government, will open its doors on September 28. Visitors can see the government meeting room, ceremonial areas and the building’s garden.

The program also includes an interactive exhibition called Journey of the Republic. Tours are free and begin at 10 a.m., with the final group scheduled to leave at 5 p.m.

The Ministry of Finance on Letenská Street will also welcome visitors. Tours start at 9:30 a.m. and include the ministry’s historic premises and the former monastery.

Museums and other attractions

The National Technical Museum in Letná will remain open on September 28, giving visitors access to its permanent exhibitions.

The Postal Museum will also be open.

For those looking for a more traditional Prague attraction, September 28 will be the final chance this year to ride the historic Letná Carousel.

Another option is the National Museum, where the Přemyslids exhibition examines the history of the dynasty that ruled the Czech lands during the country’s early medieval period.

The exhibition runs until October 15, 2026, making the public holiday particularly relevant for visitors interested in the history behind Czech Statehood Day.

World.title: Bangkok Gears Up for the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings
World.content:
All eyes are on Thailand as the country prepares to host the 2026 International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group (WBG) Annual Meetings, also known as the 2026 Annual Meetings or AM2026 Thailand.

Running from 12-18 October 2026, at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) in Bangkok, the event will mark Thailand’s second time hosting the meetings, following its first in 1991. This will make Thailand one of only three nations to have hosted the IMF–WBG Annual Meetings twice.



The IMF–WBG Annual Meetings, held for two consecutive years in Washington D.C. and every third year in one of the 191 member countries, serve as a gathering of top economic figures from around the world. By covering a broad range of issues, the meetings aim to strengthen global financial stability, combat poverty, and ensure inclusive economic growth and job creation.

Thailand’s selection to host again in 2026 highlights how the country has advanced over the past three decades in terms of its institutional progress, economic resilience, and sustained engagement with international partners. As host, Thailand brings decades’ worth of experience in economic transformation and regional leadership to the table.

The “Olympics of Finance”

Often dubbed the “Olympics of Finance,” the meetings are set to attract more than 15,000 participants, including finance ministers, central bankers, economists, business leaders, civil society representatives, and journalists from the IMF and World Bank’s 191 member countries, including the Czech Republic.

The Annual Meetings will be held under the theme of “Thailand’s New Horizons: Empowering People, Building Resilience”. Therefore, the meetings will focus on enhancing people’s potential and creating opportunities, with the goal of fostering a financial and economic system that is safe, sustainable, and inclusive.

Under the theme, the government plans to showcase four policy priorities it believes are increasingly relevant in an era marked by geopolitical fragmentation, economic volatility, and demographic change. These are indeed the issues that warrant serious conversation and sincere collaboration among the global community and all stakeholders to address them in the most efficient way:

Digital Transformation: The first centers on digital transformation and artificial intelligence, using the examples from Thailand’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including PromptPay and cross-border QR payment systems.

The first centers on digital transformation and artificial intelligence, using the examples from Thailand’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including PromptPay and cross-border QR payment systems. Connected Economy: A second pillar focuses on what is called “Building Resilience in a Fragmented World”. In order to achieve this, the concept of a “Connected Economy” capable of bridging divides between competing blocs while strengthening supply chains and investment links will be explored.

A second pillar focuses on what is called “Building Resilience in a Fragmented World”. In order to achieve this, the concept of a “Connected Economy” capable of bridging divides between competing blocs while strengthening supply chains and investment links will be explored. Climate Finance: The third pillar addresses climate finance, with emphasis on reforms to help countries adapt to climate change.

The third pillar addresses climate finance, with emphasis on reforms to help countries adapt to climate change. Longevity Economy: The final priority seeks to turn the challenges of ageing populations into new sources of economic growth.

Alongside these focus areas, the Bank of Thailand plans to unveil the “Bangkok Blueprint,” an international framework developed jointly with the IMF and the World Bank aimed at combating digital financial fraud and strengthening trust in the digital economy.

Readiness in All Aspects

According to the Fiscal Policy Office, Thailand’s overall readiness has been assessed at “Grade A” following months of coordination between the Ministry of Finance, the Bank of Thailand, and the IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings Secretariat.

Preparations extend beyond the conference venue. Authorities have developed contingency plans for traffic management, emergency responses, and arrangements for high-level foreign officials. A working group has also been established to address cybersecurity matters.

Beyond Tourism: A Regional Economic Capital

Beyond its long-established reputation as a world-renowned tourist destination, the 2026 Annual Meetings offer Thailand an excellent opportunity to present another dimension of the Kingdom to the international community.

AM2026 reinforces Thailand’s standing as a trusted international partner while highlighting its growing role as a regional economic capital and a hub for finance, investment, policy innovation, and multilateral dialogue in Southeast Asia. Having said that, countries and companies vying for economic and business opportunities cannot overlook Thailand and its potential to become an important impetus for their long-term prosperity and growth.
