World.title: Iraqi PM calls on US firms to seize investment opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on US companies on Wednesday to seize investment opportunities available in Iraq, particularly in the petrochemicals, glass, and phosphate industries, as well as the gas and clean energy sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting in New York with a delegation from the US Chamber of Commerce, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister stated that Iraq has considerable natural resources, human resources, and a key geographical position, all of which serve as necessary foundations for successful partnerships. He explained that the government is seeking to use these resources to promote economic development and increase investment possibilities.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the government’s commitment to providing support for businesses and investors, such as granting ownership of land for investment projects in accordance with Iraqi laws, as well as access to tax and customs exemptions for up to ten years.

Iraq is working on infrastructure and transportation projects, notably the strategic project of the Development Road, which will improve Iraq’s position as a corridor connecting the East and West, according to al-Zaidi.

The prime minister affirmed that the government looks forward to establishing factories and setting up projects to diversify the economy and create job opportunities.

Al-Zaidi also asked members of the US Chamber of Commerce and specialized firms to attend the Baghdad Energy Conference and capitalize on the prospects offered in the country. He added that Iraq aspires to establish economic partnerships based on collaboration, mutual interest, and long-term investment.

World.title: Iraqi PM, US president discuss partnerships, regional stability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met with US President Donald Trump in New York on Tuesday on the sideline of his participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The two leaders discussed bilateral relations and approaches to strengthen cooperation and partnership between the two countries across political, economic, and investment sectors, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The two sides also reviewed the latest developments in the region, as well as the joint efforts undertaken by Iraq and the United States to enhance regional and international security and stability.

The discussion takes place ahead of a crucial September 30 milestone, which marks a shift in Washington-Baghdad ties toward long-term economic collaboration as the US prepares to end its coalition military mission in Iraq.

Amid continuing negotiations between Iraq and US officials, including a recent meeting between al-Zaidi and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Washington pressured Baghdad on its obligations to place weapons possessed by armed factions under state supervision.

In addition to their exclusive bilateral discussion, al-Zaidi attended President Trump’s larger gathering that included leaders from important regional powers, including Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Jordan, Egypt, and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nations.

The larger gathering addressed strategies to coordinate post-war arrangements, protect global commerce supply lines, and develop diplomatic frameworks for Middle Eastern stability.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Iranian president in New York
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met on Wednesday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in New York on the sidelines of their participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the meeting addressed developments in the region and the necessity of working together to handle difficulties in ways that promote security and stability.

The two leaders also addressed approaches to keep the region from spiraling into a cycle of escalation, tensions, and crises.

During a meeting on Wednesday with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein emphasized the importance of defusing regional tensions through dialogue.

The meeting addressed bilateral relations and regional developments, as well as the importance of continued coordination between the two countries to respond to current challenges and support diplomatic efforts aimed at enhancing regional stability.

Hussein also stressed the significance of continued diplomatic efforts among the parties involved to defuse tension and prevent escalation.

Araghchi outlined the discussions that began between Iran and the United States, sponsored by an intermediary, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meetings in New York. These discussions attempt to de-escalate the situation and find approaches to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for navigation.

The two ministers also discussed the outcomes of the meeting involving the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, Iraq, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, and Turkey—attended by US President Donald Trump—as well as how regional and international relationships might help efforts for de-escalation.

World.title: Iraq’s Gulf Cup 27 match against Oman ends in 1-1 draw
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi and Omani national teams drew 1-1 on Wednesday in the opening match of the 27th Gulf Cup held at Prince Abdullah Al-Faisal Sports City Stadium in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

Iraq launched a strong attack, causing Oman to make a defensive mistake. Zaid Ismail took advantage of the rebound and set it up for Mohammed Qasim, who fired a rocket shot with his left foot into the near corner, giving the “Lions of Mesopotamia” an early lead in the sixth minute.

The Omani team’s performance improved, and their level rose during the second half. After a decisive and skillful pass from Ahmed al-Kaabi, Nasser al-Rawahi scored the equalizer brilliantly from a close range, winning the “Man of the Match” award in recognition of his outstanding performance.

In a candid evaluation, Australian coach Graham Arnold, who manages the Iraqi national team, acknowledged that the team’s performance fell short of expectations. He pointed out that the rushed preparations had hindered the implementation of their tactical plan.

The Iraqi team only had one training session before the tournament compared to six for the Omani team.

“We were not the better side, and we must work harder in the coming matches to secure the win,” Arnold said.

The manager of the Oman team, Tarik Sektioui, expressed his great pride in his team, describing the squad as “fighters” for their ability to recover from an early setback and snatch a vital opening point against the defending champions.

World.title: Turkey to hand over military base to enhance Iraqi sovereignty
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced on Wednesday that Turkish forces will gradually hand over the Bashiqa-Zelikan base to the Iraqi government.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the handover process will take place in accordance with an agreed-upon mechanism and timeline amid the progress Iraq has achieved through security measures.

During their meeting on the sideline of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, the two leaders agreed to deepen security cooperation in negotiations in which Iraqi and Turkish authorities discussed strategic relations.

Additionally, al-Zaidi and Erdogan agreed to completely expand the Iraqi state’s authority in Sinjar and to eliminate the presence of banned foreign armed groups.

Turkey established a military base in Bashiqa, near Mosul, in December 2015, initially deploying around 600 soldiers to train local forces to combat ISIS terrorist groups.

The deployment of Turkish soldiers without formal consent from Iraq has been a longstanding point of contention, often regarded as a violation of Iraq’s sovereignty and a strain on the relationship between Ankara and Baghdad.

As part of the agreement, Iraq agreed to restore state authority in Sinjar and remove or disarm foreign armed groups and militias that Turkey sees as security risks.

World.title: Iraq to raise gas production at Nahr Bin Umar to 300 million cubic feet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil revealed on Monday that it is planning to increase associated gas recovery at the Nahr Bin Umar field to 300 million cubic feet per day.

Deputy Minister for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber chaired a meeting to review associated gas recovery plans and projects at the Nahr Bin Umar field in the southern province of Basra.

The meeting was attended by representatives from the South Gas Company (SGC) and the project operator, Halfaya Gas Company, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The meeting focused on the development plan to enhance associated gas recovery, aiming for a target of 300 million standard cubic feet per day.

The plan will be implemented in two phases, each with a capacity of 150 million standard cubic feet per day.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil said earlier that the Bin Umar gas project will produce between 500 and 600 tons of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Saber mentioned earlier that the project, which will minimize gas flaring and support the country’s electricity grid, is planned to be operational by the end of April.

Saber confirmed the news while inspecting the project’s final connection point in mid-April.

The project will produce 70 million standard cubic feet per day of raw gas, between 500 and 600 tons of LPG for home consumption, around 80 million standard cubic feet per day of dry gas for power plants, and more than 1,800 barrels per day of condensates.

The initiative is an important step toward increasing gas utilization, preventing gas flaring, and strengthening the country’s electricity grid.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 3 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Tuesday that oil exports for August reached approximately 70 million barrels, with daily shipments exceeding three million barrels.

In a televised interview, Khudair explained that the deals the ministry reached to transport oil through the Turkish port of Ceyhan raised the volumes to 600,000 barrels per day, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Iraq’s oil exports fluctuated during September 2026, amid ongoing geopolitical tensions related to the Middle East war and Baghdad’s efforts to diversify its export routes.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that exports started at three million barrels per day at the beginning of September but have since gradually declined to about 2.4 million barrels per day at present.

Despite a decline in Iraqi oil exports during September, the figures still surpassed the average daily exports in August, which were approximately 2.35 million barrels per day. This increase was bolstered by enhanced shipping traffic and a decrease in shipping disruptions in the Gulf over the past few weeks.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

The prime minister indicated that it is important to improve infrastructure and export capacity to meet the expected rise in output.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

Al-Zaidi directed an increase in output from oil fields in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the expansion of exploration activities to achieve the plan’s objectives and reach a production capacity of 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

World.title: Iraq’s exports hit $19.55 billion in Q1 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Figures released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) showed that the country’s exports reached $19.55 billion in the first quarter of 2026, compared to imports of $10.27 billion.

Hydrocarbons continued to account for the significant bulk of Iraq’s exports, exposing the country to larger global energy dynamics.

Iraq’s crude oil exports totaled $18.64 billion, petroleum products $762.2 million, and other exports $148.5 million.

The state sector’s imports totaled $1.35 billion, and the private sector’s imports reached $8.92 billion, according to the National Iraqi News Agency (NINA).

Iraq’s trade balance indicated a surplus of $10.82 billion, according to figures from the CBI that compare exports with imports.

The country’s exports during the first quarter of 2026 are lower than those of the fourth quarter of 2025, which stood at $21.62 billion.

Iraq’s export capacity during the first quarter of 2026 experienced significant headwinds due to rigorous OPEC+ production limits and interruptions related to maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: PM Modi grooves with Gen Z at 'bhajan clubbing' event
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Mixing modern trends with tradition, PM Narendra Modi Friday evening attended a 'bhajan clubbing' at a park named after BJP ideologue Deen Dayal Upadhyay to pay him tributes on his 116th birth anniversary.

Attended by a young cohort, whose embrace of bhajan clubbing has made it a big trend, especially among the urban youth, across the country, the event drew praise from Modi.

"Bhajan Clubbing in Delhi. Spectacular," he said of the event, which saw a live performance by a band.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Bhajan clubbing has a concert-like feel and hosts devotional songs, with its popularity shining a light on the growing traction of religiosity in the younger demography, who has chosen to shape it in its own style.

Modi's participation marks his continuous engagement with the Gen Z crowd at a time when his political opponents are trying hard to woo them as well.

He had spoken about this at his Mann Ki Baat broadcast in Jan, saying the young generation has adapted devotion to their lifestyle.

This mindset has given rise to a new cultural trend, he had said.

World.title: Amazon, Flipkart & JioMart fined for illegal herbicide sale
World.content:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart, for selling and advertising an unregistered agrochemical product.Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed for preventing and eliminating weeds.CCPA directed the e-commerce marketplaces to discontinue false s and conduct self-audits to identify products that violate the law or pose a risk to life and safety.Proceedings began after the department of agriculture and farmers' welfare forwarded a complaint from Crop Care Federation of India. The department said insecticides and pesticides are regulated under Insecticides Act, 1968, and Insecticides Rules. It said no chemical named Cyclosinone was listed in the Act's Schedule, and the product did not disclose its composition.CCPA rejected the companies' argument that they could not be held responsible for products listed by third-party sellers.

World.title: PSU banks lift ATM charges in view of strike
World.content:
PSBs, RRBs waive ATM fees ahead of 3-day strike

NEW DELHI: Public sector banks and regional rural banks have announced their decision to waive ATM charges to ensure hassle-free cash withdrawal by their customers from Sept 28-30 due to the strike called by employee unions.Besides, all branches of state-run banks and RRB will remain open on Sunday as the unions have called a three-day strike starting Monday. "Withdrawals from other bank ATMs can be made without charges from 26th to 30th Sept," Indian Bank said. HDFC said its branches will remain open Sunday and it will be business as usual during the strike.Govt earlier asked for payment of salaries and pension to retired personnel ahead of time to avoid the impact of strike. TNN

World.title: AFSPA extended in 3 NE states; Kuki group chief held in Aizawl
World.content:
NEW DELHI/ AIZAWL: The home ministry Friday extended the application of Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 in parts of Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagal-and for six months, until March 31, 2027.

Status quo has been retained in terms of police stations and districts declared "disturbed".

Meanwhile, the commander-in-chief of the banned United Kuki National Army was arrested Thursday in Aizawl and will be sent to Manipur, a senior police officer said. Thangkhomang Haokip was held in a joint operation by Assam Rifles and Subsidiary Intelligence Bureau. "He is not in the custody of Mizoram police. The case is most likely to be taken over by NIA," the officer said.

A central agency official said NIA sleuths had also arrested two Kuki student leaders from Manipur at a hotel in Aizawl.

Haokip is accused of involvement in several attacks, including a 2024 ambush on an advance security convoy of then Manipur CM N Biren Singh.

(With inputs from HC Vanlalruata)

World.title: Months after OSM row, government appoints new CBSE chairperson
World.content:
Senior bureaucrat Mandeep K Bhandari

NEW DELHI: Senior bureaucrat Mandeep K Bhandari was appointed CBSE chairperson, months after the rollout of On-Screen Marking (OSM)-based evaluation and post-result processes triggered complaints over alleged answer-sheet mix-ups, portal glitches, payment failures and delays in re-evaluation.Bhandari, a 2001-batch IAS officer of AGMUT cadre, is currently principal secretary to J&K lieutenant governor. The appointments committee of the Cabinet approved his appointment, personnel department said. His was among 10 transfers and postings effected by govt Friday.On June 2, govt removed CBSE chairperson Rahul Singh and secretary Himanshu Gupta and ordered an inquiry into procurement of the digital evaluation system.In other postings, Vipin Kumar, AAI chairperson, was appointed additional secretary, rural development. Anand Singh will be additional secretary, economic affairs department.

World.title: EAM Jaishankar snubs scribe from 'terrorist country'
World.content:
External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Friday sharply responded to a Pakistani journalist who asked him a question related to

. "A terrorist country is asking me that question. Come on," Jaishankar said in a strong response to the question by the Pakistani journalist at the

.

Jaishankar and Liberia's foreign minister Sara Beysolow Nyanti delivered remarks to the press at the UN HQ on the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers.

After their remarks, the

i journalist stood up and shouted a question to Jaishankar, "When will your government stop sponsoring terrorism in Pakistan?"

India's permanent representative to the United Nations, Harish Parvathaneni, told the Pakistani journalist, "You have heard your reply. You have heard your response, loud and clear."

World.title: On UNGA margins, India & Liberia set up sailors' safety body
World.content:
India & Liberia set up sailorsâ safety body

NEW DELHI: India teamed up with Liberia to establish a Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers. Addressing the inaugural meeting on the margins of UNGA, foreign minister S Jaishankar said actions that disrupt maritime commerce and cost innocent lives are simply indefensible.Foreign ministers and senior diplomats from 23 other countries, including Russia, Germany and Japan, participated in the meeting."We are here to not highlight this dangerous trend but to urge the international community to close ranks and deter such attacks," he said, recalling PM Narendra Modi's proposal at the recent Brics summit for a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to help seafarers in need.Jaishankar said the Group of Friends consists of major ship-owning member states, countries with the largest number of ship registries and those providing the maximum number of seafarers.Expressing concern over attacks on civilian shipping, he said stronger international cooperation was needed.

World.title: In a first, waste plastic mixed with bitumen in pilot test section of NH-44
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a first for the road sector, govt has used waste plastic as a wet mix with bitumen to lay a bituminous highway stretch, a move that is likely to reduce imports of the key construction material while addressing the growing problem of plastic waste.On Thursday, a pilot test section was laid on the main carriageway of NH-44 in Jhansi. Officials associated with the pilot said the technology has potential to reduce conventional bitumen consumption by around 4%, lowering demand for a material that India largely imports to meet domestic requirements. They added that the modified bitumen could cost around 20% less than conventional bitumen.The waste plastic wet-process technology for producing premium-quality Waste Plastic Modified Bitumen (W-PMB 76-10) has been developed by IIT (BHU), Varanasi, under a research programme funded by the ministry of road transport and highways. The performance of the pilot stretch will be monitored by IIT (BHU) to assess its long-term engineering performance and field suitability, officials said.India generates around 25,000 tonne of plastic waste every day. Until now, waste plastic has been used in road construction only as a dry mix with aggregates while laying the bituminous layer. The new method mixes processed waste plastic directly with bitumen before it is laid, making it the first such pilot on a national highway.Officials said the technology offers multiple benefits, including the value-added reuse of waste plastic through a scientifically controlled process and improved rut resistance of bituminous mixes under high ambient temperatures and heavy axle loads.The technology has also recently been granted a patent. The low-density polyethylene (LDPE) used in the process â a soft, flexible and lightweight thermoplastic made from petroleum â includes discarded irrigation pipes, waste files and plastic folders. The material has been processed with the support of local recyclers and MSMEs, creating an opportunity to integrate local waste recycling with infrastructure development.âLaboratory evaluations have shown that LDPE-modified bitumen provides better resistance to moisture damage and greater resistance to rutting at high temperatures. The modified binder increases the stiffness and high-temperature performance of asphalt, helping pavements withstand permanent deformation under heavy traffic loads and extreme temperatures,â an official said.

World.title: U.P. Congress leaders clash with police, detained during protest against Chief Election Commissioner
World.content:
Uttar PradeshCongress unit on Friday (September 25, 2026) held a demonstration against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and clashed with the police, demanding accountability from the Commission, adding that fair elections are the foundation of democracy and alleged the people of the country are witnessing the way constitutional norms are being flouted.

The Congress leaders, including State Congress chief Ajay Rai and party workers demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, were stopped and later detained while trying to march towards the Uttar Pradesh Assembly. Mr. Rai alleged that the Chief Election Commissioner had played a role in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s victory in Varanasi and demanded that the election be cancelled.

“Attack on democracy and tampering with the autonomy of constitutional institutions will no longer be tolerated. As part of the nationwide protest of the Indian National Congress, today a fierce demonstration was held on the streets of Lucknow along with the Uttar Pradesh Congress colleagues against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. Fair elections are the foundation of democracy, but the people of the country are witnessing the way constitutional norms are being flouted. Congress will continue its fight from the streets to Parliament to protect the rights of the people and democracy. We are going to organize district-level protests on Monday. The way heavy police force was deployed on the streets of Lucknow shows that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government is fully protecting the Chief Election Commissioner. Our workers were detained during the protest; it shows the dictatorial mindset of the state administration,” told Mr. Rai, to The Hindu.

Mr. Rai and other Congress leaders climbed the barricades and raised slogans, following which a scuffle broke out between them and the police. The Congress leaders and hundreds of protesting Congress workers were taken to the Eco Garden — a protest site in the State capital, and later released in the evening.

World.title: FIR lodged against Bihar CMO staff for posting Jamui victim’s photo on X
World.content:
Biharpolice on Friday (September 25, 2026) registered an FIR at Secretariat Police Station against Sagar Prasad, an official posted at Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), in connection with posting the photographs of Jamui molestation victim’s family on Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary’s official social media handle X.

Earlier, the Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav had accused the Bihar CM of revealing the identity of the victim, calling it a violation of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, by sharing the photograph of the minor girl who was molested on September 19, 2026. However, the photograph was deleted within 15 minutes after posting it.

The minor girl, along with her family members, met Mr. Choudhary at his official residence in Patna on Thursday (September 24, 2026).

Following a meeting with the victim’s family, a post was shared from Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary’s official X handle stating, “Met the girl from Jamui and her family at the official residence. Assured the daughter that she could move forward fearlessly and promised the family speedy justice. The family also expressed satisfaction with the police action. The strictest punishment will be ensured for all the accused within one month through a speedy trial.”

The unblurred photo of the minor girl along with her mother and family members was shared on X.

“The viral nature of the post has compromised the privacy and dignity of the minor victim and her family, creating a situation where the victim’s identity is at risk of exposure. Upon verification, it was found that Sagar Prasad, a stenographer in the CMO’s office, had uploaded the victim’s photograph to the ‘X’ platform,” police said.

Police have registered an FIR against Sagar Prasad as well as other individuals or social media users who forwarded or circulated the post.

World.title: Greater Noida bus fire: booking manager arrested for negligence
World.content:
The Greater Noida police on Friday arrested the booking manager of Raj Kalpana Travels, one of whose buses, en route to Mahoba in Uttar Pradesh, burst into flames on the night of September 23, killing nine passengers.

An officer said analysis of call detail records showed that passengers had contacted the manager — 42-year-old Kanpur resident Vikas Kumar — to flag concerns about smoke and fire before the blaze.

However, he did not take any action despite being alerted, said the police. He has been booked for negligence.

The bus, with around 35 passengers on board, was about 5 km from the Noida International Airport when the fire broke out.

As per the FIR, registered at the Jewar police station following a complaint by a survivor, passengers noticed a burning smell from the driver’s cabin around 11.30 p.m. and repeatedly asked the crew to stop. But the driver dismissed it as a common occurrence and did not stop to inspect the vehicle.

Sent to judicial custody

Earlier, the police had arrested two drivers and a conductor. All four accused were produced before the District and Sessions Court in Surajpur on Friday and were remanded in 14 days’ judicial custody.

Breathalyser tests conducted on the drivers and conductor have returned negative results, the police said. Meanwhile, three more victims were identified on Friday and their bodies were handed over to their families. A senior officer said the bodies were severely burnt and were identified through DNA tests, along with the verification of physical features by relatives.

World.title: Former IAS officer appointed on Maha UCC panel
World.content:
Shatrughna Singh, a retired IAS officer of the Uttarakhand cadre, has been appointed as a member of the MaharashtraUniform Civil Code committee. The proposal was approved by the Maharashtra government early this week. This was after the chairperson of the committee moved a proposal to include him in the panel. Ranjana Desai, retired Supreme Court judge, heads the panel.

“The proposal was sent by her quite a few days ago. Mr. Singh has worked with her previously on the consultations related to the Uniform Civil Code. He knows the functioning of the panel due to his past experience. That is why Ms. Desai had requested that he should be made a part of the committee. The government approved her proposal recently,” a senior government official told The Hindu.

When asked if the appointment was made after the resignation of former Bombay High Court judge R.C. Chavan, the official said that the two incidents were unrelated. “The decision of Mr. Singh’s appointment is independent of any other development, least of all the resignation of Justice [retired] R.C. Chavan. These are two unrelated incidents. There is no statutory requirement for the panel to consist of seven members. We can have more than eight or less than seven,” the official said.

Mr. Chavan had recently tendered his resignation, citing serious reservations about certain aspects of the functioning of the panel. He had levelled criticism at the panel’s methodology, questioning the purpose of consensus-building by underplaying complex issues.

Maharashtra UCC panel was formed two months ago to draft a framework for the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code. It consists of former High Court judge S.G. Mehare, Maharashtra ex-chief secretary D.K. Jain, former advocate general Virendra Saraf, constitutional expert Ramesh Patange and educationist Suvarna Rawal. It has been asked to examine the legal, social, cultural and administrative aspects of the Uniform Civil Code and give a report about it in six months. The panel will do a comparative study of the experiences of other states which have already implemented the code.

Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has earlier said that the State government will table the legislation this year during the winter session. Union Home Minister Amit Shah had said in his address in Mumbai this month that the UCC will be introduced in 21 States before the year 2029. The year 2029 is when the next Lok Sabha elections will be held.

World.title: Congress hopes for calm in Punjab unit but storm clouds remain ahead of 2027 Assembly election
World.content:
The absence of a few senior leaders, including former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi, from the Punjab Congress unit’s demonstration on Friday in Chandigarh against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar has again raised questions about the party’s internal cohesion.

The July 1 revamp of the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) had sparked turmoil in the Punjab unit. Amarinder Singh Raja Warring was retained as the PPCC chief, and Mr. Channi, the Lok Sabha member from Jalandhar and the Congress’s most prominent Dalit face in the State, was appointed to lead the election campaign committee in the run-up to the 2027 Assembly election. Mr. Channi and a few other leaders, including Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, Rana Gurjit and Tript Rajinder Singh Bajwa, were believed to be upset with the revamp of the party unit. Their supporters demanded that Mr. Warring be replaced as PPCC president, exposing the factional fault lines within the State unit.

PPCC revamp

With the elections approaching and differences persisting, the central leadership of the Congress brought in Sachin Pilot to replace Bhupesh Baghel, a former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister, as the general secretary in charge of the poll-bound State. Soon after taking charge, Mr. Pilot asserted that nearly all the leaders in Punjab have assured him of working collectively and unitedly.

Amid the ongoing power tussle, particularly between Mr. Channi and the PPCC president, the senior leaders showed a rare sign of unity by participating in the demonstration on September 9 against the Punjab government in Chandigarh, led by Mr. Pilot, a former Rajasthan Deputy Chief Minister.

A party source said earlier this week that a meeting regarding the State unit took place at the residence of national president Mallikarjun Kharge, where senior party leader Rahul Gandhi and Mr. Pilot were present. Mr. Pilot reportedly submitted a detailed feedback report on the affairs of the Punjab unit to the party’s top leadership.

The source added, “The situation in the State unit at present is quiet, but it could be like a calm before the storm. The party high command had asked the new in-charge to take a broad view of the PPCC’s affairs and issues and share it. The feedback has been given. I am confident the issues such as changes at the top leadership of the State unit will be resolved by next week, after which a possible bus yatra led by Mr. Gandhi to kick off the party’s election campaign could be organised.”

World.title: ‘What steps are you taking?’: HC questions DU over hostel shortage, flags ‘vague’ reply
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Friday criticised Delhi University over its response on the issue of adding additional hostel facilities for students as “absolutely vague” while hearing various petitions on the September 6 Satya Niketan multi-storey building collapse in which seven persons, including five students, lost their lives.

The court made stern remarks on the question of building new hostels for students.

A counsel for one of the petitioners pointed out that DU’s affidavit showed that only 5,698 students were being provided hostel accommodation, even as nearly 1.3 lakh students regularly attend classes. The Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia then stated: “You (DU) are only giving figures, as against the students’ strength of more than a lakh, you are giving hostel facilities to a few thousand. And then you say that you are taking steps. What are those steps?”

“From which corner are you not getting cooperation? Tell us,” it added.

The DU counsel said the university would file a “better affidavit”.

During the proceedings, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the civic agency and the Delhi police, shared details of the action taken by the MCD and the police following the collapse.

Multiple inquiries

He said the Delhi government had commissioned a magisterial inquiry to look into the incident, as well as issues such as the validity of permissions, compliance with building by-laws and the role of the concerned officials.

The Delhi government had also constituted a high-powered committee on student accommodation and safety to examine issues relating to student accommodation and safety in Delhi and to recommend appropriate, time-bound measures, Mr. Mehta added.

On the Satya Niketan tragedy, the MCD said the exact cause of the collapse could not be ascertained. It, however, said that the downpour before September 6 “could have weakened” the old structure. The civic agency added that it had carried out a detailed inspection of about 300 properties in the students’ hub and found 101 housing PGs.

PGs vacated

“Of these, three properties were declared dangerous, and the PGs in them were vacated. Ten properties were identified as vulnerable and requiring major repairs, while 14 were found to require minor repairs,” the MCD told the court, which listed the matter for hearing on October 14.

World.title: M.M. Joshi condemns music concert at Badrinath, urges Centre and Uttarakhand government to ban such events
World.content:
Amid a controversy over concert-style “Bhajan Jamming” organised by the Indian Army at the Badrinath shrine, veteran Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader M.M. Joshi on Friday criticised the act and termed it a violation of the shrine’s cultural traditions and religious sanctity.

Organised under the theme “Our Heritage, Our Future”, the event was held at the Tourist Arrival Plaza adjoining the Badrinath temple, at an altitude of over 10,200 feet on September 19-20, 2026. The Chamoli district administration and Uttarakhand Tourism Department attributed the event’s organisation to the Indian Army.

Taking to the social media platform X, Mr Joshi said that organising a loud musical event at the sacred Himalayan shrine amounted to an assault on the faith of millions of devotees.

“It is noteworthy that this temple was established by Adi Guru Shankaracharya in the Himalayan environment for peaceful devotion through divine hymns....even blowing a conch shell is prohibited at this site, yet we disregarded this and organized a noisy music event, thereby gravely neglecting India’s spiritual, cultural, and environmental values,” he said.

Mr. Joshi added that allowing thousands to dance at such a high altitude, ignores the adverse health impacts on them as well.

Calling out the ‘transformation of Dev Bhoomi into a hub of commercial culture’, the senior BJP leader urged the Centre and Uttarakhand government to prohibit such events and preserve the spiritual character of the state.

“The Himalayas are divine, the abode of Lord Shiva and the origin of Mother Ganga. Turning this sacred land into a dance venue is a deep blow to the faith of crores of Indians,” he said in his post.

The event drew criticism from religious leaders like Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, Shankaracharya of Jyotirmath. Local stakeholders and Opposition Congress leaders also questioned the appropriateness of concert-style entertainment at one of Hinduism’s most revered pilgrimage sites.

World.title: Revisit history with The Hindu’s special Gandhi Jayanthi edition
World.content:
This Gandhi Jayanthi, readers can own a slice of history. The Hindu is bringing out a commemorative reprint of the October 2, 1969 edition and the 2003 feature, The Mahatma and The Hindu.

The special commemorative edition brings together rare archival pages from its history.

The edition traces Gandhiji’s journey from his early years as an attorney and activist in South Africa, to the moment of India’s Independence and features archival photographs capturing the Mahatma at various moments in history.

The limited edition is available on Zepto ahead of Gandhi Jayanthi across major Indian cities. Readers may place orders through https://newsth.live/zepto-Oct2 or scan the code.

World.title: Any attempt to divert Pakistan’s water to be treated as act of war, India ‘must make no mistake about it’: PM at UNGA
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that any attempt by India to divert Pakistan’s share of water would be treated as an “act of war”.

“Any attempt to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of the waters will be treated as an act of war. India must make no mistake about it,” he said during a speech at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, where he called attention to the neighbouring country’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance.

In his address, the prime minister highlighted India’s abeyance of the IWT since last year, stressing that it had no legal basis.

He highlighted that the country’s claims and actions regarding the treaty had been rejected by UN experts as well as by the Permanent Court of Arbitration, leaving Pakistan “vindicated beyond any ray of doubt” in its position.

“Water must never be weaponised. Rivers should nourish nations, not divide them,” he stressed, calling the Indus river system the “lifeblood” of the entire region.

PM Shehbaz also addressed last year’s brief military conflict with India, which came after an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26 tourists — an incident New Delhi blamed on Islamabad without evidence. For its part, Pakistan strongly denied the allegations and called for a neutral investigation.

“Our brave and valiant armed forces, under the courageous leadership of Field Marshal Asim Munir, responded with precision and professionalism,” he said.

He once again praised US President Donald Trump’s “resolute and visionary leadership” in brokering a ceasefire between the two countries in May 2025, stressing that it saved “hundreds of millions of lives”.

“Who knows the extent of devastation that could have taken place had President Trump not stepped in at this critical moment with clarity of thought and action?” he questioned.

“We must therefore ensure that South Asia never reaches this precipice ever again,” he said. This, however, the premier added, required a fair resolution of the Kashmir dispute.

“For eight decades, the Kashmiri people have waited for the United Nations to fulfill its solemn commitment of a free and impartial plebiscite,” he pointed out, adding that they had endured “illegal occupation, arbitrary detention, extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, sexual violence and collective punishment” for generations.

He declared that Pakistan would continue to extend its full diplomatic, political and moral support to Kashmiris until they were granted their right to self-determination, terming Kashmir “Pakistan’s jugular vein”.

Pakistan’s peace efforts

During his address, the prime minister also addressed the conflict in the Gulf region and the Middle East, highlighting the loss of lives, economic suffering and pressure faced by critical maritime routes, particularly the Strait of Hormuz.

“At this critical moment, Pakistan chose to act swiftly. Through concerted efforts, Pakistan brought Washington and Tehran under one roof in Islamabad,” PM Shehbaz said, referring to the Islamabad Talks that resulted in the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding by the US and Iran in June.

In this regard, he appreciated Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Munir, whose “relentless efforts helped create space for diplomacy under exceptionally difficult and challenging circumstances”. He also extended his appreciation to Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar for his role in the process.

“Amid the roar of missiles, drones and guns, the voice for diplomacy must echo even louder and stronger,” the premier stated.

“The Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab are arteries of the global economy. They must remain open, connecting nations, not becoming choke points of confrontation,” he said.

He also condemned, “in the strongest possible terms”, the recent attacks by the Houthis against the kingdom of Saudi Arabia, calling them “deplorable” and expressed Islamabad’s complete solidarity with Riyadh.

He also highlighted the tripartite defence agreement recently signed by Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia as a reflection of Pakistan’s commitment to peace.

“This alliance is not directed against any country; it is a collective commitment for defence, stability and peace in the region, and nothing more,” he stressed.

PM Shehbaz also restated Pakistan’s support for Palestine, expressing his concern for ongoing Israeli violence in Gaza and the West Bank as well as its continued aggression against Lebanon and Syria.

He said that last year he had mentioned the “heart-wrenching story” of Hind Rajab, a 5-year-old Palestinian girl who was shot dead by Israeli forces in Gaza after being trapped for hours in a car with her family members.

“This year, another tragedy weighs heavy on the heart. This time, it is the deafening cries of the sobbing mother of eight-year-old Wafaa Akila, who embraced martyrdom in this senseless aggression. What should have been the first day of her school became the last day of her life,” he said.

“Does not a child born in Gaza deserve the same life, and the same future as a child anywhere else in the world? The tragedies of Hind Rajab, Wafaa Akila, and countless others will echo through history as an indictment of our collective silence and inaction,” he said.

In particular, he noted that the forcible eviction of Palestinians in the West Bank “clearly reflects Israel’s genocidal agenda”.

“Pakistan believes that the only just and lasting solution is the creation of an independent, sovereign, viable and contiguous state of Palestine based on pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital,” he reaffirmed.

Terrorism and Afghanistan

Talking about terrorism, the premier said: “Terrorism remains one of the gravest threats to international peace and security.”

He said that as a frontline state in combating the menace of terrorism, Pakistan had “fought terrorists in our own cities, in our own mountains and along our frontiers”.

“Pakistan has sacrificed, almost 100,000 precious lives and suffered economic losses exceeding $150 billion. The world is safer today thanks to the valuable sacrifices of our valiant armed forces and brave civilians who took on these terrorists. The peace-loving world must never forget this reality,” he said.

He added that Afghan territory continued to be exploited by the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and the Balochistan Liberation Army.

“These foreign-funded groups operated from sanctuaries in Afghanistan with the aim of destabilising Pakistan,” he said. The premier said that all such attacks from the territory of Afghanistan “must come to a grinding halt”.

He called on Afghan authorities to fulfill their international commitments and take “verifiable, decisive action to ensure that Afghan soil is never again used against Pakistan or any other country”.

“The fundamental rights of the Afghan people, especially women and girls, must be respected,” he said.

On restoring trust

PM Shehbaz also called attention to the theme of this year’s assembly, saying, “The theme of this session calls upon us to restore trust. But trust cannot be restored by words alone. It must be earned through action.

“We will restore trust when rivers become lifelines of cooperation, not faultlines of conflict. We will restore trust when those who fuelled the climate crisis protect those who suffer most from its devastating consequences. And above all, trust will be restored when the guns are silenced and replaced by handshakes, embraces and smiles,” he said.

He called for the UN to become stronger and more effective, stressing that reform must reflect “the interests and aspirations of the overwhelming majority of member states, not the ambitions of a select few”.

“We live at a dangerous moment. But our future is not predetermined. War is a choice. Peace is also a choice. And sometimes, courage lies not in starting a war but in preventing one,” he said.

“Pakistan has made its choice. We have chosen dialogue over confrontation. We have chosen cooperation over coercion. We have chosen peace over war,” the premier said.

“Let this 81st General Assembly make it a unanimous choice … Let us restore trust. Let us preserve peace. And let us prove that even in a divided world, humanity can still choose to stand together,” he concluded.

World.title: Petrol price raised by Rs2.02 per litre, high-speed diesel rate reduced by Rs3.59
World.content:
The government on Friday increased the price of petrol by Rs2.02 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.59 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs391.30 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs408.53 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable from Sept 26 (Saturday) to Sept 28 (Monday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Pakistani, Saudi, Turkish military chiefs meet to discuss ways to assist Riyadh under Makkah defence pact
World.content:
Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan held military chiefs of staff talks on Friday with the objective to explore ways to assist Riyadh under the Makkah Defence Alliance.

The Turkish defence ministry published photographs of the three military officials in uniform, stating that the meeting had taken place, without disclosing where.

However, Turkiye’s Defence Ministry earlier said its Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu would travel to Saudi Arabia for the meeting.

The meeting took place against the backdrop of the kingdom being dragged into fresh fighting between the Houthis and the Yemeni government, with the former declaring a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. In recent weeks, Houthis have also carried out attacks in Saudi Arabia.

Earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) in Islamabad had shared that the three countries were mulling a military chiefs’ meeting to consider ways to assist Riyadh under the Makkah pact.

The FO statement came after Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a discussion on the defence pact with Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan bin Abdullah and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

In the statement, the FO noted that the tripartite agreement, signed on Aug 7, stipulated that an attack against any one of its parties should be considered an attack against all parties.

In their New York meeting, the foreign ministers of the three countries condemned in the “strongest terms the heinous attacks targeting the holy city of Makkah and civilian and economic facilities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia”, the FO statement said.

At the same time, it added, the ministers “commended the vigilance of the Saudi armed forces and their ability to defend the kingdom’s security”.

“They reaffirmed the kingdom’s right to take such measures as it deems appropriate to defend its security, in accordance with Article 51 of the UN Charter.”

They further discussed the current situation in the region, underscoring the importance of upholding the principles of international law, good neighbourliness, mutual respect for the sovereignty of states, and non-interference in their internal affairs, as well as ensuring the security and freedom of navigation, the statement said.

Moreover, they reiterated their determination to work together towards achieving sustainable peace and stability in the region, support efforts towards de-escalation and encourage peaceful resolution to crises.

During the meeting, the ministers also reviewed progress made towards establishing the general secretariat and committees and working groups under the Makkah agreement, as well as preparations for the commencement of their work, the FO statement said.

Earlier in the day, Dar also posted on X: “Under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), we reviewed progress towards establishing the institutional structures under the agreement and exchanged views on regional and international security issues.”

The Makkah Defence Alliance’s inaugural meeting was held on Aug 31, where officials from all member states met in Istanbul to establish the institutional structure of the alliance, and Pakistan was picked to head its secretariat in Riyadh. Retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood has been appointed as the first secretary general.

Pakistan expresses solidarity with Saudi Arabia

A day earlier, Saudi Arabia intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis after issuing warnings for several regions, including Makkah. This was the second time that a warning was issued for the holy city in the last two weeks.

As Yemen’s Houthi rebels continue to attack Saudi Arabia, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry on Sept 18 said that Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend Saudi Arabia, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security was “unconditional”.

On Wednesday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had also vowed to stand “shoulder to shoulder” with Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty and security.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia’s King Salman this week denounced the Houthis as a “terrorist militia” in a rare statement. He condemned the Houthi attempt “to target Makkah”, calling it “a provocation to Muslims around the world”, according to the official Saudi news agency.

Additional input from Reuters.

World.title: PTI postpones Islamabad long march to Oct 4
World.content:
ISLAMABAD/PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said on Friday that the PTI’s long march towards Islamabad, which was originally scheduled for Sept 27, would now commence from Peshawar on Oct 4.

The announcement by the KP CM came during a press conference in Peshawar, where he said the PTI’s political committee had held a meeting and “unanimously agreed” to now commence the march on Oct 4 from Peshawar.

“This struggle of ours is just for the supremacy of the Constitution, restoration of the independent judiciary, media freedom and Haqiqi Azadi, as envisioned by Imran Khan,” he added.

The PTI has been gearing up for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan, who is currently incarcerated in Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail.

Afridi claimed that Imran would be out of jail within half an hour if justice was served. But, he rued, court directives were not being abided by, referring to court orders for Imran’s medical treatment and meetings with his family.

“So when you are not heard even after adopting all legal and constitutional means, the Constitution allows you to protest peacefully,” he added.

Afridi further condemned the reported arrests and detentions of PTI leaders and workers, including ministers. He alleged that Punjab authorities had been directed to take action in KP and denounced the authorities for placing containers and hammering nails on roads along the KP-Punjab boundary to block the march’s route.

Coming back to the postponing of the march, he remarked the PTI workers “know that it is a Test match”. He added that the PTI’s allies had also been informed of the party’s decision.

Earlier in the day, amid speculation that the march would be postponed, Afridi sounded resolute that the march would take place. However, he did not specify at the time whether the protest would be delayed.

The PTI would hold the Islamabad march whether they hammer nails into the roads, place containers, or fire bullets, he said while addressing a press conference in Peshawar.

“The PTI will not step back from its demand for Imran Khan’s release and medical treatment despite threats of arrests and governor’s rule,” he added.

Earlier, a senior PTI leader, who requested anonymity, had also told Dawn that the march would now leave from Peshawar on Oct 4.

“There was a proposal to exhaust the federal government and law enforcement agencies, as they have already closed down the federal capital and a number of routes,” he said.

The leader claimed that the PTI had already achieved what it wanted to do via the march.

“They have closed down roads and are spending hundreds of millions on law enforcement,” he noted.

Asked if the PTI intended to march alongside the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI), which had postponed its own protest march against the petroleum levy on the request of the premier, the leader said that the decision had nothing to do with them.

“We are capable of arranging the march on our own,” he said.

The development comes a day after a PTI leader had hinted at the possibility of postponing its protest march if the federal government agreed to hold elections within six to eight months, release Imran and other political prisoners, and investigate the May 9 and November 26 crackdowns on the opposition party.

Advocate Naeem Haider Panjutha told Dawn that the protest could be postponed if these three assurances were given by the government.

Party spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram, however, had denied any such proposal was being discussed at any party forum, saying only Imran could take a decision even if such a proposal was on the table.

Meanwhile, preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation have been in full swing in light of the potential long march and other protests in Islamabad.

Punjab has already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province for 13 days and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad for two months.

The Punjab government has also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed on Sept 27.

Meanwhile, the federal government on Thursday approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab from Sept 20 to Oct 5.

“The deployed troops may respond appropriately in self-defence to any threats or violent activities encountered in the course of their duties as per rules/regulations in vogue,” the notification stated.

HRCP urges govt to de-escalate political tensions

All three of Imran’s sisters — Uzma Khan, Noreen Khan and Aleema Khan — have been detained and there have also been reports of the arrests of PTI members and workers.

The Human Right Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) said in a statement on Friday that it “deplores the mounting arrests and preventive detention of PTI workers, lawmakers and leaders ahead of the party’s planned protest march”.

Reports indicated that scores of workers, including women, had been arbitrarily detained, with some families claiming that they had no information as to the whereabouts of their relatives, the HRCP said.

It added that it was “incumbent on the state to uphold the right to peaceful assembly for all citizens”.

“Pre-emptive mass detention and restrictions on freedom of movement cannot be justified as proportionate or necessary. Moreover, repeated blanket restrictions, including the imposition of Section 144, are an affront to democratic principles.

“We urge the government to de-escalate political tensions by resuming a purposeful dialogue with the opposition and to immediately release those who have been arbitrarily detained,” the HRCP said.

Tarar takes aim at KP govt for ‘facilitating terrorism’

As political tensions persist between the PTI and the federal government, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar continued his criticism of the party and the KP government on Friday.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he accused the KP government of avoiding to take steps to maintain law and order in the province.

He alleged that they also gave “full facilitation” to terrorists and called their policy on law and order “evasive”.

“In one way or another, terrorists have attacked all political parties in KP,” the minister said.

“But the PTI is held in high regard by terrorists. And not only do they avoid condemning terrorists, but they also fully avoid taking any sort of action against them. Facilitating terrorists is part of their policy.”

He called KP’s PTI government the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan’s (TTP) “B-team”, and Tehreek-i-Taliban Afghanistan’s (TTA) “C-team”, claiming that it was facilitating the TTP while also “representing” the TTA.

He also took aim at KP CM Afridi specifically, saying he “looks less like a chief minister and more like a TTP commander, in both his words and actions”.

“When drones are fired at Kohat from Afghanistan, and the Pakistan Army and Air Force very skilfully take them down, you will not see any sort of condemnation or statement from KP government,” Tarar claimed.

“When there is firing from Afghanistan in Kurram … you will never see them go to Kurram and say ‘We have come here, we stand with our forces, and we will not tolerate such firing under any circumstances’.”

He termed this a sign of cowardice from CM Afridi, his cabinet and his entire KP government, adding that this was also the reason they were “running away” from protests.

“They are not even prepared. I’ve just come from KP. They don’t have any sort of preparations,” the minister said.

“Come and protest, if you have the courage,” he said.

He stressed that the provincial government was in charge of controlling law and order, highlighting that 2,456 terror attacks had taken place in KP in 2026 — around 10 a day on average. He added that 472 police, army, rangers, and FC personnel were martyred and over 1,500 people injured this year.

The information minister asserted that the reason the KP government did not want to fix the law and order situation was to maintain a “political terror-crime nexus” and illegal trade and mining activities in the province, through which they “funded terrorists”.

“A provincial government which doesn’t want to stop terrorism and fix law and order, and countless citizens lose their lives — this cannot be justified in any part of the world,” he said.

World.title: Info ministry dismisses Afghan claims of destroying Pakistani post near border in Balochistan as 'fake'
World.content:
The information ministry dismissed on Friday claims by the Afghan defence ministry of a Pakistani post having been destroyed near the Spin Boldak border — the frontier between Balochistan and Kandahar — as “fake and fabricated”.

The information ministry also took note of Afghan claims that there had been no casualties among the Afghan forces in the latest episode of clash between the two sides.

“The claim is fake and fabricated. As per actual facts, an attempted Afghan aggression in the Gulistan sector was thwarted on night between Sept 24 and Sept 25, and during the process and subsequent heavy punishment inflicted on opposing Taliban posts, at least 13 Afghan Taliban personnel were killed and several injured,” the information ministry said in a post on X.

It also shared visuals in the post, which the ministry said were of the incident.

The incident, it added, had already been “widely covered by media and circulated extensively across social media, providing visual evidence of the border engagement and punishment inflicted on the Afghan Taliban after their cowardly attack”.

“The […] Afghan ministry’s attempt is no surprise since the Taliban are habitual liars having no moral and reputational standing,” it added.

The latest clash has taken place amid an uptick in tensions at the Pak-Afghan border.

Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes in 10 locations across Afghanistan on Thursday in retaliation for drones launched from the neighbouring country a day earlier.

The response came after eight drones, launched from Afghanistan, entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat on Wednesday. Security sources said they were subsequently shot down. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.

On Sept 21, Pakistan, in response to recent terrorist attacks in KP, conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations.

A statement from the information ministry on Monday said that over 28 terrorists were eliminated in the strikes. “It is a matter of grave concern that Afghanistan continues to remain a hub of terrorism,” the ministry said at the time, specifying that the “threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan”.

The airstrikes had come after a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area.

Ghazab lil-Haq

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described Monday’s action as part of Pakistan’s ongoing counter-terrorism campaign, Ghazab lil Haq.

On the night of February 26, following unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban from across the border, Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil Haq against terrorist hideouts.

Pakistan also carried out strikes in the border region with Afghanistan in late June , with the government saying they were in response to a wave of terrorist attacks, including one on a Rangers camp in Karachi .

At the time, Tarar said that 25 terrorists were killed in those strikes in Paktia, Paktika and Kunar.

Pakistan had carried out similar strikes on terrorist hideouts along its border with Afghanistan earlier that month, killing 26 terrorists.

In July, security forces responded to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban at border posts in Kurram, security sources had said. In the same month, the Afghan Taliban regime launched four rudimentary drones across the border into Balochistan, which were shot down by security forces. Two drones were also shot down in June in Qila Abdullah and Chagai districts.

Pak-Afghan ties

As clashes continue, tensions between Islamabad and Kabul have remained high. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

Earlier this week, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar addressed a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), where he called for steps towards concrete and verifiable action to prevent the use of Afghan soil for terrorism against any neighbouring country, particularly Pakistan.

Dar said Pakistan was “seriously concerned” about the presence of over two dozen terrorist groups in Afghanistan that threatened regional and international peace and security.

Last week, Pakistan also told the UN Security Council that it would respond to terrorist threats emanating from Afghanistan in self-defence as and when needed and in accordance with international law.

Earlier this month, the Foreign Office (FO) declared that meaningful progress in relations with Kabul would depend on the Taliban taking concrete and verifiable action against Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory.

It maintained that while Islamabad welcomed China’s continuing engagement, the external facilitation could not substitute for action by Kabul against terrorist infrastructure.

According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from December 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group.

The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

World.title: 33 India-sponsored terrorists killed by security forces in Balochistan since Sept 21: ISPR
World.content:
Security forces have killed 33 terrorists in counter-terrorism operations in Balochistan since Sept 21, the military’s media affairs wing said in a statement on Friday.

Terrorists from Fitna-al-Khawarij and Fitna-al-Hindustan were targeted in the operations, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

The state uses the term Fitna al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

Detailing the operations, the ISPR said that on Sept 24, as part of the ongoing Operation Shaban, security forces “busted additional terrorist hideouts, and after an intense fire exchange, five “India-sponsored terrorists” were killed.

This took the tally of killed terrorist to 22, it added.

“Weapons, ammunition and explosives were also recovered from khawarij locations. The clearance operation will continue till the complete neutralisation of threat from the area,” the statement said.

In another engagement on Sept 25, security forces conducted an intelligence-based operation in the Nushki district.

“During the conduct of [the] operation, own troops effectively engaged [the] terrorists’ hideout and after an intense fire exchange, 11 terrorists were sent to hell,” the ISPR stated.

“[The] relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision ‘Azm-i-Istehkam’ (as approved by [the] Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out [the] menace of foreign-sponsored and -supported terrorism from the country,” the military’s media wing added.

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the security forces for the successful operations, according to a statement from the Presidency.

“Eliminating 33 India-backed terrorists in Balochistan is a commendable achievement for the security forces,” he was quoted as saying, praising security personnel for seizing weapons and ammunition from the terrorists.

“The nefarious designs of India-backed terrorist elements will be thwarted at all costs,” he vowed.

Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks in recent weeks, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations.

The number of terrorist attacks in the province increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies.

On Wednesday, the ISPR said security for­ces had killed 19 terrorists in separate intelligence-ba­s­ed operations in Sha­ban, Kech and Quetta West during which a soldier was also martyred.

On September 22, six terrorists were killed and nine suspected individuals were arrested during an intelligence-based operation by security forces in Balochistan’s Saran Tangi area, state-run Radio Pakistan reported .

According to Radio Pakistan, a large cache of ammunition and weapons were also recovered from the possession of the terrorists.

Earlier that day, security forces killed four more terrorists belonging to a banned organisation in an intelligence-based operation carried out in two areas of Panjgur district.

According to officials, security forces launched an intelligence-based operation on the information about the presence of armed militants in Koh-Prom and the Aphan area of Panjgur district.

“Four armed terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan were killed in the heavy gun battle during the operation,” they said, adding that a large quantity of arms and ammunition was seized from the hideouts of the terrorists.

World.title: Lawyer challenges Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway closure in IHC
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: A lawyer moved the Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Friday against the closure of the Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway (M-1) and sought directions to reopen the blocked routes for lawyers, litigants and emergency services.

The government announced the motorway’s closure earlier this week as it stepped up arrangements to prevent the PTI from marching on Islamabad.

The march was part of the party’s planned nationwide protest to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan, and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. The protest was originally planned for Sept 27, but the party has now reportedly deferred it.

Advocate Mian Shafqat Jan, a lawyer of the Supreme Court, filed a petition on Friday against the government’s move to shutdown the M-1 Motorway after he was unable to reach the Peshawar High Court (PHC) to appear in a case due to the closure.

According to the petition, the lawyer was scheduled to appear before the PHC on Sept 24. He managed to enter the motorway from the Islamabad toll plaza at around 7am after facing difficulties but found the route closed at the M-1 Attock Bridge.

The petitioner said he sought information from officials deployed at the site about any written order authorising the closure but was unable to obtain a confirmation.

He contended that closing public routes without a notification, written order or disclosed reasons infringed citizens’ fundamental rights and warranted judicial intervention.

The petition named the federation through the interior and information secretaries, the inspectors general of the National Highways and Motorway Police and Islamabad Police, the National Highway Authority through its chairman, the Islamabad Capital Territory administration through the chief commissioner, and the Punjab government through its home secretary and inspector general of police as respondents.

The petitioner also referred to a recent IHC judgement about the planned PTI protest, arguing that the court had recognised constitutional protections for citizens, including freedom of movement and access to courts.

In its detailed 37-page judgement in the case pertaining to the PTI’s planned protest, the IHC held that any activity resulting in the infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounted to a violation of the Constitution. It also observed that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the rights of other citizens.

The bench, headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Azam Khan and Justice Muhammad Asif, directed the authorities to ensure that no political party, leader or public office holder occupied roads, highways, interchanges or toll plazas in a manner that obstructed free movement or hindered access to medical and educational facilities.

On the basis of these arguments, Advocate Jan urged the high court in his plea to declare the closure of roads and highways without any notification, written order or disclosed reasons illegal and unconstitutional.

He has also sought directions for the interior secretary, communications secretary and Islamabad chief commissioner to ensure the reopening of blocked routes for emergency traffic, lawyers, litigants, witnesses, sick persons, funeral processions and other emergency services.

According to the National Highways and Motorway Police (NHMP), the M-1 has been closed to all traffic in both directions between the Islamabad Toll Plaza and Chhachh Interchange, while the M-14 was closed from Hakla to Kundal. The GT Road was also closed at Attock Khurd.

The government had also decided to close the Islamabad-Dera Ismail Khan Motorway (M14) — also known as the CPEC road — and GT Road.

Security arrangements were also intensified in Attock, with containers and sandbags placed at key bridges and security tightened at major entry and exit points, as authorities prepared for the PTI protest.

The federal government also approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab ahead of the PTI’s planned march on the federal capital.

Punjab has already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province for 13 days and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad as well for two months.

Gatherings in the federal capital are also banned under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act 2024 , which had been rushed through the National Assembly amidst the opposition’s outcry ahead of a PTI gathering .

Meanwhile, Section 144 has also been imposed in Karachi, Hyderabad, Sukkur and Balochistan.

The Punjab government had also sent a letter to the federal interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed on Sept 27 due to the “expected law and order situation”.

World.title: Indian police use tear gas against protesters seeking election chief's ouster
World.content:
Indian police used tear gas and water cannons on Friday to disperse opposition Congress party members during nationwide protests demanding the resignation of the head of the election commission, whom they accuse of manipulating voter rolls.

The “cockroach” youth movement, which counts millions of supporters and forced the education minister out in July, said it would launch protests across India on Oct 2 if Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by Saturday.

The protests, which are backed by other opposition groups, mark a new political challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as Kumar, 62, a former civil servant, was appointed to head the independent Election Commission of India by Modi’s government.
